picks.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma.

sections.objective: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety.
sections.results: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered.
sections.conclusion: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

picks.title: ANGPTL4 Inhibition in Adults with Elevated Triglyceride Levels.

sections.objective: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) inhibits lipoprotein lipase and regulates triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism. MAR001 is a monoclonal antibody against ANGPTL4 that is being evaluated for lowering triglyceride levels.
sections.methods: We conducted a two-part, phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. In part A, the focus of this report, we enrolled adults who had a nonfasting triglyceride level of at least 175 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 35 mg per deciliter at initial screening, followed by a fasting triglyceride level of at least 150 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 30 mg per deciliter on confirmatory screening. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive MAR001 at a dose of 300, 450, or 900 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 24 weeks. The primary end point was the percent change from baseline in the fasting triglyceride level at week 12, reported as the difference between each MAR001 dose group and the placebo group (placebo-adjusted change).
sections.results: A total of 236 participants were enrolled in the trial, with 177 assigned to receive MAR001 and 59 to receive placebo; a total of 235 participants received at least one dose of MAR001 or placebo and were included in the primary efficacy analyses. The mean age of the participants was 60.4 years, and 39% were women. The median triglyceride level at baseline was 249.5 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 210.0 to 313.0). At week 12, in an intention-to-treat analysis, the placebo-adjusted least-squares mean percent changes in the fasting triglyceride level were -39.1 percentage points, -40.5 percentage points, and -45.3 percentage points for the 300-mg, 450-mg, and 900-mg doses, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Adverse events occurred in 123 of 177 participants (69%) in the pooled MAR001 group and in 45 of 58 participants (78%) in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: Inhibition of ANGPTL4 with MAR001 significantly reduced fasting triglyceride levels at 12 weeks. (Funded by Marea Therapeutics; TYDAL-TIMI 78 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07028749.).

picks.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
sections.methods: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.
sections.results: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).
sections.conclusion: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
sections.other: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.

picks.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis.
picks.abstract: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1-5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal-immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

picks.title: Early epidemiological and spatial assessment of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak 2026
picks.abstract: A Bundibugyo virus outbreak was first reported on May 15th, 2026 in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with multiple cases reported across health zones during the early phase of the outbreak and suggestions of circulation weeks prior to detection. We pair highly resolved case and testing records with human mobility data to investigate the early outbreak dynamics of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). We show that human movement was a principle driver of early spatial expansion between May 10th and June 1st when the number of health zones and health areas reporting positive cases increased by 12 and 49, respectively. The early doubling time was estimated at ~10 days. Our work shows the rapid spatial expansion and growth of BVD with implications for intervention strategies.

picks.title: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity.
picks.abstract: Germline pathogenic BRCA1 variants predispose women to breast and ovarian cancer. Despite accumulation of functional evidence, over half of reported single-nucleotide variants in BRCA1 lack a definitive clinical interpretation. Furthermore, the consistency of variant effects across cell types remains largely unexplored. Here we performed saturation genome editing (SGE) of BRCA1 in HAP1 cells to score 4,113 previously unassayed variants. Additionally, we developed an SGE assay in human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs), allowing comparison of effects across cell lines, drug treatments and genetic backgrounds. We identified 538 variants impacting gene function through distinct mechanisms. HAP1 function scores discriminate between known pathogenic and benign variants with near-perfect accuracy. Intriguingly, however, nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants scored neutrally in HMECs. We show that discordantly scored variants are hypomorphic and confer intermediate cancer risk. Overall, this work demonstrates how performing SGE across cell models improves the functional interpretation of rare variants.

picks.title: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.

sections.objective: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete.
sections.results: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups).
sections.conclusion: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes.

picks.title: Harmonized brain ontology and 3D atlases for human, macaque, and marmoset basal ganglia.
picks.abstract: A major goal of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is to create a suite of foundational reference cell atlases and associated standards for human and nonhuman primate brains. Central to this goal is the creation of cross-species-harmonized cellular taxonomies and structural parcellations with formal ontologies that can be mapped onto 3D reference frameworks, bridging neuroimaging and cellular and histological resolutions. We describe an iterative approach, focused initially on the basal ganglia, to co-create structural and cellular ontologies for human, macaque, and marmoset brains and to map and refine structural parcellations into neuroimaging-based common coordinate frameworks. We create a Harmonized Ontology of Mammalian Brain Anatomy (HOMBA) to meet these needs. These references provide the framework for documenting and mapping all experimental sampling in BICAN, allowing analyses of cellular and molecular variation as a function of topographic position and enabling comparisons of cellular, molecular, and neuroimaging-based functional variation across species.

items.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
sections.methods: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).
sections.conclusion: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

items.title: 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan.

sections.objective: Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.
sections.methods: PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.
sections.conclusion: A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

items.title: Ambient scribes as narrative technologies.
items.abstract: Ambient scribes, also known as artificial intelligence-powered voice-to-text technology, are widely cited as time-saving tools that reduce administrative burden for clinicians. Yet, in their current use, these tools pose substantial, often unacknowledged risks that threaten to undermine patient-centred care. We argue that ambient scribes are inherently narrative technologies whose risks-and potential benefits-cannot be fully understood without careful attention to the ways that patients tell their stories and the broader context in which those stories are told. Drawing on medical humanities scholarship, we show that current approaches to ambient scribes take a superficial approach to narrative interpretation that omits the clinically relevant aspects of patient experience. We propose three ways to integrate more robust narrative analysis that can increase the value of ambient scribes: centring patient perspectives, accounting for material and social structures that shape narrative, and reframing the clinical encounter as a node in a broader narrative system. We conclude by outlining five priorities for commissioners, administrators, clinical leaders, and practice managers to ensure that the roll-out of ambient scribes does not deepen existing harms, and could instead contribute to more humane and trustworthy care.

items.title: Empirical treatment with valganciclovir in infants living with HIV and hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa: a multicentre, open-label, factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high. This trial (EMPIRICAL) tested whether empirical valganciclovir treatment for cytomegalovirus improves survival in infants in Africa.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2 × 2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity to receive standard of care (SOC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SOC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SOC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, assessed at day 15 and over 1-year follow-up in the intention-to-treat population. In this Article, we report results for the valganciclovir comparison groups. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03915366 and is complete.
sections.results: From March 15, 2020, to Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were included in the analyses, with 276 allocated to valganciclovir groups (140 valganciclovir; 136 valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and 282 to groups without valganciclovir (142 SOC; 140 tuberculosis treatment). The median patient age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4), and 274 (49%) were female. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and tuberculosis treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·73-1·95], heterogeneity p=0·48). At day 15, 64 (23%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir group and 76 (27%) of 282 in groups without valganciclovir died (rate ratio 0·81 [95% CI 0·61-1·08], p=0·15). 24 (9%) of 276 participants and 13 (5%) of 282, respectively, were lost to follow-up. After 12 months, 119 (43%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir groups and 134 (48%) of 282 in the groups without valganciclovir died (0·88 [95% CI 0·74-1·05] p=0·15). In a time-varying effects model, at day 15, the adjusted hazard ratio of death was 0·60 (95% CI 0·41-0·87, p=0·0063), and their hazard of death over 1 year was 0·79 (0·62-1·01; p=0·068), or 0·76 (0·58-1·00; p=0·0500) when excluding deaths within 48 h of treatment. Severe adverse events during follow-up were not more common in the valganciclovir treatment groups (odds ratio 0·64 [95% CI 0·35-1·16]).
sections.conclusion: Empirical valganciclovir treatment appeared to be associated with a lower hazard of death in infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia than SOC alone or SOC plus empirical tuberculosis treatment, and there was little evidence of associated harms.

items.title: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring.
items.abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), a primary stress-sensing signal in today's wearables, requires skin-electrode contact that drifts and degrades over time, limiting long-term use. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered ring for all-optical sensing of dermal activity (ODA), using light rather than electrodes to track sweat gland activation, thereby enhancing durability and comfort. An optimized dual-wavelength design (960 and 1250 nanometers) captures perspiration dynamics while concurrently recording photoplethysmography. The ODA ring integrates temperature and motion sensors for multimodal monitoring with on-device inference. In correlation studies, ODA and EDA signals showed 86% agreement. In classification tasks, the ODA ring achieved 92.3% binary accuracy versus 77.95% for EDA. In multiclass tasks, ODA outperforms EDA by 100 to 74.58% (short term) and 89.72 to 43.20% (long term). On-device one-dimensional convolutional neural network inference enabled 87.53% autonomous accuracy. This electrode-free modality establishes a scalable, all-optical platform for rings, watches, and patches for accurate, robust, and long-term stress monitoring.

items.title: A periodontal Piezo1-dependent brain-bone interoceptive circuit couples occlusal force to craniofacial bone homeostasis.
items.abstract: The skeleton continuously monitors mechanical state to maintain tissue homeostasis, but whether such interoceptive control operates in the craniofacial skeleton remains unclear. Here, we identify a brain-bone axis in which Piezo1 in Gli1-lineage periodontal mesenchymal stromal cells (Gli1-lineage MSCs) senses occlusal force and initiates prostaglandin E2 (PGE2)-dependent interoceptive signaling. Mechanistically, mechanical loading activates a transcriptional complex comprising YAP and Gli1 that directly promotes COX-2 expression and PGE2 production. This signal engages trigeminal sensory pathways and is associated with sustained ventromedial hypothalamic (VMH) activity and reduced paraventricular nucleus (PVN)-related sympathetic output. Disruption of this circuit under occlusal hypofunction elevates sympathetic tone, increasing osteoclast activity and impairing type H vessel formation. Importantly, conditional deletion of Piezo1 in Gli1-lineage MSCs largely abolished occlusal force-dependent regulation of VMH activity, sympathetic tone, and mandibular bone homeostasis, establishing its required role in this pathway. Our findings define a Piezo1-PGE2-mediated skeletal interoceptive circuit that links occlusal force to central sympathetic control of craniofacial bone mass, revealing a potential neuromechanical strategy for preventing disuse-induced bone loss.

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.

sections.objective: Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence. The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes.
sections.methods: Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events.
sections.results: Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037).
sections.conclusion: Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.

items.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
sections.methods: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.
sections.results: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).
sections.conclusion: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
sections.other: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.

items.title: Lynch syndrome.
items.abstract: Lynch syndrome is the most common inherited cancer predisposition syndrome, affecting approximately one in 350-450 individuals, yet the majority of carriers remain undiagnosed, representing a substantial and preventable public health burden. Caused by germline pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, Lynch syndrome confers markedly elevated and heterogeneous risks of colorectal, endometrial, and multiple extracolonic cancers. Advances in molecular diagnostics, particularly universal tumour testing for MMR deficiency, have transformed case identification and enabled targeted germline testing and cascade screening of relatives at risk. Despite these advances, implementation remains inconsistent, with substantial attrition across diagnostic pathways and inequities in access to care. Preventive strategies-including colonoscopic surveillance, aspirin chemoprevention, and risk-reducing surgery-are effective but require gene-specific and individualised application. Therapeutically, the immunogenic biology of MMR-deficient tumours has positioned Lynch syndrome at the forefront of precision oncology, with immune checkpoint inhibitors delivering substantial benefit and emerging vaccine strategies offering promise for cancer interception. In this Review, we provide an integrated overview of Lynch syndrome across the continuum of care, highlighting advances in biology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment, while emphasising the crucial need to align scientific progress with equitable and effective health-system delivery.

items.title: Harmonized brain ontology and 3D atlases for human, macaque, and marmoset basal ganglia.
items.abstract: A major goal of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is to create a suite of foundational reference cell atlases and associated standards for human and nonhuman primate brains. Central to this goal is the creation of cross-species-harmonized cellular taxonomies and structural parcellations with formal ontologies that can be mapped onto 3D reference frameworks, bridging neuroimaging and cellular and histological resolutions. We describe an iterative approach, focused initially on the basal ganglia, to co-create structural and cellular ontologies for human, macaque, and marmoset brains and to map and refine structural parcellations into neuroimaging-based common coordinate frameworks. We create a Harmonized Ontology of Mammalian Brain Anatomy (HOMBA) to meet these needs. These references provide the framework for documenting and mapping all experimental sampling in BICAN, allowing analyses of cellular and molecular variation as a function of topographic position and enabling comparisons of cellular, molecular, and neuroimaging-based functional variation across species.

items.title: An integrative single-cell epigenomic atlas annotates the regulatory genome of the adult mouse brain.
items.abstract: Histone modifications underpin the cell-type-specific gene regulatory programs that drive the remarkable cellular diversity of the mammalian brain. Here, we jointly profiled four histone modifications and the transcriptome in 2.5 million nuclei from the adult mouse brain. By integrating these data with chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and three-dimensional genome organization, we constructed a unified epigenomic atlas spanning over 100 brain cell subclasses and assigned active, primed, and repressive chromatin states across 81% of the genome. Active chromatin states marked by combinatorial histone modifications better nominate candidate enhancers with functional support than chromatin accessibility alone, while H3K27me3- and H3K9me3-marked chromatin states delineate distinct modes of cell-type-specific gene repression. Finally, this multimodal resource enables the development of deep learning models that predict cell-type-specific epigenomic features and gene expression from DNA sequence, providing a comprehensive framework for annotating the brain regulatory genome and interpreting non-coding disease risk variants.

items.title: Single-cell, multi-region profiling of the macaque brain across the lifespan.
items.abstract: Brain aging is a complex process with profound health and societal consequences. However, the molecular and cellular pathways that govern its progression, and inter- and intra-individual variation, remain poorly defined. We present a transcriptomic atlas of 5.3 million cells from 582 samples spanning 11 brain regions of 55 rhesus macaques (aged 0.5-21 years). We identify age-depleted and vulnerable neuronal populations and subtle, age-associated compositional differences in glia-detectable only at single-cell resolution. We chart convergent and divergent age-associated molecular signatures across regions and cell types, which include sex-specific signatures that could underlie biases in neurological disorders. These signatures overlap those of Alzheimer's disease (AD), which suggests that aging and AD share molecular roots that emerge at different ages and in region- and sex-specific windows of vulnerability. This work provides a temporal, regional, and sex-stratified atlas of the aging primate brain, offering insights into cell-type-specific vulnerabilities and regional heterogeneity with translational human relevance.

items.title: A single-cell and spatial 3D multi-omic atlas of developing human basal ganglia.
items.abstract: Human basal ganglia (BG) neurons and inhibitory interneurons originate in the ganglionic eminences (GEs), transient structures in the ventral prenatal brain. This study delineates the specification and maturation of GEs and GE-derived neurons using single-nucleus methyl-3C sequencing (snm3C-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and single-molecule chromatin + RNA imaging, and we found heterogeneous temporal progression across GE subregions. Spiny projection neurons (SPNs), the principal cells of the BG, acquire distinct subtypes through synchronized 3D-epigenomic remodeling, in contrast to the asynchronous maturation of other neuron types. Oligodendrocyte differentiation involves a transient short-range chromatin state during infancy, showing that the short-range and long-range chromatin conformations previously linked to terminal glial and neuronal fates can also be transient. The temporal cortex matured epigenomically faster than other cortical regions during this period. Lastly, SPNs were enriched in genetic risk for neuropsychiatric disease. Our study extends findings on unique 3D-epigenomic dynamics during human brain development.

items.title: Disruption of cell-type-specific molecular programs of striatal spiny projection neurons in autism.
items.abstract: Rare genetic variants contribute substantially to autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the regulatory logic of vulnerable subcortical cells is poorly understood. In a 16p11.2 deletion mouse model, lineage tracing across five brain regions revealed prominent striatal changes. In the human putamen from ASD and neurotypical donors, single-nucleus multi-omics showed transcriptional alterations concentrated in D1 striosome spiny projection neurons (SPNs), affecting synaptic and energy metabolism genes, with altered synapse-supporting programs in astrocytes. Gene regulatory network analysis integrating chromatin accessibility and expression identified EGR1 and EGR3 as key regulators of these programs, with reduced activity in D1 striosome SPNs. Deleting EGR1 or EGR3 in human striatal organoids produced partially overlapping transcriptional changes. These findings establish the striatum as a site of molecular convergence in ASD and provide a multi-omic resource for dissecting subcortical mechanisms.

items.title: Circuit-aligned specialization of human basal ganglia astrocytes.
items.abstract: Astrocytes shape synapses and circuits, yet their diversity within the human basal ganglia remains poorly defined. Integrating single-nucleus transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with spatial transcriptomics, we identify three anatomically organized astrocyte subgroups-striatal gray matter (GM), extra-striatal GM, and white matter (WM)-distinguished by neurotransmitter transporter expression and synapse-associated programs that reflect afferent input. These molecular distinctions generalize brain-wide, separating telencephalic from non-telencephalic astrocytes, with LHX2 marking telencephalic astrocyte identity across species. Within the striatum (STR), dorsal and ventral populations align with distinct microcircuits; a ventral population maps to the nucleus accumbens mediodorsal shell alongside specialized neuronal subtypes, a pattern conserved in nonhuman primates. A deep learning sequence model identifies subgroup-specific enhancer codes and recovers established transcription factor motif logic from published enhancer-AAV datasets, providing a foundation for targeted viral vector design. These findings define intersecting axes of human astrocyte specialization and offer a framework for cell-type-specific dissection of basal ganglia circuits.

items.title: Morphoelectric diversity and specialization of primate striatal neuron types.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia are evolutionarily ancient subcortical nuclei that form interconnected loops with the neocortex and limbic system to regulate movement, learning, habit formation, emotion, and motivation. Their dysfunction contributes to major neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet most cellular-level insights derive from rodent studies, leaving knowledge gaps in humans and translationally relevant primate species. To address this, we generated multimodal Patch-seq data linking transcriptomic identity with morphological and electrophysiological properties in the macaque striatum-the input nucleus of the basal ganglia. We found underappreciated diversity among spiny projection neurons (SPNs), including non-canonical types, and variation aligned with functional gradients. Interneurons also exhibited spatial variation and even greater morphoelectric diversity, highlighting their functional modularity. Despite broad evolutionary conservation, we identified primate-specific features and key differences from rodent striatal neurons. By integrating molecular classification with cellular properties that shape network function, our findings provide insights into the functional organization of the primate striatum.

items.title: Spatial and regulatory organization of cell identity across the primate subcortex.
items.abstract: Mammalian brain cell identity is shaped by intrinsic factors and external context. We present a spatially resolved transcriptomic and gene regulatory atlas of cell types across all subcortical regions in a primate, the common marmoset. Dense sampling and cross-species integration revealed spatially precise neuronal assemblies, including ones in complex midbrain and diencephalic structures. Chromatin accessibility and transcriptional identity are spatially tuned within and across subcortical structures; spatial gradients within hippocampal subfields are orchestrated by graded transcription factors acting through graded enhancers. The primate-expanded thalamic γ-aminobutyric acid (GABAergic) population shares transcriptional and regulatory syntax with conserved midbrain populations, reflecting an evolutionary adaptation compared with rodents. Similar regional expression across cell types can arise by distinct regulatory architectures, as observed in telencephalic astrocytes and neurons. Conversely, distant cell types can share regulatory programs despite divergent identities: striatal GABAergic spiny projection neurons and telencephalic glutamatergic neurons share a postsynaptic regulatory program despite divergent lineages, regions, and neurotransmitter identities.

items.title: Single-cell multimodal atlas reveals regulatory programs in the human brain.
items.abstract: Direct measurement of chromatin states together with transcription is essential for understanding how cell-type-specific regulatory programs are established and maintained in the adult human brain. Here, we present a large-scale single-cell multimodal atlas by jointly profiling the transcriptome with active (H3K27ac) or repressive (H3K27me3) histone modifications across 18 adult brain regions. We targeted over 750,000 nuclei spanning 160 cell types and integrated these data with chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, 3D genome architecture, and spatial transcriptomes. This framework resolved chromatin states for over 500,000 candidate regulatory elements, identified enhancer-gene links and regulatory programs, revealed Polycomb-associated ultra-long-range contacts, and uncovered brainwide epigenomic heterogeneity. We further developed a sequence-to-function model to predict cell-type-specific effects of candidate neurological disease variants. Finally, comparative analyses across species reveal conservation in active regulatory programs but divergence in repressive programs. Together, this study provides a comprehensive epigenomic reference for interpreting regulatory principles and epigenetic memory underlying human brain organization and disease.

items.title: Multiscale spatial atlas of human basal ganglia cell types and communities.
items.abstract: The human basal ganglia comprise functionally varied nuclei, but their cell-type composition and spatial organization have not been comprehensively resolved. We generated a multi-region, subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas by integrating multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH)+ and spatiotemporal enhanced-resolution omics sequencing (Stereo-seq) across four neurotypical donors. The datasets profiled ∼7.9 million cells across the caudate, putamen, nucleus accumbens, and globus pallidus, resolving 60 transcriptionally distinct cell types. We identify region-selective molecular and spatial diversification of spiny projection neurons and non-neuronal populations. Subcellular RNA localization captures somatic size and projection-inferred signatures, reflecting direct- and indirect-pathway topology. Cellular community analyses reveal astrocyte and oligodendrocyte subclusters enriched at striosome-matrix borders, while primate-expanded interneurons are confined to matrix territories. Cross-species comparisons reveal conserved and species-specialized organization, including orthologous striosome-matrix architecture and conserved dorsolateral-to-ventromedial transcriptional gradients. Together, this multi-centimeter-scale human basal ganglia atlas links cell types, spatial architecture, and subcellular transcript topography across scales.

items.title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generated a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical human donors. This atlas resolved cell-type- and region-specific landscapes of active and repressive candidate cis-regulatory elements and delineated gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We found that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors provides distinctive molecular descriptors of neuronal cell identities in the basal ganglia. Integration with matched MERFISH spatial transcriptomics further uncovered regional heterogeneity in epigenomic and transcriptional programs. Finally, we used this atlas to interpret noncoding risk variants associated with neuropsychiatric disorders and to construct a deep-learning model that predicts gene regulatory activities and variant effects. Together, this work provides a multimodal regulatory framework for understanding human basal ganglia organization, evolution, and disease genetics.

items.title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) underlie motor control, reward processing, and many neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet cell-type-resolved epigenomic and 3D genome maps of the human BG remain limited. Here, we present a multimodal single-cell atlas of DNA methylation (261,331 nuclei) and 3D chromatin conformation (229,286 nuclei) from eight subregions, harmonized under the BG consensus taxonomy and integrated with matched data across multiple regulatory layers. We identify millions of differentially methylated regions across cell types, enriched for distinct transcription factor motifs, and link them to disease-associated heritability. We characterize the POU6F2+ STR D2 SMYD2-HTR7 spiny projection neuron (SPN) subtype, with concordant signatures across multiple modalities, and reveal region-specific methylation and contact gradients. Integrative gene regulatory networks (GRNs) predict cell-type-resolved enhancer-promoter interactions, nominating candidate regulatory mechanisms for Parkinson's disease (PD) risk variants at SNCA. Finally, multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) profiling combined with cross-species Patch-seq identifies a neuronal subtype, STR FS PTHLH-PVALB GABA, with electrophysiological differences across the striatal matrix-striosome (MS) boundary.

items.title: Common variation of cell abundances and gene expression in the human striatum.
items.abstract: The cellular and molecular bases of inter-individual variation in the human brain are not yet understood, particularly beyond the neocortex. Here, we describe cellular and gene-expression variation in the striatum and prefrontal cortex from single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis of 3.9 million nuclei from 178 adult brain donors. People with more astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) in any one brain region tended to have this property in all gray-matter regions sampled. OPC proportions declined by 40% across ages 30-80 in the cortex and striatum. Age-associated gene-expression changes differed substantially across cell types. Donor age was predicted from RNA-expression patterns with a median absolute error of 6.6 years across cell types. Common genetic variants were associated with the expression of nearly 10,000 genes; these effects were mostly cell-type specific and distinguished striatal from cortical neurons. These open-access data provide a foundation for future studies of human brain variation and vulnerabilities.

items.title: Mesoscale molecular architecture of the striatum across cell types and adult aging.
items.abstract: The human striatum governs diverse motor, cognitive, and affective behaviors yet lacks the obvious cytoarchitectural boundaries defining functional territories elsewhere in the brain. Using Slide-tags single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics, we profiled 1.1 million cells across 19 postmortem donors to uncover the striatum's spatial organization. These data revealed a consistent subdivision of the striatum into six zones, each defined by molecularly distinct populations of spiny projection neurons (SPNs) and featuring spatially coordinated neuron-astrocyte interaction networks. To determine their structural relevance, we generated a companion mouse spatial atlas that identified four homologous zones that aligned with territories defined by brain-wide afferent projections. Finally, imputing zonal identities onto a 131-donor single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cohort revealed that dorsal zones exhibit the greatest age-related transcriptional change and that the expression differences defining zonation attenuate with age. This resource establishes a conserved mesoscale spatial framework for the mammalian striatum, linking single-cell molecular identity to structural connectomics and aging.

items.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are interconnected subcortical nuclei with a complex topographical organization that orchestrate goal-directed behaviors and are implicated in neurodegenerative movement disorders. We generated a cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics atlas of the BG in human, rhesus macaque, and common marmoset, sampling over one million cells in each species. By integrating spatial data with a cross-species consensus single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cell-type taxonomy, this atlas reveals principles of molecular organization within and across structures. Extensive spatial sampling across the rostral-caudal axis illuminates complex, yet highly stereotyped, multi-axis gene expression gradients superimposed onto discrete compartments of the striatum. Additionally, we identify core-shell organization of the internal globus pallidus. This unified, cross-species spatial transcriptomics atlas will be a foundational resource for characterizing the molecular and functional organization of the BG and their roles in health and disease.

items.title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are conserved brain regions essential for motor control, learning, emotion, and cognition and are implicated in neurological and psychiatric disease, yet a unified cross-species taxonomy of BG cell types is lacking. We present a multiomic consensus atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from humans, macaques, and marmosets spanning eight BG structures, integrating gene expression, open chromatin, and spatial profiling. Alignment across species and to mouse and human whole-brain atlases identifies 61 homologous cell types conserved over 76 million years. Dorsal-ventral spatial identity is more conserved than D1/D2 receptor or striosome/matrix identity, and striatum (STR) D2 SMYD2-HTR7 spiny projection neurons have distinct molecular, electrophysiological, and morphological features. Cis-regulatory analysis reveals conserved sequence grammars that encode cell identity and inform viral targeting, and cell-type-resolved mapping localizes psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk to specific BG cell populations. This work provides a foundational resource for BG evolution, function, and disease.

items.title: Toward an integrated framework for a human and mammalian brain cell atlas.
items.abstract: The NIH BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is developing a standardized, integrated reference framework for classifying and studying brain cell types across human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse. We present a cross-species, multimodal atlas of the basal ganglia, a group of subcortical nuclei central to motor control, adaptive behavior, and neurological disease. Built from large-scale single-cell transcriptomic classification and integrated with epigenomic, spatial genomic, multiomic, and developmental datasets, the atlas provides a curated, data-driven taxonomy with standardized nomenclature, extensive phenotypic characterization, and community-informed annotation. Cell types are mapped into species-specific anatomical reference frameworks and linked across species through structural ontologies. Realizing this resource required coordinated standards for tissue acquisition and processing, harmonized donor metadata, anatomical registration, sequencing pipelines, data infrastructure, visualization, mapping tools, and interoperable metadata. The BICAN basal ganglia atlas demonstrates how pipelines and standards can be implemented, validated, and scaled toward a whole-brain human and mammalian cell-type reference.
items.authors: BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN). Electronic address: ecker@salk.edu

items.title: Stepping (hi)stones: Charting a single-cell multiomic path toward understanding the human brain.
items.abstract: In this issue of Cell, two single-cell multiomic atlases jointly profile transcription and histone modifications across different regions of the adult human brain, revealing cell-type-specific regulatory landscapes, developmental epigenetic memory, and improved interpretation of neurological variants. These studies establish a framework for understanding human brain cell identity, evolution, and pathology.

items.title: From the human genome to the human brain cell atlas.
items.abstract: The BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is establishing an evolving reference for neuroscience by integrating cell identities, anatomy, and multimodal evidence across species. In analogy with the Human Genome Project, the BICAN basal ganglia atlas is a model for a federated reference to advance understanding of brain organization, function, variation, and disease.

items.title: Deploying liquid intelligence in cancer: Finding answers in our blood.
items.abstract: Liquid biopsies are one of the few noninvasive procedures for probing disease at the molecular level. They represent a scalable solution to cancer detection and monitoring by capturing tumor-derived signals from circulating biomolecules such as proteins, DNA, RNA, and metabolites. However, these signals are often sparse, heterogeneous, and shaped by genetics, demographics, and comorbidities. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, especially with multimodal foundation models, have proven capable of extracting signals from noisy, high-dimensional data. Pretraining on large cohorts and integrating complementary modalities may improve sensitivity for tumor signals in blood, though significant clinical and infrastructural barriers remain. This review synthesizes advances in liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence and examines how their convergence can enable enhanced cancer monitoring.

items.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4+ T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer.
items.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (TH1)-like immune architectures in mismatch repair-deficient tumors associated with response to anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T-dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4+ T cells differentiated into TH1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r+ early effector CD4+ intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with TH1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ-dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8+ effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4+ T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

items.title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA).
items.abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53, PIK3CA, PTEN, SETD2, MAP3K14, and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

items.title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability.
items.abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

items.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants.
items.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

items.title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris.
items.abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO2) ice in both the 12CO2 and 13CO2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

items.title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia.
items.abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport-0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III-independent reverse-topology budding.

items.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes.
items.abstract: Lysosomal Ca2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca2+-imaging-based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca2+ stores, diminished Ca2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca2+ transport, and Tmem184b-deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

items.title: Building a cell engineering toolbox.
items.abstract: Biological diversity and deep learning are harnessed for discovery.

items.title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides.
items.abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

items.title: Atmospheric O2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990.
items.abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O2) and CO2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year-1 decade-1) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year-1), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year-1, accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

items.title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene.
items.abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss-like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

items.title: Nature's cellular nuke.
items.abstract: Discovery of an unknown immune cell type and its cytotoxic killing mode.

items.title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis.
items.abstract: Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

items.title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly.
items.abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a "molecular glue," stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain-containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This "produce-and-trap" mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

items.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs.
items.abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

items.title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity.
items.abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth's viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

items.title: New tools for an old problem.
items.abstract: How does one map, measure, and model the aging brain?

items.abstract: Heat from thermogenic plants serves as a signal to pollinators.

items.title: Fixing the power transmission crisis.
items.abstract: Experimentation, learning, and existing regulatory and technology options could help align stakeholders.

items.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore.
items.abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens, multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on 'Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.
