items.title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids.
items.abstract: Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the T2 dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime, theoretically predicted to be generic for two-dimensional electron systems.

items.title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April-May 2026.
items.abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

items.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak.
items.abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

items.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment.
items.abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

items.title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space.
items.abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

items.title: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination.
items.abstract: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

items.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.

sections.objective: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.
sections.methods: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.
sections.results: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.
sections.conclusion: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

items.title: Deep sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes uncovers substantial contribution of rare variants to agronomic traits.
items.abstract: Rare variants are highly abundant, yet their genome-wide contributions to agronomic traits remain elusive in plants. Here, we performed deep whole-genome sequencing of 3,367 diverse elite maize inbred lines, uncovering 75.3 million variants, of which 79.2% were rare. Overall, we identified 411 independent association signals for 10 agronomic traits, including 359 attributable to globally rare variants, with rare variants showing effect sizes approximately 2.4 times those of common variants. Frequency-stratified genome-based restricted maximum likelihood (GREML) analyses indicated that rare variants captured a substantial proportion of phenotypic variance for traits under strong adaptive selection, consistent with the allele frequencies of trait-associated variants shifting from common in tropical to rare in temperate maize. Complementing conventional variant-level genome-wide association studies (GWAS), gene-based tests identified an additional 94 candidate gene-trait associations. Our study highlights rare variants as important components of the genetic architecture of complex agronomic traits in maize and provides much-needed resources for future functional studies and breeding.

items.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy - Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial.

sections.objective: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9.
sections.methods: In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

items.title: Prasugrel versus Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndromes.

sections.objective: Whether prasugrel or ticagrelor should be the preferred P2Y12 inhibitor for patients with an acute coronary syndrome is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted a registry-based, open-label, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomized trial in Sweden involving adults who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention for an acute coronary syndrome. Seven regions, grouped into three clusters, switched from ticagrelor to prasugrel as the default P2Y12 inhibitor in a randomized sequence across four 9-month periods between 2021 and 2024. The primary end point was a composite of death from any cause, fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction, or fatal or nonfatal stroke through 1 year, as ascertained from national registries. In the intention-to-treat analysis, a mixed model adjusted for cluster and calendar time was used to obtain a policy-level estimate.
sections.results: A total of 17,095 patients were enrolled; 9444 received care under the default ticagrelor policy, and 7651 received care under the default prasugrel policy. The mean (±SD) age of the patients was 69.8±11.5 years, and 36.8% were at least 75 years old; 27.8% of the patients were female. A total of 39.4% presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), 43.7% with non-STEMI, and 16.8% with unstable angina. At 1 year, a primary end-point event had occurred in 11.8% of the patients in the ticagrelor-policy group and in 11.1% of those in the prasugrel-policy group (adjusted odds ratio [prasugrel vs. ticagrelor], 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.06), and major bleeding had occurred in 4.4% and 4.2%, respectively (adjusted odds ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.99).
sections.conclusion: In an unselected population of patients with an acute coronary syndrome who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention, the risk of ischemic events was not lower with a default prasugrel policy than with a default ticagrelor policy. (Funded by Region Västra Götaland; SWITCH-SWEDEHEART ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05183178.).

items.title: Rivaroxaban Then Aspirin vs. Aspirin Alone after Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.

sections.objective: Aspirin after an initial short course of rivaroxaban has been shown to be safe and effective for the prevention of venous thromboembolism after total hip or total knee arthroplasty, but uncertainty remains about the use of aspirin alone.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients to receive once-daily thromboprophylaxis with either 81 mg of aspirin or 10 mg of oral rivaroxaban for the first 5 days after total hip or total knee arthroplasty. All the patients then received further thromboprophylaxis with 81 mg of aspirin daily for 9 additional days after knee arthroplasty and for 30 additional days after hip arthroplasty. Patients were followed for 90 days for symptomatic venous thromboembolism, which consisted of either proximal deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (primary effectiveness outcome), and for bleeding complications (primary safety outcome). The noninferiority margin for aspirin alone as compared with rivaroxaban-aspirin was 0.7 percentage points.
sections.results: A total of 5429 patients underwent randomization. Venous thromboembolism developed in 13 of 2718 patients (0.48%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 12 of 2647 patients (0.45%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, 0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.34 to 0.39; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events occurred in 45 of 2718 patients (1.66%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 54 of 2647 patients (2.04%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, -0.38%; 95% CI, -1.11 to 0.34).
sections.conclusion: After total hip and total knee arthroplasty, the use of aspirin alone was not inferior to a strategy of using rivaroxaban followed by aspirin for the prevention of symptomatic venous thromboembolism, with no clinically relevant difference in bleeding events. (Funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research; EPCAT III ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04075240.).

items.title: Key Determinants and Clinical Impact of Male Factor Infertility: From Etiology to Treatment.

sections.objective: To summarise the key determinants, classification systems, diagnostics and treatments of MFI, and the environmental, nutritional and lifestyle factors influencing male fertility, with their implications for personalized therapy and for men's reproductive and general health.
sections.conclusion: MFI is multifactorial, requiring a holistic approach to diagnosis and treatment. Comprehensive andrological assessment, alongside personalized treatment strategies, is essential for optimizing fertility outcomes and addressing comorbidities in subfertile men.
sections.other: Male factor infertility (MFI) contributes to a substantial proportion of couple infertility, yet the male partner is often incompletely evaluated, particularly when medically assisted reproduction is pursued. New clinical, hormonal and genetic classification systems, and evidence linking MFI to broader male health, are changing how these men should be assessed. A narrative review was conducted based on expert consensus and a focused review of the literature. Key publications were identified from major international guidelines, high-impact reviews, and original studies relevant to MFI. Evidence was selected to reflect clinically relevant developments in diagnostics, classification systems, and management. Genetic variants, environmental exposures and lifestyle choices are key determinants of male fertility. Three complementary classification systems - pathophysiological, endocrine (APHRODITE) and phenotypic (Human Phenotype Ontology) - aid diagnosis, standardized communication and gene discovery. Hormonal and surgical treatments are effective but should be personalized, and evidence for several add-on diagnostics and empirical therapies remains limited. The limitations of current diagnostics, such as semen analysis, are critically evaluated. As a consensus-based narrative review without a systematic search, selection bias cannot be excluded.

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of Nectin-4-targeted [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT versus [18F]-FDG PET/CT for Staging of Locally Advanced and Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma: A Prospective, Single-center, Phase 2 Feasibility Trial.
items.abstract: Enfortumab vedotin (EV), an anti-nectin-4 antibody-drug conjugate, alone and with pembrolizumab (EV plus pembrolizumab [EV/P]), has transformed the treatment of locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC), yet remains biomarker agnostic. We prospectively evaluated [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT ([68Ga]-N188 PET/CT) as a whole-body alternative for nectin-4 imaging, with [18F]-FDG PET/CT as an active comparator and conventional computed tomography as the reference standard for staging la/mUC in 25 patients planned for EV/P. [18F]-FDG PET/CT showed a higher maximum standardized uptake value and tumor-to-background ratio than [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT across most lesion types (primary tumor, visceral, and osseous), except for lymph nodes. The overall tracer correlation was weak (Spearman r = 0.196), strongest in lymph nodes (r = 0.657), and absent in primary tumors and bone lesions. For primary tumor detection, [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT had higher specificity (86% vs 57%) and positive predictive value (92% vs 83%) than FDG, which had higher sensitivity (88% vs 67%). Nodal staging performance was similar in the tracers. For distant metastases, both achieved 100% sensitivity and negative predictive value, with [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT showing marginally higher specificity. [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT is feasible for whole-body nectin-4 assessment in la/mUC and supports a distinct biodistribution from FDG, suggesting complementary rather than interchangeable roles. Further prospective evaluation with treatment-outcome correlation is warranted before its use as a biomarker to guide EV-based therapy selection.

items.title: Step change in glaucoma polygenic risk score performance enables clinical utility.

sections.objective: Open-angle glaucoma (OAG) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness and is highly heritable. Despite effective treatments, approximately 50% of cases remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate a clinically applicable, genetics-based risk prediction tool for OAG across diverse ancestries.
sections.methods: Genetic association study and risk prediction analysis. More than 6 million individuals contributing genome-wide association study data from multiple ancestry groups. We constructed a comprehensive polygenic risk score (PRS) for OAG using a multitrait modeling framework that integrated glaucoma-related traits, including intraocular pressure, optic disc parameters, and ocular hypertension. PRS performance was evaluated for OAG risk across major ancestry groups and assessed for associations with age at diagnosis, treatment escalation, surgical outcomes, and familial risk.
sections.results: In Australian individuals of European ancestry, those in the top 10% of the PRS distribution had a 10-fold increased risk of OAG compared with the remainder (OR 10.04, 95% CI 7.43-13.59), substantially outperforming our previously published PRS (OR 4.2). Similar performance was observed in U.S. European ancestry data (OR 9.09, 95% CI 5.09-16.26). In UK Biobank Europeans the OR for the top 10% versus the remainder was 4.91 (95% CI 4.25-5.69). Although performance was attenuated in other ancestry groups (OR top 10% vs. remainder: 4.01 in South Asian, 3.39 in East Asian, and ranging from 2.26 to 3.81 in African ancestry populations depending on cohort), high PRS percentiles corresponded to elevated absolute risk across all groups. On average, individuals in the highest-risk decile developed glaucoma approximately 25 years earlier than those in the lowest decile and had ∼100-fold (OR 96.83, 95% CI 52.61-178.21) higher risk. The PRS also predicted treatment escalation in early disease, prevalent and incident glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk among first-degree relatives.
sections.conclusion: This enhanced PRS, available for clinical use through an accredited genotyping workflow, enables effective risk stratification for OAG across diverse ancestries, facilitating earlier identification and treatment of high-risk individuals while supporting resource rationalisation for those at low risk. Performance is strongest in European ancestry populations, and further work is needed to improve equity of performance across ancestries.
sections.other: Odds ratios (ORs) for OAG by PRS percentile, age at disease onset, absolute risk estimates, treatment escalation, glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk in first-degree relatives.

items.title: The ONSET Study: Optic Neuritis Frequently Represents the Onset of Central Nervous System Inflammatory Disease.

sections.objective: To determine the long-term diagnostic transition and temporal pattern of central nervous system (CNS) inflammatory events after a first episode of optic neuritis.
sections.methods: Multicenter retrospective cohort study. Patients with MRI-confirmed first-episode optic neuritis were retrospectively enrolled. Clinical characteristics, antibody status, treatments, subsequent events, and final diagnoses were collected from longitudinal follow-up.
sections.results: A total of 601 patients were enrolled and followed for a median of 2 years (interquartile range [IQR], 1-4.5 years). At onset, initial diagnoses were idiopathic in 295 patients (49.1%), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) in 134 (22.3%), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in 120 (20.0%), multiple sclerosis (MS) in 16 (2.7%), and other diagnoses in 36 (6.0%). At last follow-up, final diagnoses were single isolated optic neuritis in 222 patients (36.9%), recurrent isolated optic neuritis in 23 (3.8%), MOGAD in 134 (22.3%), NMOSD in 125 (20.8%), MS in 77 (12.8%), and other diagnoses in 20 (3.3%). Overall, 166 of 601 patients (27.6%) experienced at least one CNS inflammatory event other than the initial optic neuritis. Recurrent optic neuritis was the most frequent event (58.8%), followed by encephalitis (22.9%) and myelitis (18.3%). Among patients with post-onset events, 64 (48.9%) developed an event within 1 year and 97 (74.0%) within 2 years after the initial episode of optic neuritis. Among the 131 patients with post-onset events, more than half (77 patients, 58.8%) developed outside maintenance therapy, including 68 after treatment discontinuation and 9 without maintenance therapy.
sections.conclusion: More than one-quarter of patients with first-episode optic neuritis experienced CNS inflammatory events other than the initial optic neuritis, and only approximately one-third ultimately remained classified as having single isolated optic neuritis. These findings demonstrate that first-episode optic neuritis frequently represents the onset of an underlying CNS inflammatory disease, underscoring the importance of long-term neurological surveillance following the initial episode.
sections.other: Six hundred one consecutive patients with first-episode optic neuritis who presented to 11 tertiary referral centers in Japan between January 2016 and December 2023. Transition in the diagnosis of optic neuritis from the time of initial onset to the end of longitudinal follow-up.

items.title: Applicability of Prediction Models: Aligning Models with Clinical Use.
items.abstract: Doctors increasingly rely on models that predict a patient's risk of future health problems. These models only work well when the patients they were built on resemble the patients being treated now, in illness type, care setting, and stage of disease. This is easy to see when the mismatch is obvious: a model built on hospital patients may not suit those seen in a family doctor's office. The same problem is harder to appreciate when it comes from where a patient sits on a chronic illness journey. Using severe chronic kidney disease as an example, this review shows that a model built from patients who have recently progressed to this more severe stage works better for patients at that same point, while a model built from patients who have lived with the disease for years works better for those further along. This review offers practical steps to keep predictions aligned with the patients they serve.

items.title: Pooled cohort analysis of renin-angiotensin system inhibition and the risk of kidney outcomes in APOL1-mediated chronic kidney disease in the CRIC and SPRINT studies.

sections.objective: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) variants are common in individuals of African descent and increase risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASis) are a mainstay of therapy for hypertension and proteinuric CKD but were not historically recommended as first-line anti-hypertensive therapy in Black individuals. Here, we evaluated RASis versus other antihypertensive therapy on kidney outcomes in Black individuals by APOL1 genotype.
sections.methods: We included Black participants with APOL1 genotyping on first-line anti-hypertensive therapy from the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) and Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT). We evaluated whether the impact of RASi-prescription on kidney outcomes was modified by APOL1 risk allele number or baseline albuminuria, using Cox models with inverse probability of treatment weighting and marginal structural models.
sections.results: A total of 3418 participants (62% from SPRINT), 40%, 44% and 16% carrying zero, one and two APOL1 risk alleles, respectively, were included. RASi-use compared to other first-line antihypertensive therapy was associated with a comparably lower risk of the kidney outcome in individuals with zero (hazard ratio (HR) 0.62 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.87]), one (HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.49-0.94]) or two risk alleles (HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.40-0.86]). This benefit was driven by albuminuric participants, but estimates were similarly low for RASi-use compared to other antihypertensive therapy in albuminuric (HR 0.62, 95% CI [0.41-0.93]) and non-albuminuric (HR 0.37, 95% CI [0.13-1.08]) participants with two APOL1 risk alleles, although the estimate was imprecise in non-albuminuric participants.
sections.conclusion: RASi-based therapy, addressed as a time-updated pooled treatment, provided similar benefit across APOL1 genotypes, driven by albuminuric participants. Among individuals with two APOL1 risk alleles, outcomes were similar regardless of baseline albuminuria. However, further studies are needed due to small sample sizes and the inability of statistical methods to capture clinical variables that may have affected prescription changes.

items.title: A coronavirus protease activates sensory neurons via TRPA1 to drive sneeze, cough, and pain.
items.abstract: Sneezing, coughing, and pain are common symptoms of respiratory viral infection. These responses are initiated by airway-innervating nociceptors that detect noxious stimuli, but how SARS-CoV-2 activates these neurons remains unclear. Here, we show that the coronavirus papain-like protease (PLpro) directly activates airway-innervating nociceptors in mice and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived nociceptors. PLpro triggers sneezing, coughing, acute pain, and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release in the airways. Both the proteolytic activity of PLpro and the host ion channel transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) are required for neuronal activation and sneezing. Infection with the mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 or the murine coronavirus MHV-A59 also induces sneezing in mice, and MHV-A59-evoked sneezing is TRPA1-dependent. SARS-CoV-2 infection of the trigeminal ganglia altered transcriptional programs associated with nociception, including upregulation of the TRPA1-CGRP signaling pathway activated by PLpro. Together, these findings reveal a direct mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 triggers pain and airway reflexes and identify PLpro and TRPA1 as potential therapeutic targets for COVID-19.

items.title: A consensus spinal cord cell-type atlas across mouse, macaque, and human.
items.abstract: The spinal cord contains cell types critical for motor, sensory, and autonomic function, many of which are implicated in neurological disease and injury. Yet no shared molecular framework links human spinal cord cell types to the animal models used to study them. Here, we present a cross-species atlas integrating single-nucleus gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics from over one million nuclei spanning cervical to sacral segments in human, macaque, and mouse. Consensus clustering resolves 111 cell type groups replicable across all three species, whose spatial distributions map spinal laminae and nuclei, including Clarke's column. Identity and laminar organization are highly conserved, yet abundance and expression are allometrically scaled, with the dorsal horn being the principal site of divergence, concentrated in neurotransmitter receptor genes and including a primate-specific glycine receptor subunit switch. Sequence models uncover a conserved transcription factor grammar and nominate motifs underlying enhancer-adeno-associated virus (AAV) access to a divergent dorsal horn population.

items.title: Implications of Image-Level Duplication in Public Glaucoma Datasets.

sections.objective: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) can be trusted only if validated in patients not used for development. In glaucoma AI, a few public datasets from 1 laboratory serve as those independent cohorts. To determine whether 3 public glaucoma datasets used for external validation and fairness evaluation are independent patient cohorts.
sections.methods: This cross-sectional dataset audit and record-linkage analysis was conducted in July 2026 using the publicly distributed files of Harvard-GDP (1000 eyes), Harvard-GF (3300 eyes), and Harvard-FairVision (10 000 eyes), all from a single laboratory. Records were linked by exact visual field and demographic fingerprints, with chance modeled from the within-dataset collision rate and permutation. All 1302 candidate pairs underwent direct image comparison.
sections.results: Harvard-GF and Harvard-FairVision matched on 1302 eyes against 1.9 expected by chance. Direct comparison confirmed 1031 (79.2%; 95% CI, 76.9%-81.4%) as the same 3-dimensional OCT volume (cosine similarity ≥0.9999; 88% of voxels exactly equal), at least 31% of the 3300 Harvard-GF eyes, a lower bound. Duplication was similar across the 3 Harvard-FairVision splits (78.5%-80.8%). Harvard-GDP and Harvard-GF shared 22 eyes matching exactly on all 52 total-deviation points and mean deviation, all in the Harvard-GF validation split; Harvard-GDP distributes no OCT volume, so its overlap rests on weaker evidence. No file carried a patient identifier, and no release disclosed the overlap; among the 64 of 105 citing studies whose full text we obtained, none reported it. Across 5 training runs, a classifier trained on 1 dataset and evaluated on the other gave an area under the curve of 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94) where 78.5% (95% CI, 74.0%-82.5%) of test eyes were training data, against 0.78 (95% CI, 0.72-0.83) out of sample (inflation, 0.12; 95% CI, 0.06-0.18). Inflation occurred in every racial subgroup and was larger where out-of-sample performance was lower (Spearman ρ = -0.57; permutation P = .02).
sections.conclusion: These findings suggest that the examined datasets were not independent cohorts. Treating them as independent benchmarks inflates reported performance and might mask fairness gaps through data leakage and nonindependent validation.
sections.other: Number of shared eyes and image-level identity of optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans distributed under different identifiers.

items.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Heterogeneity in Clinical Evidence: JACC Evidence Review.
items.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

items.title: Longitudinal Endoleak Behaviour Following Complex Aortic Repair With Branched Devices.

sections.objective: This study aimed to determine the incidence, natural history, outcomes and risk factors of endoleak following branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex abdominal aortic aneurysm (cAAA) and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).
sections.methods: This retrospective, single-centre study enrolled patients with cAAA and TAAA treated with BEVAR. Patients with at least 1 target vessel incorporated using directional branches were included. End points were spontaneous resolution of endoleak detected on completion angiography, 3-year freedom from persistent type I/III endoleak and endoleak-related reintervention. Multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for type II endoleak (T2EL) and branch-related endoleak (BREL).
sections.results: In a 6-year period, 298 patients underwent fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) of which 129 patients (mean age 72 ± 9 years; 62% male) underwent F/BEVAR for 36 cAAA (27.9%) and 93 TAAA (72.1%) with at least 1 directional branch. In all, 458 reno-mesenteric arteries were incorporated using directional branches. Completion intra-operative angiography detected endoleak in 81 patients (64.8%), of which 43.2% demonstrated spontaneous resolution on postoperative computed tomographic angiography. During a mean follow-up of 20.2 ± 19.9 months, 14 branches (3.0%) in 14 patients (10.9%) developed BREL, predominantly type Ic. Freedom from persistent type I/III endoleak and endoleak-related reintervention were 70.6% and 68.5% at 3 years, respectively. Aneurysm diameter ≥80 mm (hazard ratio [HR] 2.76, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-4.95; P < .001), post-dissection aetiology (HR 1.84, 95% CI, 1.02-3.33; P = .043) and accessory renal artery (ARA) ≥3 mm in diameter that was not incorporated or pre-emptively embolised (HR 2.03, 95% CI, 1.11-3.74; P = .022) were identified as independent risk factors for T2EL.
sections.conclusion: Immediate endoleak following BEVAR was common, but a substantial proportion were self-limiting. Type Ic endoleak was the most common type of BREL and the most frequent indication for endoleak-related reintervention. Large aneurysm diameter, post-dissection aetiology and ARA increased risk for T2EL.Clinical ImpactEndoleak following branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) was commonly detected on completion angiography; however, immediate intervention was not required after ensuring adequate sealing zones and optimised bridging stent configuration, as 43% demonstrated spontaneous resolution on early postoperative imaging. Type Ic endoleak was the predominant form of branch-related endoleak, highlighting the importance of meticulous attention to target vessel landing zones. When anatomically feasible, incorporation of accessory renal artery ≥3 mm in the repair is recommended; alternatively, pre-emptive embolisation may reduce type II endoleak incidence.

items.title: Prognostic Impact of Post-Contrast Acute Kidney Injury in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.

sections.objective: Post-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) has been regarded as a serious complication after contrast administration, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the prognostic significance of PC-AKI following endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains controversial due to heterogeneity in previous study populations. This study evaluated the association between PC-AKI and longitudinal changes in postoperative renal function and mortality in a well-defined CKD cohort undergoing EVAR.
sections.methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with CKD undergoing elective, primary, and non-complex infrarenal EVAR. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of PC-AKI. Longitudinal changes in serum creatinine after EVAR, dialysis initiation, all-cause mortality, and the association between contrast volume and PC-AKI were evaluated.
sections.results: Among 479 EVAR procedures, 164 patients with CKD were included, of whom 17 (10.4%) developed PC-AKI. The linear mixed-effects model showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Serum creatinine remained significantly higher in the PC-AKI group than in the non-PC-AKI group at all postoperative time points. However, in the PC-AKI group, model-adjusted mean serum creatinine decreased significantly from 1.75 mg/dL in the postoperative period to 1.46 mg/dL at 12 months with an estimated change of -0.29 mg/dL (95% CI, -0.50 to -0.09; P = .003). No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation (5.9% vs 0.7%; P = .197) or all-cause mortality (29.4% vs 23.8%; P = .565). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival between the groups (log-rank P = .246). In the multivariable analysis, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI (odds ratio [OR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.98-1.01; P = .845), whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate remained significantly associated with PC-AKI (OR, 1.06 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 decrease; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; P = .018).
sections.conclusion: In this study, PC-AKI may not necessarily be associated with adverse subsequent renal or survival outcomes. In addition, underlying renal vulnerability may be more closely associated with the development of PC-AKI than contrast volume alone. While PC-AKI should not be disregarded, judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.Clinical ImpactPost-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) occurred in approximately 10% of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing elective, primary, non-complex infrarenal endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Although serum creatinine remained higher in patients with PC-AKI at all postoperative time points, it decreased significantly from the postoperative period to 12 months. No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation or overall survival between the groups. In addition, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI, whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate was. These findings suggest that contrast use should not be excessively restricted solely because of concerns regarding PC-AKI, and that judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.

items.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
items.abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

items.title: Gene discovery and pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain in a genome-wide association study of >1.2 million individuals.
items.abstract: Chronic pain is highly prevalent worldwide, yet its genetic architecture remains to be fully elucidated. Here we leveraged data from 1,235,695 European-ancestry individuals across three biobanks. In a meta-analytic genome-wide association study of multidimensional pain (MP), we identified 343 independent loci, 92 of which were new pain associations. Sex-specific meta-analyses revealed 115 independent loci (12 of which were new) among males (n = 583,066) and 12 loci (2 of which were new) among females (n = 241,266). Multi-omic gene prioritization analyses highlighted 490 genes associated with MP through their effects on brain-specific and blood-specific regulation. Mendelian randomization analyses showed causal associations between MP and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders and C-reactive protein levels. MP variants also showed pleiotropic associations with several brain imaging-derived phenotypes. This study expands our knowledge of the genetics of pain and its pathogenesis, highlighting the importance of its pleiotropy with multiple disorders and elucidating its multi-omic pathophysiology.

items.title: Personalised mobile health coaching from early pregnancy to 12-months postpartum for females at risk of gestational diabetes (Bump2Baby and Me): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Maternal overweight and obesity increase the risk of gestational diabetes and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Digital health interventions offer scalable, personalised support, but evidence for interventions spanning both pregnancy and postpartum remains scarce. We evaluated the effectiveness of a personalised mobile health (mHealth) coaching intervention for females at increased risk of gestational diabetes.
sections.methods: This multicentre, randomised controlled trial conducted in Australia, Ireland, Spain, and the UK enrolled pregnant females aged 18 years and older between 12-24 weeks of gestation with increased risk of gestational diabetes (Monash GDM risk tool score ≥3; tool risk factors were maternal age, BMI, ethnicity, family history of diabetes, and past history of gestational diabetes). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using computer-generated block randomisation (block size 200; stratified by site) to receive either personalised mHealth coaching via smartphone providing synchronous and asynchronous support through pregnancy to 12 months postpartum alongside usual maternity care, or usual maternity care alone. Usual maternity care, including gestational diabetes screening and management, continued unchanged in both groups, and both groups received Bluetooth-enabled scales. Participants and health coaches could not be masked to allocation; clinical staff providing usual care, laboratory staff, and trial statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was the between-group mean difference in BMI at 12 months postpartum among females at risk of gestational diabetes. The trial was registered at Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Register, ACTRN12620001240932.
sections.results: Between Feb 9, 2021, and Oct 22, 2023, 4386 females were screened, 3521 were excluded, and 865 were randomly assigned (437 to the mHealth intervention group and 428 to the control group). The mean age of participants was 35·2 years (SD 4·3), and most participants were White (588 [73%] of 804). Mean BMI change did not differ between groups (intervention, -0·04 kg/m2 [SE 0·12] vs control, 0·04 kg/m2 [0·13]). Adverse events were recorded in 18% (79 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 25% (106 of 428) of participants in the control group; serious adverse events occurred in 6% (28 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 9% (40 of 428) of participants in the control group. No adverse or serious adverse events were considered related to the intervention.
sections.conclusion: Personalised mHealth coaching spanning pregnancy and an extended postpartum support period did not reduce mean maternal BMI at 12 months compared with usual care. Findings suggest that mHealth interventions targeting at-risk females might benefit from addressing a broader range of maternal health outcomes beyond weight management.

items.title: A longitudinal mixed methods investigation into young people's collective environmental action, climate change distress, and wellbeing: The EnvironMental Action study.

sections.objective: Taking collective climate action, such as activism and volunteering, can be a response to climate change distress. Although action has been linked to both improved wellbeing and greater climate change distress, these relationships remain unclear. The aim of this study was to better understand the interrelationships between climate change action, climate change distress, and wellbeing in young people using longitudinal and mixed methods.
sections.methods: The study took place from Jan 26, 2024, to April 16, 2025. We collected longitudinal surveys (at 0, 6, and 12 months) from self-selecting environmental activists, volunteers, and a control group (general population), measuring psychological distress (depression and anxiety symptoms), social connectedness, wellbeing, climate change distress and impairment, and climate-change hope. Co-designed reflective journals and workshops were co-analysed to understand participants' experiences and contextualise quantitative findings using qualitative themes.
sections.results: Linear regression analysis of survey data from 241 young people revealed that self-allocation to an environmental activist or environmental volunteer group at baseline was cross-sectionally associated with higher wellbeing (β=1·88, 95% CI 0·52-3·25) alongside higher climate change distress and impairment (β=4·36, 95% CI 0·57-8·12). Between 0 and six months, the baseline group was associated with increases in social connectedness (β=6·42, 95% CI 2·88-9·96), wellbeing (β=5·61, 95% CI 4·10-7·12), and hope; lower psychological distress (β=-3·74, 95% CI -7·12 to -0·38); and increased climate change distress (β=5·38, 95% CI 1·37-9·39). At 12 months, action was associated with subsequent decreases in climate change distress and impairment below 0-month and 6-month values (β=-8·65, 95% CI -14·97 to -2·33), and wellbeing benefits were sustained (β=2·72, 95% CI 0·52-4·91). 24 young people took part in journalling, focus group discussions, or both. Convergent themes across activists, volunteers, and the general population included "challenging emotions", "barriers to change", and the "influence of media". Themes unique to activists and volunteers were "challenges with action", "motivation to action", and "rewards and resilience." "Barriers to action" and "values and small actions" were unique to young people not involved.
sections.conclusion: Young environmental activists and volunteers can be expected to experience a complex and dynamic mix of challenging and rewarding emotions and experiences, potentially including elevated climate change distress requiring adequate support. Policy changes that reduce barriers to involvement (eg, subsidisation of costs) and action-oriented climate messaging could support more young people to get involved. Yet, the mental health risks associated with climate change can only be directly addressed through meaningful social and political action on climate, for which young people should not carry the burden.

items.title: Nasal mucosal humoral responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination priming schedules in the UK: a substudy of the Com-COV single-blind, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

sections.objective: Mucosal surfaces form the first line of defence against respiratory pathogens. Most licensed COVID-19 vaccines are delivered intramuscularly and elicit strong systemic immunity. Whether such vaccines generate locally derived nasal mucosal responses remains uncertain. In this substudy, we aimed to investigate mucosal and systemic antibody responses following different intramuscular SARS-CoV-2 priming vaccination schedules.
sections.methods: In the Com-COV single-blind, randomised, non-inferiority trial, adults aged 50 years or older who were COVID-19 unvaccinated and SARS-CoV-2 infection-naive were enrolled across eight sites in the UK between Feb 11, 2021, and Feb 26, 2021. Participants were randomised to receive homologous or heterologous vaccination schedules using ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 (ChAd) and BNT162b2 (BNT), administered at either a 28-day or 84-day interval. This substudy collected nasal lining fluid using nasosorption strips in long-interval cohorts. Anti-spike and anti-nucleocapsid IgG and IgA were quantified in serum and nasal samples by electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. Correlations were assessed using Pearson's coefficients.
sections.results: Mucosal lining fluid samples were collected from 101 participants (mean age 59·1 years [SD 5·0]; 49 [49%] women; 33 [33%] non-White ethnicities). Significant increases in mucosal anti-spike IgA from baseline were seen for ChAd-BNT (geometric mean concentration was 612·8 AU/mL [95% CI 363·6-1032·7]) and BNT-BNT (906·4 AU/mL [619·36-1325·8]). This corresponded to fold rises of 2·78 (1·39-5·54) for ChAd-BNT and 3·11 (1·76-5·50) for BNT-BNT. Mucosal anti-spike IgA trajectories did not mirror vaccination-induced systemic markers, including serum anti-spike IgG (r=0·13, 0·03-0·23, p=0·013). Instead, mucosal anti-spike IgA trajectories correlated with mucosal anti-nucleocapsid IgA (r=0·78, 0·74-0·82, p=5 × 10-77), consistent with mucosal SARS-CoV-2 exposure. Across all schedules, no evidence existed of de novo nasal IgA induction following one or two intramuscular doses, irrespective of baseline serostatus. Observed increases in nasal anti-spike IgA were more consistent with intercurrent mucosal SARS-CoV-2 exposure than direct vaccine effect. Nasal IgG appeared to reflect systemic vaccine responses, whereas SARS-CoV-2 exposure was associated with additional changes in mucosal IgG.
sections.conclusion: Intramuscular immunisation induces robust systemic immunity and remains central to emergency and routine vaccination schedules. However, intramuscular immunisation does not appear to generate de novo local nasal IgA, levels of which have been associated with protection beyond that conferred by serum IgG. Interpretation of vaccine-induced mucosal responses could be confounded by asymptomatic community exposure. Mucosally delivered vaccines are a biologically plausible complementary strategy to enhance protection and reduce transmission, and thus, need further investigation.

items.title: Geographical targeting of active case-finding for tuberculosis in Pakistan using artificial intelligence software (SPOT-TB): a pragmatic, stepped wedge, cluster-randomised control trial.

sections.objective: Community-wide active case-finding is being increasingly implemented as a tuberculosis elimination intervention. However, conventional site selection strategies can result in low screening yields. We aimed to evaluate whether geographical targeting using artificial intelligence (AI) software can improve detection of tuberculosis during screening in comparison to conventional approaches for site selection, within the programmatic setting in Pakistan.
sections.methods: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped wedge, cluster-randomised trial across all four provinces of Pakistan, and was embedded within The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria-supported active case-finding activities implemented by Pakistan's National TB Control Program and private sector partners. 30 mobile x-ray van teams operating in 68 districts were randomised to transition from conventional site selection approaches (based on field team knowledge, experience, and historical data) to an AI-guided targeting strategy using the Mapping and Analysis for Tailored disease Control and Health system strengthening-Artificial Intelligence (MATCH-AI) software. All individuals attending community active case-finding camps were eligible for participation except those excluded as per the national guidelines. The primary outcome, camp positivity yield, was defined as the number of individuals diagnosed with bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis per camp. The primary analysis was by intention to treat and camps conducted within a 5-km radius of AI recommended locations were included in a validated per-protocol analysis. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06017843, and has been completed.
sections.results: Between Aug 1, 2023, and Sept 28, 2024, 3936 screening camps were conducted (2046 [52·0%] control, 1890 [48·0%] intervention), screening 269 254 individuals. In the intention-to-treat analysis, camp positivity yield was 7% higher in the intervention group, but not statistically significant (adjusted risk ratio 1·07, 95% CI 0·94-1·22; p=0·27). In the validated per-protocol analysis, the camp positivity yield was 32% higher in the intervention group (1·32, 1·12-1·54; p<0·0001). Yields were highest in districts with moderate yields at baseline before the trial and in rural districts.
sections.conclusion: AI-guided targeting was associated with substantially higher detection of bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis during active case-finding in the validated per-protocol analysis and could improve efficiency of community-based tuberculosis case-finding interventions in high burden countries. Routine programmatic data did not capture all implementation or process-quality indicators, limiting assessment of implementation fidelity and variation across sites.

items.title: Degradation of mucin O-glycans by a human gut symbiont requires a complex enzyme repertoire and promotes colonization.
items.abstract: Secreted mucins are the major component of the mucus layer that protects intestinal epithelial surfaces. Mucins are complex glycoproteins decorated with over 100 different O-glycans. Some bacteria degrade mucins, contributing to disruption of the mucus barrier and inflammation. However, the enzymatic pathways by which gut bacteria degrade colonic mucin O-glycans and the impact of this process on gut colonization are unknown. Here, we identified >100 genes that are expressed by the symbiont Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron during growth on different O-glycan substrates, revealing the effects of specific glycan structures on gene expression. The characterization of 33 Bacteroides glycoside hydrolase enzymes revealed the pathway for colonic O-glycan degradation, uncovering 13 collective enzymes sufficient for mucin degradation. In vivo competition experiments showed that multiple exo-acting enzymes targeting mucin capping structures are central to gut colonization. This repertoire of Bacteroides enzymes illuminates complex mucin degradation pathways and potential targets to inhibit bacterial mucin degradation.

items.title: UC Irvine's BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) Brain Procurement Program for the Center for Multiomic Human Brain Cell Atlas Project.
items.abstract: High-quality neurotypical postmortem human brain tissue is essential for constructing comprehensive human brain cell atlases, but it is difficult to obtain. Here, we describe the establishment of UC Irvine's Brain Procurement Program, a coordinated multi-institutional pipeline to collect and process neurotypical donor brains for multiomic mapping studies within the National Institute of Health (NIH) BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) consortium. Through partnerships with the Orange County (OC) coroner's office, UC Irvine's Willed Body Program, UC Irvine's Medical Center (UCIMC), and the Children's Hospital of Orange County, we have developed standardized workflows encompassing donor identification, postmortem brain recovery and processing, region-of-interest dissection, neurotypical donor selection, and data management. Our experience demonstrates the feasibility of a community-based, multi-institutional procurement framework while highlighting challenges in recruiting neurotypical donors and ensuring demographic representation reflective of Southern California. We further identify opportunities to strengthen outreach and donation pathways. This program provides a scalable model for advancing population-reflective, high-quality human brain cell atlas efforts.

items.title: The PELICANS Registry: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Extended Longitudinal Investigation of Clinical Outcomes-Adverse Events, Nonrecovery, and Survival.

sections.objective: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) disproportionately affects Black women, yet long-term outcome data in socially vulnerable, predominantly Black cohorts remain limited. The purpose of this study was to characterize long-term outcomes and baseline predictors of survival, major adverse events (MAEs), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery in a U.S. PPCM cohort.
sections.methods: This retrospective-prospective registry included 159 women with PPCM (1982-2024). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, MAEs, and LVEF recovery (≥50%). Multivariable and extended Cox models evaluated predictors, adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy.
sections.results: The cohort was 80.5% Black. Over a median 9.0-year follow-up (IQR: 3.4-15.5), 41 patients (25.8%) died and 64 (40.3%) had MAEs. Among 148 patients with echocardiographic follow-up, 69 (46.6%) had sustained LVEF recovery, though 23 (25.0% of initially recovered) declined to LVEF <50%. Independent mortality predictors included elevated creatinine (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.37-5.97), lower index LVEF (aHR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98), family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure (aHR: 3.27; 95% CI: 1.41-7.56), and non-O blood type (aHR: 2.36; 95% CI: 1.04-5.33), retaining significance after adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy (n = 62). Elevated creatinine increased MAE odds (adjusted OR: 7.09; 95% CI: 1.98-32.9), while higher LVEF, parity, and obesity reduced them. Baseline LV dilation (≥60 mm), Black race, older age, and family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure predicted lower LVEF recovery odds.
sections.conclusion: This long-term predominantly Black PPCM cohort had high mortality, low LVEF recovery, and frequent late relapse. These findings highlight the importance of baseline risk stratification and sustained echocardiographic surveillance to guide clinical decision-making.

items.title: Sub-second dopamine reinforcement shapes juvenile social play.
items.abstract: Juvenile social play is critical for neurodevelopment, yet the neural mechanisms organizing moment-to-moment interactions remain elusive. Using social behavior sequencing (Social-seq)-an occlusion-robust 3D pose estimation and unsupervised clustering pipeline-we found that nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine was tightly coupled to sub-second social syllables during naturalistic interactions. In wild-type juveniles, males exhibited a sharper dopaminergic contrast between proactive play and forced submission than females did, consistent with sex-divergent play strategies. In Shank3-deficient autism models, this process was fundamentally corrupted: proactive play-evoked dopamine responses were abolished in males and significantly sign-inverted in females, with male-specific enhancements during non-social behaviors, driving social play deficits. A multi-agent reinforcement learning model parameterized by disrupted, play-related dopaminergic reinforcement values recapitulated mutant phenotypes. Closed-loop optogenetic stimulation of ventral tegmental area (VTA)-NAc dopamine projections, time-locked to proactive play, restored reciprocal play in Shank3-deficient rats. Sub-second dopaminergic reinforcement thus orchestrates naturalistic social behavior, providing a behaviorally contingent interventional framework for neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks.
items.abstract: The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth's early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1-3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8-16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740-820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

items.title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses.
items.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) displays, originating from early optical see-through head-mounted systems1, have evolved towards lightweight glasses that seamlessly integrate digital information with the physical world2,3. However, their widespread adoption requires compact optical systems that enable bright, wide-field and comfortable viewing. Diffractive waveguides (WGs) offer a promising approach towards lightweight AR displays yet face inherent trade-offs among field of view (FoV), optical efficiency and eyebox size owing to limited degrees of freedom in light control. Here we show an all-day-wearable AR glass prototype based on spatially varying, interwoven metasurfaces that provide several grating vectors for multidirectional light control. The resulting dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide (meta-WG) achieves a 30° FoV and an 8 × 8-mm2 two-dimensional (2D) eyebox while maintaining an average luminance efficiency of 1,938 nits lm-1 (up to 4,225 nits lm-1) within a 1.5-mm-thick form factor. The prototype produces bright and stable virtual images under outdoor ambient illumination, demonstrating the compatibility of meta-WGs with practical wearable display requirements. By expanding the degrees of freedom for light routing beyond conventional diffractive WGs, our approach provides a scalable framework for balancing efficiency, viewing range and form factor, bringing high-performance AR glasses closer to practical consumer applications.

items.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart.
items.abstract: Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45-MCM-GINS) helicase1,2. Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability3-6. Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment4. In human cells, the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress7-10, but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG-PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

items.title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice.
items.abstract: Nuclei in early mammalian embryos undergo epigenetic reprogramming that enables the zygote to develop into a complete organism. Whereas changes in chromatin state during this critical transition period have been extensively studied1-3, changes in the nucleus that houses chromatin remain poorly understood. Here, using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation methods, we find that nuclei attain profound softness and plasticity during the two-cell embryonic stage in mice, facilitating major zygotic gene activation. The prominent nuclear deformability is attributable to the rapid clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope by the autophagy factor LC3. Nuclear stiffening by lamin B1 retention or its overloading results in incomplete activation of zygotic genes and impaired development. However, embryos that maintain nuclear deformability escape from this transcriptional interference. High-resolution microscopy and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization analyses revealed an accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the deformable nuclear envelope. An engineered molecular tether that stiffens the nuclei restricts these nuclear activities and suppresses expression of key zygotic gene activation genes. Together, our study identifies a distinct physical nuclear state that embryos acquire at the beginning of life that supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

items.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene1, and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats2-7, yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals' proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.
items.authors: de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz M

items.title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
items.abstract: Disconnects between in vitro and in vivo results in experimental biology have long been recognized as potential hurdles to understanding health and disease. A prototypical example of such a disconnect is the NLRP3 inflammasome, which mediates inflammation in diverse settings of disease and protective immunity1,2. Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro requires two signals: (1) priming by pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as bacterial lipopolysaccharides and (2) activation by molecules that disrupt cellular homeostasis1,3. By contrast, the NLRP3 inflammasome in vivo is activated by lipopolysaccharide alone. The mechanisms that underlie the difference between in vitro and in vivo activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome are undefined. Here we report that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness is a determinant of NLRP3 activities and that in vitro systems using physiological ECM stiffness enable one-signal in vivo-like NLRP3 activities to occur in human and mouse phagocytes. Physiological ECM stiffness induced expression of the transcription factor NRF2, which was found to be necessary for one-signal NLRP3 activation. Mechanistically, we identify Panx1 as an NRF2-regulated gene that promotes NLRP3 activity. Macrophages derived from the stiff matrix of the bone-osteoclasts-had reduced NRF2 levels and impaired NLRP3 activity. Moreover, alveolar macrophages from patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity. Finally, NRF2 was required for antitumour immunity induced by cancer vaccines consisting of NLRP3 agonistic adjuvants. These findings indicate that NRF2 may be a transcriptional checkpoint that controls NLRP3 inflammasome activity.

items.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics.
items.abstract: Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics-although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost-faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints1,2. Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability3. Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

items.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis.
items.abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1-3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4-7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

items.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines.
items.abstract: The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource1. However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs2,3. Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

items.title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL.
items.abstract: Eukaryotic genomes are exposed to numerous sources of DNA damage that impede replication. Only a decade ago, repriming by the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL was identified as a pathway that enables cells to tolerate DNA damage1-4.
