However, the molecular mechanism that underlies repriming remains poorly understood, and it is unclear how PRIMPOL is precisely targeted to stalled forks, where along single-stranded DNA PRIMPOL binds and how PRIMPOL is regulated to minimize error-prone DNA synthesis. Here, to dissect the molecular basis of repriming, we perform real-time single-molecule imaging in nuclear extracts that recapitulate genome maintenance. We directly visualize how stalled forks restart through repriming. We show that PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG). This facilitates primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis. At near-physiological concentrations, PRIMPOL reprimes leading strands in a CMG-dependent manner and polymerase ε extends those primers. This primary mode of repriming does not require DNA damage checkpoint signalling. PRIMPOL overexpression and checkpoint activation promote a secondary mode of repriming, whereby PRIMPOL restarts DNA synthesis far from CMG and polymerase δ extends those primers. Our data reveal a simple yet effective mechanism that directs PRIMPOL's activity to stalled forks awaiting restart, and suggest a strategy to inhibit the repriming pathway.

items.title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity.
items.abstract: Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS-STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

items.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia.
items.abstract: Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers1,2. However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples3, collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

items.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores.
items.abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm1,2. Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated3-13. Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG-FG and FG-importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations14 of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization4,5,7,9,15 and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

items.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis.
items.abstract: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1-5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal-immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

items.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA.
items.abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis1. IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function2,3, with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities4-8. Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health.

items.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer.
items.abstract: Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer1, in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP)2. Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain-domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR-p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a 'super-inhibitory' effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR-p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

items.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss.
items.abstract: TDP-43 nuclear depletion is a defining pathological feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia that induces widespread cryptic splicing defects in hundreds of transcripts1-8. Despite this, whether TDP-43 loss affects synaptic function has remained unclear. Here we show that TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact but suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication. Genetic correction of a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A was sufficient to rescue these deficits. We developed splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that correct UNC13A cryptic splicing in human cortical and spinal motor neurons and in a humanized mouse model. In human neurons this intervention restored spontaneous and evoked synaptic vesicle release, release probability at individual synapses and wider network synchrony. Together, this establishes UNC13A splice correction as a mechanistically defined and genetically validated therapeutic strategy relevant to roughly 97% of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and roughly 50% of patients with frontotemporal dementia with TDP-43 pathology.

items.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China.
items.abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1-10. Notably, even China's total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China's one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China's total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research.

items.title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti.
items.abstract: Extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1. Their effects on species' distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood2-9. Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Here we integrate new spatial data on severe drought10, including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58-61% to 69-72%. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26-43% to 55-58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1-15% to 25-35%. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69-72% to 84-85% across SSPs. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

items.title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2',3'-cNMP produced by insect effectors.
items.abstract: RNA-derived 2',3'-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1-3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2',3'-cNMPs; 2',3'-cAMP and 2',3'-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3'→5')-guanosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Exogenous application of 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling.

items.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts.
items.abstract: In 2025, a Lancet Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status1. Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2-3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2-8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3-7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7-31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6-10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64-1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14-1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the Lancet Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

items.title: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.

sections.objective: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial. 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.
sections.results: 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.
sections.conclusion: Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.
sections.other: Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023. The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.

items.title: Changes in pregabalin use and overdose after government interventions and media coverage: retrospective observational study.

sections.objective: To evaluate trends in pregabalin use and overdose in Australia and examine temporal relationships with media coverage (December 2018), prescribing and dispensing restrictions (April 2020), and boxed warnings (February 2021).
sections.methods: Retrospective observational study of dispensing and overdose data, with changepoint, interrupted time series, and latent class analysis.
sections.results: 227 864 people were dispensed 3 441 851 pregabalin prescriptions in the PBS 10% sample and 4871 pregabalin overdose calls were made to the Poisons Centre. Pregabalin use peaked in 2018 before plateauing and declining. Three breakpoints were found in dispensing data, with major decreases in level and slope: December 2018, May 2020, December 2021. The combined rate ratio for dispensing was 0.748 (95% confidence interval 0.700 to 0.800). Compared with the projected historical trend in the absence of interventions (counterfactual), approximately 118 390 (93 960 to 140 940) fewer pregabalin prescriptions were recorded nationally in December 2021, and an ongoing reduction of 0.7% (0.5% to 0.9%) was found each month. All breakpoints were associated with declines in overdose rates, with a combined rate ratio of 0.532 (95% CI 0.406 to 0.695). This reduction corresponded to approximately 41.3 (26.9 to 52.4) fewer pregabalin overdose calls in December 2021 and an ongoing reduction of 1.6% (1.0% to 2.3%) each month. Latent class analysis of 57 744 people dispensed pregabalin in the 12 months after the final breakpoint revealed four groups. The high risk group (7790, 13.5%) were more likely male, younger, dispensed more pregabalin, with shorter refill interval and high rates of opioids and benzodiazepine co-use (5120 (65.7%) and 2455 (31.5%), respectively).
sections.conclusion: Pregabalin use and overdose in Australia have declined in recent years. Major decreases in trend corresponded with media coverage (December 2018) and prescribing and dispensing restrictions (May 2020). The third breakpoint may be a delayed impact of boxed warnings (implemented February 2021). These findings suggest that regulatory and risk communication measures may contribute to reducing pregabalin related harm.
sections.other: Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data (PBS; 10% random sample of people with drug subsidies) and overdose calls (self-harm, recreational use, and misuse) reported to Australia's largest Poisons Centre (50% national sample), 2016-24. Population adjusted rates of dispensing and overdose, timing of breakpoints and rate ratios, proportion of people who use pregabalin at high risk of misuse.

items.title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C-H arylation of arenes.
items.abstract: Direct arylation of C-H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C-H bonds as reactive sites,2-4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5-12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C-H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C-H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C-H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C-H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

items.title: Trevogrumab (anti-GDF8) with or without garetosmab (anti-activin A) for prevention of muscle loss during semaglutide-induced weight reduction in people with obesity (COURAGE): a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.

sections.objective: Rapid weight loss, as induced by GLP-1 receptor agonists, is accompanied by pronounced muscle loss. GDF8 (myostatin) and activin A (ActA), acting via ActRIIA/B receptors, are negative regulators of muscle mass. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of antibodies blocking GDF8 (trevogrumab) and ActA (garetosmab) on semaglutide-induced weight and muscle loss.
sections.methods: COURAGE is a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial. This multicentre (60 sites), US-based trial enrolled participants aged 18-80 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). In part A, participants were treated for 26 weeks with semaglutide (titrated to 2·4 mg subcutaneously weekly) in addition to a randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) concomitant treatment: placebo, trevogrumab 200 mg, trevogrumab 400 mg, or trevogrumab 400 mg and garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Trevogrumab was administered subcutaneously weekly and garetosmab was administered intravenously every 4 weeks. Part A also included a subsequent semaglutide withdrawal period, at which point participants (randomly assigned at baseline 1:1 within each group) received either trevogrumab 400 mg or placebo for an additional 26 weeks. In part B, participants were treated with semaglutide for 52 weeks and randomly assigned (1:2:2) to concomitant treatment with placebo, trevogrumab 25 mg, or trevogrumab 75 mg. Groups were stratified according to sex, BMI (<35 kg/m2vs ≥35 kg/m2), and participation in an exploratory MRI substudy assessing thigh muscle volume. Study participants, the principal investigators, and study site personnel were masked to all randomisation assignments throughout the study. Primary endpoints were percent change in lean mass, fat mass, and bodyweight from baseline to week 26 (part A) or week 52 (part B). Efficacy and safety analyses were done in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of a study drug (efficacy, as randomly assigned; safety, as treated). COURAGE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299098, and is currently active, not recruiting.
sections.results: 975 participants were enrolled between June 21, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Mean age was 49·0 years (SD 13·2) and mean BMI was 36·7 kg/m2 (SD 5·0); 627 (64%) of 975 participants were female and 348 (36%) were male. In part A (n=605, of whom n=599 received at least one dose of study drug), a substantial decrease in lean mass was observed in the semaglutide plus placebo group at week 26 (-6·6% [95% CI -7·4 to -5·7]); the estimated treatment difference (ETD) versus semaglutide plus placebo was +3·1% (95% CI 1·9 to 4·3) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg, +2·7% (1·5 to 4·0) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg, and +4·5% (3·1 to 5·9) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg. In part B (n=376), lean mass percent change from baseline to week 52 for semaglutide plus placebo was -7·3% (-8·8 to -5·8); the ETD versus semaglutide plus placebo was +1·5% (-0·3 to 3·3) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 25 mg, and +3·1% (1·3 to 4·9) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 75 mg. Change from baseline in fat mass in part A was -15·6% (-17·4 to -13·9) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg group (-3·4% [-5·9 to -0·9]) and the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-11·7% [-14·4 to -9·0]) in part A. No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in fat mass compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Percent change in bodyweight in part A was -10·6 (-11·6 to -9·7) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant for the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-2·7 [-4·1 to -1·2]). No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in bodyweight compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Semaglutide plus trevogrumab (25 mg, 75 mg, 200 mg, or 400 mg) was generally well tolerated with a safety profile similar to semaglutide plus placebo; however, semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg had a high incidence of serious adverse events (14 [9%] of 149) and treatment discontinuations (48 [32%] of 149). Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most commonly reported, and they occurred with similar incidence across treatment groups. Muscle spasms occurred more frequently in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (61 [41%] of 149) compared with the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg or 400 mg groups (23 [8%] of 299) and semaglutide plus placebo groups (seven [5%] of 151). Most adverse events were mild to moderate in severity. Two deaths occurred during the study, both in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group; a causal association between treatment and these events was not identified.
sections.conclusion: This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health.

items.title: The blood-brain barrier imports diverse neuroprotective proteins through pathways impaired early in Alzheimer's disease models.
items.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) has been defined primarily by what it excludes, yet the scale and function of physiological blood-to-brain protein transport remain largely unknown. Using bioorthogonal proteomics, we find that the healthy BBB samples 191 plasma proteins and permits 92 into the brain parenchyma. Enriched for carrier and metabolic functions, these proteins home to distinct brain cell types, such as apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) to astrocytes and alpha-1 antitrypsin (SERPINA1) to microglia. This cell-type tropism relies on a BBB-parenchyma receptor hand-off: APOA1 crosses the BBB via SR-B1 and engages astrocytic ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1), a key Alzheimer's risk gene, driving cholesterol efflux that supports synapse integrity. Unlike LPS-induced nonspecific leakage, early-stage 5xFAD mice show selective BBB transport remodeling, with reduced APOA1 and increased SERPINA1 uptake. Hepatic APOA1 overexpression restores APOA1 in the 5xFAD brain, rescuing astrocytic, synaptic, and behavioral deficits. These findings recast the BBB as a selective interface that recruits neuroprotective circulatory proteins for brain health.

items.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma.

sections.objective: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety.
sections.results: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered.
sections.conclusion: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

items.title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials.
items.abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses and discrete length scales. Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes or repeating features1,2. In contrast, as network science has revealed, real-world and biological systems-from the Internet to the brain-derive their function from broad, multiscale variability in connectivity and link length3-6. Here we introduce scale-rich metamaterials, a design framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials, achieving orders-of-magnitude heterogeneity in ligament lengths, thicknesses and connectivity. Governed by only two parameters, scale-rich networks span orders of magnitude in structural features, overcoming previous constraints in metamaterial design. Translating these network models into physically realizable materials, we use simulations and experiments to show that scale-rich metamaterials exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems, including highly tunable elastic anisotropy, delocalized nonlinear deformation with high energy absorption, enhanced energy dissipation under dynamic loading and programmable elastic-wave control. This network-based framework establishes a minimal and universal model for engineering multifunctional materials whose mechanical behaviour emerges directly from scale diversity, and also opens avenues of enquiry for network science itself.

items.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87.
items.abstract: A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image1-4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features3,5-7, with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source8,9. Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

items.title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion.
items.abstract: Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal-iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation1-9. Here we show a kosmotropic anion-polar anion-nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water-Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc-I+-Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn-I2 and Al-I2 batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

items.title: Pragmatic Clinical indicators of Tuberculosis Transmission Risk: a Household Contact Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions.
sections.methods: We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates.
sections.results: Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk.
sections.conclusion: Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.
sections.other: Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB?

items.title: Associations between temperatures, extreme temperature events, and onset of acute exacerbations of COPD: a time-stratified case-crossover study in China.

sections.objective: Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups.
sections.methods: We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation.
sections.results: Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations.
sections.conclusion: Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden.
sections.other: Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible? ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

items.title: From surgical video to ophthalmic surgical intelligence: Evidence and translational challenges.
items.abstract: Microscope video provides a rich source of information for artificial intelligence in ophthalmic surgery, but recognition accuracy alone does not establish clinical benefit. We examine video-based workflow understanding, skill assessment, intraoperative assistance, and their potential integration with multimodal sensing and supervised robotic action, with emphasis on cataract and vitreoretinal surgery. Public datasets support retrospective recognition of phases, instruments, anatomy, and selected aspects of technical performance. Early live-use studies suggest possible workflow benefits, whereas patient-outcome evidence remains limited. Video foundation models extend technical capabilities, but porcine-eye navigation results remain surrogate evidence. Small human robotic studies establish feasibility for selected surgeon-controlled tasks, not safety equivalence, clinical superiority, or artificial intelligence autonomy. We propose an unvalidated framework comprising technical validity, external robustness, human factors and workflow, and clinical safety and benefit, assessed independently of the system's permitted level of action. These dimensions are neither a validated scale nor a compulsory sequence. A worked example of live cataract phase assistance illustrates how they identify use-specific evidence gaps without implying that greater autonomy confers greater clinical value. Translation requires independent validation, prospective human-factors evaluation, patient-relevant endpoints, data governance, and post-deployment monitoring. The central question is whether a defined system improves decisions, training, or outcomes under its intended conditions of use.

items.title: Characteristics and Outcomes of Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Undergoing Peripheral Vascular Interventions.

sections.objective: Atrial fibrillation (Afib) is a common dysrhythmia in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and can alter antithrombotic management. However, the characteristics and outcomes of patients with Afib undergoing peripheral vascular interventions (PVI) is not well characterized.
sections.methods: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry for PVI (2011-2024) was reviewed. The characteristics of patients with Afib were compared to patients without Afib. Perioperative and long-term outcomes were compared including reintervention, major amputation, mortality, and the composite outcome of MALE or mortality (MALE = reintervention or amputation), stratified by indication. Regression analysis was used to determine the independent association of Afib with outcomes.
sections.results: There were 118,095 patients analyzed (14% with Afib). Patients with Afib were older, more often male, white, and less likely to have history of smoking. Compared with patients without Afib, patients with Afib had higher comorbidities including cerebrovascular disease, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension (P<0.001). Preoperatively, Afib patients were more likely to be on anticoagulants (63% vs. 11%; P<0.001), whereas patients without Afib were more likely to be on antiplatelets (80% vs. 68%; P<0.001). Afib patients were more likely to be treated for CLTI (70% vs. 57%; P<0.001). Postoperatively, patients with Afib had significantly higher rates of 30-day mortality in both the claudication (1.0% vs. 0.3%; P<0.001) and CLTI subgroups (4.1% vs. 1.5%; P<0.001). Logistic regression showed that Afib was independently associated with higher odds of 30-day mortality in CLTI (odds ratio = 1.55 [95% CI, 1.33-1.80]; P<0.001). At 18-month follow-up, patients with Afib had significantly higher rates of mortality for claudication (16% vs. 7%; P<0.001, adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) = 1.28 [95% CI, 1.16-1.42]; P<0.001) and CLTI subgroups (40% vs. 22%; P<0.001, aHR = 1.28 [1.23-1.34]; P<0.001). Among patients with CLTI, the composite outcome (MALE or mortality) was significantly higher in patients with Afib (33% vs. 30%; P<0.001), with a trend toward higher risk after adjustment (HR = 1.05 [95% CI, 0.99-1.12]; P=0.094), whereas rates were similar in claudication (14% vs. 15%; P=0.78).
sections.conclusion: Patients with Afib undergoing PVI present with a higher burden of comorbidities, have different antithrombotic medications, and are more likely to be treated for CLTI compared to patients without Afib. Afib was independently associated with a significant increase in perioperative and long-term mortality but did not seem to be associated with limb outcomes.

items.title: Early prediction of surgical site complications after vascular groin incision using postoperative drainage kinetics: A retrospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Groin incisions in vascular surgery are associated with a considerable incidence of postoperative surgical site complications (SSCs), with lymphatic complications such as lymphorrhea and lymphocele representing a frequent and clinically relevant source of morbidity. Previous studies have identified postoperative drainage volume as a potential surrogate marker for impaired lymphatic healing and subsequent wound complications. Based on these observations, researchers have proposed standardized drainage management strategies to help identify high-risk patients early and guide timely intervention. This study retrospectively evaluates postoperative outcomes after implementing this strategy.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective cohort analysis included 106 patients with 114 vertical groin incisions undergoing open vascular procedures requiring femoral exposure between June 2023 and June 2024. We defined SSCs according to a previously published classification. We defined the groin incision as the unit of analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of clinically relevant SSCs (grades 2-4). Secondary outcomes included drainage characteristics, drain removal timing, lymphatic interventions, and risk factors for lymphatic complications.
sections.results: Postoperative drainage volumes were significantly associated with clinically relevant surgical site complications (SSC grade 2-4). Drainage on POD 1 was not significantly associated with complications. Higher drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards were significantly associated with complications, with increasing effect sizes over time (POD 2: OR 1.048, p = 0.022; POD 3: OR 1.047, p = 0.023; POD 4: OR 1.178, p < 0.001). Cumulative drainage up to POD 4 demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (OR 1.024, p = 0.0006; c = 0.831). Overall, 43.0% of groin incisions developed clinically relevant SSC.
sections.conclusion: Postoperative drainage kinetics enable early identification of patients at risk for clinically relevant lymphatic complications after vascular groin surgery. While drainage of POD 1 is not predictive, drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards allow reliable risk stratification with progressively increasing predictive accuracy. POD 2 drainage output is a clinically relevant predictor of subsequent lymphatic complications. A POD2 drainage output ≥80 mL/24 h may support early identification of high-risk patients and facilitate timely interdisciplinary planning of targeted lymphatic interventions.

items.title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.

sections.objective: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis.
sections.methods: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed.
sections.results: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies.
sections.conclusion: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

items.title: Success Rate and Factors Predictive of Redo Endothermal Ablation of Anterior Saphenous Veins (ASV).

sections.objective: Endothermal ablation (ETA), including endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), is commonly used to treat anterior saphenous vein (ASV) insufficiency, previously termed the anterior accessory saphenous vein (AASV). Although less prevalent than great saphenous vein (GSV) reflux, ASV incompetence represents a significant and often under-recognized cause of chronic venous disease. This study evaluates the success of redo ASV ablation and identifies factors associated with recanalization.
sections.methods: A retrospective review was conducted of 16,506 ETA procedures performed in 4,871 patients between 2012 and 2022, which was due to changes in protocol and different device usage in the practice. Of these, 763 ASV ablations were performed in 542 patients with chronic venous insufficiency (CVI). Postoperative duplex ultrasound surveillance was conducted 3-7 days following ablation, every 3-6 months during the first year, and every 6-12 months thereafter. Redo ablation was defined as duplex-confirmed recurrent reflux in a previously treated ASV associated with persistent or recurrent symptoms. Patients were followed at 3-month intervals during the first postoperative year and semiannually thereafter. Redo ablations were performed in patients with symptomatic ASV reflux involving ≥10 cm of vein length.
sections.results: A total of 763 ASV ablation procedures were analyzed, including 552 performed in women and 211 in men; 447 involved the left leg and 316 the right. The cohort was 5% Asian (n = 27), 24% Black (n = 129), 25% Hispanic (n = 138), and 46% White (n = 470). Redo ablation procedures occurred in 29 cases, including 1 Asian, 3 Black, 3 Hispanic, and 22 White patients. Among redo cases, mean age was 63.0 ± 14.7 years, mean BMI was 33.9 ± 9.2 kg/m2, and mean follow-up was 24.5 ± 15.9 months. CEAP classifications for the overall cohort were C2 (n = 26), C3 (n = 276), C4 (n = 320), C5 (n = 14), and C6 (n = 98). EVLA was performed in 316 procedures and RFA in 447. The technical success rate of the index ablation was 92.9% (709/763), compared with 96.6% (28/29) for redo ablations. Older age was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of requiring redo ASV ablation (p = 0.003). No significant associations were observed for BMI, CEAP class, sex, laterality, or ablation modality.
sections.conclusion: Redo ASV ablation is safe and effective, achieving outcomes comparable to primary procedures. These findings underscore the importance of recognizing ASV insufficiency as a major component of CVD and support its appropriate treatment when clinically indicated.

items.title: Acute Zonal Occult Outer Retinopathy: Reappraising a Historical Clinical Concept in the Era of Multimodal Imaging.
items.abstract: Acute zonal occult outer retinopathy (AZOOR) and the broader "AZOOR complex" have historically encompassed several disorders sharing acute visual symptoms and outer retinal dysfunction. Advances in multimodal imaging have revealed structural abnormalities in many of these presentations, challenging the original concept of an "occult" retinopathy without a visible anatomical correlate. We therefore revisit these concepts in light of modern imaging and current understanding of outer retinal disease. A systematic reassessment of 207 eligible published cases showed that 188 (90.8%) could be assigned a more specific contemporary diagnostic category based on the information available in the original reports. The most frequent assignments were multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS), acute outer retinopathy (AOR), and multizonal outer retinopathy and retinal pigment epitheliopathy (MORR). These findings do not establish that the original diagnoses were incorrect or that each contemporary diagnosis represents a biologically independent disease, but show that many presentations historically grouped under AZOOR can now be characterized more specifically. We review the clinical features, multimodal imaging findings, natural history, and management of the principal retinal entities identified through this reassessment. We also examine inherited, toxic, autoimmune, paraneoplastic, post-infectious, and other disorders that may produce similar retinal appearances or provide the underlying clinical or etiological setting for these presentations. Rather than proposing a new disease classification, we suggest a pattern-based diagnostic approach in which OCT and fundus autofluorescence form the core imaging assessment, with additional imaging modalities selected according to the clinical presentation and differential diagnosis. Imaging is used to characterize the predominant pattern and anatomical level of retinal injury and, when possible, to identify a more specific retinal diagnosis; clinical history, systemic evaluation, laboratory testing, electrophysiology, and genetic testing can then guide further investigation of its etiological setting or identify a specific alternative diagnosis. This approach allows patients presenting within the broad clinical spectrum historically associated with AZOOR to be characterized at the most specific level supported by contemporary imaging, while recognizing that the biological relationships among these retinal entities remain incompletely understood.

items.title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.

sections.objective: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints.
sections.methods: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively.
sections.results: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%).
sections.conclusion: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.

items.title: Metabolic Unloading: How SGLT2i Recalibrate Cell Energetics to Slow CKD Progression.
items.abstract: Kidney outcome trials demonstrate that sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors consistently slow chronic kidney disease progression; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, as benefits extend beyond glycemic control and hemodynamic effects across diabetic and non-diabetic chronic kidney disease. This review advances a unifying framework in which metabolic unloading of the proximal tubule contributes to renoprotection. The metabolic burden of solute reabsorption places the proximal tubule at the center of renal energetics, predisposing it to hypoxia, mitochondrial stress, and maladaptive injury responses. We synthesize evidence that these agents reduce adenosine triphosphate-dependent transport workload, oxygen consumption and may also reduce megalin-dependent endocytosis, with downstream effects on mitochondrial efficiency, redox balance, and autophagy/mitophagy supported by emerging preclinical data. By mitigating energetic stress, these agents divert tubular cell fate away from maladaptive hypertrophy and fibrosis toward adaptive repair. This framework integrates spatial cortex-medulla vulnerability, reconciles early hemodynamic changes with durable slowing of estimated glomerular filtration rate decline, and explores disease-agnostic benefit. We discuss translational implications including early initiation, identification of high workload phenotypes (hyperfiltration, recovery after acute kidney injury), and deployment of energetics associated biomarkers such as ketones, oxidative stress profiles, and estimated glomerular filtration rate slope. This review positions cellular energetics as an important upstream constraint shaping kidney disease progression, offering a foundation for nephroprotective strategies.

items.title: Scarring Alopecias Part 1: Diagnosis.
items.abstract: Primary cicatricial alopecias (PCAs) represent a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by irreversible destruction of hair follicles that are replaced with fibrotic tissue. These conditions typically result in irreversible hair loss and are associated with a significant psychological burden and quality of life impact. The pathophysiology involves immune privilege collapse, follicular stem cell destruction, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition leading to fibrosis. Diagnostic challenges persist due to overlapping phenotypes and nonspecific end-stage scarring. This two-part CME article presents updates to current classification systems based on predominant immune infiltrate patterns (lymphocytic, neutrophilic, mixed, nonspecific) to enhance diagnostic precision and guide therapeutic decisions. High-yield entities, including lichen planopilaris, collagen vascular diseases, frontal fibrosing alopecia, central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia, folliculitis decalvans, and dissecting cellulitis, are emphasized. Here, we focus on contemporary classification, pathophysiology, clinical recognition, biopsy techniques, trichoscopy, and the emerging role of digital pathology in PCA diagnosis.

items.title: Glial progenitor-like state is preferentially co-opted in glioblastoma and sustained by POU3F3.
items.abstract: Oncofetal reprogramming in glioblastoma (GBM) relies on the co-option of still poorly defined pathways that are transiently active during brain development, thereby exposing therapeutically actionable vulnerabilities. To better characterize GBM biology in the context of neurodevelopment, we create an expanded human spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset that resolves both gliogenic and neurogenic lineage fate and assess oncofetal reprogramming at the tumor core and infiltrative margin in both primary and recurrent disease. Analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of a glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like state, which is most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPCs, across tumor regions and in recurrence. We uncover EGFR and the long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) NRXN1-DT as co-opted gIPC-specific markers, demonstrate NRXN1-DT's clinical utility in GBM diagnostics, and prioritize POU3F3 as a gIPC-like oncofetal driver, confirming its regulatory role in NRXN1-DT enhancer activity, EGFR expression, and maintenance of GBM stem/progenitor-like properties. This study lays the groundwork for future investigations into targeting POU3F3 and other co-opted gliogenic drivers as GBM therapeutics.

items.title: Antisense oligonucleotide silencing rescues neurodevelopmental deficits in AMPA receptor gain-of-function mice.
items.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission and are essential for neuronal development and brain function. We investigated the role of a recurrent AMPAR GluA1 variant (GRIA1 p.A636T) identified in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). Using a Gria1-A636T knock-in mouse model, we show that this variant is sufficient to produce core ASD/ID-like behaviors and cause selective hippocampal vulnerability characterized by progressive dendritic atrophy and neuronal loss. Despite a reduction in GluA1-containing complexes, synaptic AMPARs exhibit hyperexcitability and fail to transition from calcium-permeable to calcium-impermeable AMPARs during development, resulting in persistent excitotoxicity. To explore potential therapeutic interventions, we developed an allele-specific antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) to selectively silence the mutant transcript. A single neonatal ASO dose prevents hippocampal pathology and rescues behavioral deficits. These findings define a mechanism of developmental excitotoxicity driven by a GRIA1 gain-of-function channelopathy and support RNA-targeted precision therapy for AMPAR-related neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Slow-timescale regulation of dopamine release governs recovery of a motivational drive over days.
items.abstract: The rise and fall of a motivational state can unfold over many days. We used mouse mating behavior to model how the brain orchestrates such slow-timescale changes in motivation. Male mice become sexually satiated after successful matings, and their motivation to mate recovers over a week. Using deep-brain fluorescence-lifetime imaging in the medial preoptic area (MPOA), we found that tonic dopamine transmission-which regulates mating drive-also declined after mating and gradually re-emerged across several days. Two mechanisms regulated dopamine transmission. First, successful mating transiently reduced the tonic firing of hypothalamic dopamine-releasing neurons, thereby inhibiting dopamine release and mating behavior for 1 to 2 days. Second, these neurons' ability to produce and release dopamine dropped after mating and recovered over the following week, paralleling the recovery of mating drive. Therefore, changes in neuronal firing rate and neurotransmitter composition cooperate to control the early and late phases of motivational dynamics, respectively.

items.title: Dissociable cerebellar pathways for reach correction and learning.
items.abstract: Sensory feedback can trigger rapid motor corrections, but how self-generated movement errors are corrected and influence subsequent behavior remains less clear. Here, we found that corrective submovements (CSMs), structured, feedback-driven adjustments, occurred either spontaneously or in response to neural perturbations during mouse reaching. Corrections were modestly encoded in the cerebellar anterior interposed nucleus (IntA) along with non-corrective reach kinematic correlates. Closed-loop perturbations directed to red nucleus-projecting neurons were readily compensated for with corrective movements and led to learned shifts in the timing of future submovements, while perturbations to IntA more broadly were not compensated for and produced no learning. Thus, subsets of IntA outputs differentially permit or corrupt accurate corrections and subsequent learning, respectively.

items.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non-Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.
keywords: United States Department of Veterans Affairs

items.title: PKA signaling controls ILC3 homeostasis and IL-23-mediated inflammation in the gut.
items.abstract: Group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) are tissue-protective lymphocytes that are enriched in the healthy gut and depleted in gastrointestinal disorders. Here we created a single-cell atlas to define how ILC3s respond to distinct stimuli, observing that prostaglandin engages protein kinase A (PKA) to upregulate tissue-protective factors. In contrast, the canonical activator interleukin-23 (IL-23) decreased negative regulators of PKA, including PRKAR1A. Lineage-specific Prkar1a deletion reduced ILC3s and increased susceptibility to enteric infection in mice. PRKAR1A was not required in early life but continuously preserved ILC3 homeostasis in adults by restraining PKA activity. Overproduction of IL-23 was sufficient to reduce PRKAR1A in ILC3s and increase PKA signaling that provoked gut inflammation. Finally, ILC3s from the healthy human intestine expressed PRKAR1A, which was downregulated by IL-23 or in inflammatory bowel disease. These results demonstrate that regulated PKA signaling is essential for tissue-protective ILC3s, while IL-23 drives aberrant PKA signaling to elicit intestinal inflammation.

items.title: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity.
items.abstract: Germline pathogenic BRCA1 variants predispose women to breast and ovarian cancer. Despite accumulation of functional evidence, over half of reported single-nucleotide variants in BRCA1 lack a definitive clinical interpretation. Furthermore, the consistency of variant effects across cell types remains largely unexplored. Here we performed saturation genome editing (SGE) of BRCA1 in HAP1 cells to score 4,113 previously unassayed variants. Additionally, we developed an SGE assay in human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs), allowing comparison of effects across cell lines, drug treatments and genetic backgrounds. We identified 538 variants impacting gene function through distinct mechanisms. HAP1 function scores discriminate between known pathogenic and benign variants with near-perfect accuracy. Intriguingly, however, nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants scored neutrally in HMECs. We show that discordantly scored variants are hypomorphic and confer intermediate cancer risk. Overall, this work demonstrates how performing SGE across cell models improves the functional interpretation of rare variants.

items.title: Comparative efficacy and tolerability of pharmacological interventions for the acute treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder across the lifespan: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Pharmacological treatment is recommended for obsessive-compulsive disorder. Several options are available, yet little is known on comparative effects of individual medications. We aimed to elucidate the efficacy and tolerability of pharmacotherapy for people with obsessive-compulsive disorder, across the lifespan.
sections.methods: We did a systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing short-term pharmacological interventions for obsessive-compulsive disorder. We searched multiple databases, including MEDLINE, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, for literature on licensed or recommended pharmacological treatments for obsessive-compulsive disorder, without age restrictions, from database inception up to March 11, 2026. We included double-blind, randomised controlled trials with outcomes between 8 and 16 weeks. Two reviewers independently and in duplicate extracted outcomes, with a quality check done by a third reviewer. Primary outcomes were efficacy, defined as change from baseline score, and tolerability, defined as the proportion of participants discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. Separately for children and adolescents (aged 0-17 years) and adults (aged ≥18 years), we calculated standardised mean differences (SMDs) and odds ratios (ORs) with random-effects pairwise and network meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework. People with lived experience of obsessive-compulsive disorder were involved in the entire review process, including protocol development, writing, and interpretation of the findings. The study was preregistered in Open Science Framework (identifier 4V3GS).
sections.results: We included 52 randomised controlled trials with 7316 participants. Nine trials were included for children and adolescents (N=822; median age 12·5 years [IQR 11·6-13·2]; 352 [55%] male and 285 [45%] female among 637 participants with reported sex distribution). 43 trials were included for adults (N=6494; median age 36·4 years [35·0-37·9]; 3105 [49%] male and 3200 [51%] female among 6305 participants with reported sex distribution). Data on ethnicity were reported in 15 (29%) of 52 randomised controlled trials, using inconsistent definitions. In children and adolescents, clomipramine was more efficacious than placebo (SMD -1·19, 95% CI -1·73 to -0·64, CINeMA low), as were sertraline (-0·52, -0·80 to -0·02, low), fluoxetine (-0·43, -0·76 to -0·10, low), and fluvoxamine (-0·39, -0·71 to -0·07, low). Clomipramine was more efficacious than fluoxetine (SMD -0·75, 95% CI -1·39 to -0·11; very low), fluvoxamine (-0·79, -1·43 to -0·16; very low), paroxetine (-0·87, -1·51 to -0·22; very low), and sertraline (-0·87, -1·51 to -0·22; very low). Only sertraline was less tolerable than placebo (OR 4·51, 95% CI 1·36 to 14·96; low). In adults, clomipramine (SMD -0·71, 95% CI -0·88 to -0·54; high), fluvoxamine (-0·63, -0·83 to -0·43; high), paroxetine (-0·51, -0·73 to -0·29; moderate), sertraline (-0·49, -0·70 to -0·28; moderate), escitalopram (-0·43, -0·85 to -0·02; moderate), and fluoxetine (-0·37, -0·6 to -0·08; moderate) were more efficacious than placebo, and clomipramine was more efficacious than fluoxetine (-0·34, -0·65 to -0·04; low). Clomipramine (OR 4·65, 95% CI 3·27 to 6·60; moderate), fluvoxamine (2·73, 1·77 to 4·20; moderate), fluoxetine (2·52, 1·27 to 4·98; moderate), sertraline (2·23, 1·49 to 3·34; moderate), and paroxetine (1·99, 1·36 to 2·93; moderate) were less tolerable than placebo. Clomipramine was less tolerable than all active comparators (OR range 1·70 to 3·50; moderate) except fluoxetine (moderate) and venlafaxine (low).
