sections.conclusion: Clomipramine showed the largest estimated efficacy for obsessive-compulsive disorder but had a lower tolerability than SSRIs. The evidence of its superiority over individual SSRIs was more pronounced in children and adolescents. Our findings suggest that the trade-off between efficacy and tolerability should be discussed within an individualised, shared, decision-making framework.

items.title: Longitudinal change in FEV1 in adults with cystic fibrosis treated with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor in France: a prospective observational study.

sections.objective: Without cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators, cystic fibrosis is associated with an accelerated decline in percent predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of approximately 1·5% per year. Although treatment with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) initially increases ppFEV1, little is known about its subsequent effect on ppFEV1 decline. Recent analyses of the extension phases of the phase 3 ETI pivotal studies found no evidence of ppFEV1 decline over 4 years in patients aged 12 years and older who were treated with ETI. The objective of this study was to examine the decline in ppFEV1 in a large, real-world cohort of adults with cystic fibrosis.
sections.methods: Data from adults (aged ≥18 years) with cystic fibrosis and at least one F508del CFTR variant who initiated treatment with ETI between Dec 24, 2019, and Dec 23, 2023, at 31 cystic fibrosis centres included in the French prospective national observational ETI study in adults were analysed over 3 years. Eligible participants were those with at least three measures of ppFEV1 taken within 3 months following ETI initiation and the end of follow-up. The reference ppFEV1 was the highest ppFEV1 reached during the first 3 months of ETI treatment, after which subsequent decline in ppFEV1 was analysed by use of a linear mixed-effects model with random effects to estimate each participant's variation from the population mean.
sections.results: Data from 2321 adults with cystic fibrosis were included in this analysis. 1262 (54·4%) participants were male and 1059 (45·6%) were female. Median age was 29·2 years (IQR 23·1-36·7) and the pre-ETI initiation ppFEV1 was 59·7% (IQR 39·8-79·1). Within the first 3 months following ETI initiation, ppFEV1 increased by a median of 14·5 percentage points (IQR 7·9-22·7). The subsequent mean decline in ppFEV1 was 0·70% (95% CI 0·57-0·83) per year. Importantly, the decline in ppFEV1 was heterogeneous, with 1583 (68·2%) of 2321 participants showing no or limited decline (less than or equal to 1·5% per year). The remaining 738 (31·8%) participants showed a decline of greater than 1·5% per year, with 342 (46·3%) of these participants having a decline of greater than 3·0% per year. In multivariable analyses, the decline in ppFEV1 was greater in participants with a higher ppFEV1 at 3 months after ETI initiation. Treatment with oral azithromycin at 1 year after ETI initiation was associated with a lower risk of having a decline greater than 1·5% per year (relative risk 0·78 [95% CI 0·68-0·90]; p <0·01), as was treatment with inhaled antibiotics (0·81 [0·70-0·94]; p <0·01).
sections.conclusion: These results suggest that approximately a third of adults with cystic fibrosis who are treated with ETI had a persistent decline in ppFEV1. These data emphasise the importance of regular ppFEV1 monitoring and highlight the need to improve current therapeutic strategies to prevent ppFEV1 decline. Proposed strategies could include use of newer CFTR modulators to restore CFTR function more effectively, as well as mucoactive, anti-infective, and anti-inflammatory therapies.

items.title: Safety and efficacy of weekly pemvidutide versus placebo for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (IMPACT): 48-week results from a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, phase 2b study.

sections.objective: Glucagon-GLP-1 dual receptor agonists have shown promise in treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The aim of the IMPACT trial was to assess the effects of one such agent, pemvidutide, in patients with MASH and stage F2 or F3 fibrosis. We previously reported the 24-week primary endpoints of MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement. Here we report the secondary endpoints following 48 weeks of treatment.
sections.methods: IMPACT was a 48-week, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 2b trial in patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH and fibrosis stage F2 or F3. Patients from 83 sites, including academic and community hospitals and private clinical research clinics, in the USA and Australia were randomly assigned (1:2:2) using an interactive web response system to receive once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide (1·2 mg or 1·8 mg), administered without dose titration, or placebo. Patients, investigators, the funder, and all other staff, were masked to treatment assignments throughout the study. The dual primary endpoints of MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis or at least one stage liver fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH were assessed at week 24. Liver biopsies were not collected at week 48, and only secondary endpoints were assessed at this timepoint. All analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population consisting of all randomly assigned patients. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05989711) and is complete.
sections.results: From July 27, 2023, to Nov 21, 2025, 1557 patients were screened and 212 patients were randomly assigned to pemvidutide 1·2 mg (n=41), pemvidutide 1·8 mg (n=85), or placebo (n=86). Mean age was 53·4 years (SD 12·4), mean BMI was 38·7 kg/m2 (7·8), 123 (58%) patients were female, 89 (42%) were male, and 90 (42%) had type 2 diabetes. At week 48, least-squares mean relative changes in liver fat content were -45·2% (95% CI -56·0 to -34·5; difference from placebo -37·1 percentage points [95% CI -50·6 to -23·5]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -54·7% (-62·3 to -47·1; difference from placebo -46·5 percentage points [-57·7 to -35·3]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and -8·2% (-16·5 to 0·2) in the placebo group. The least-squares mean absolute change in corrected T1 relaxation time was -124·2 ms (95% CI -157·1 to -91·4; difference from placebo -103·8 [95% CI -143·9 to -63·6]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -139·5 ms (-161·7 to -117·3; difference from placebo -119·0 [-151·2 to -86·9]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and -20·5 ms (-44·5 to 3·6) in the placebo group. Least-squares mean changes in alanine aminotransferase were -37·8 IU/L (95% CI -44·5 to -31·1; difference from placebo -27·5 [95% CI -35·8 to -19·2]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group and -37·4 IU/L (-42·1 to -32·7; difference from placebo -27·1 [-33·9 to -20·3]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group versus -10·3 IU/L (-15·2 to -5·4) for the placebo group. Least-squares mean changes in enhanced liver fibrosis score were -0·49 (95% CI -0·71 to -0·28; difference from placebo -0·65 [95 % CI -0·92 to -0·38]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -0·58 (-0·74 to -0·43; difference from placebo -0·74 [-0·97 to -0·52]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and 0·16 (-0·01 to 0·32) for the placebo group. The most frequent pemvidutide-related adverse events were nausea (occurring in nine [22%] of 41 patients in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 35 [41%] of 85 patients in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and 15 [17%] of 86 patients in the placebo group), diarrhoea (five [12%] in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 19 [22%] in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and seven [8%] in the placebo group), and constipation (five [12%] in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 15 [18%] in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and ten [12%] in the placebo group). No severe or serious adverse events were defined as study medication related. Discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in no patients in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, one (1%) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and three (3%) in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: In patients with MASH, 48 weeks of pemvidutide treatment led to significant reductions in non-invasive tests of MASH inflammation and fibrosis, suggesting continued improvement in liver health. These data warrant the continued investigation of pemvidutide in a phase 3 trial.

items.title: Dual inhibition of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling through BIG2 ameliorates osteoarthritis in mouse and primate models.
items.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA), a leading cause of disability, is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic dysregulation in chondrocytes. TNF-α and IL-1β are key inflammatory drivers in OA pathogenesis, but clinical trials targeting them individually have been unsuccessful, highlighting the potential need for dual-targeting strategies. By screening a US Food and Drug Administration-approved drug library, we identified dabigatran, a thrombin inhibitor, as a potent dual suppressor of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling that restored chondrocyte metabolism. In preclinical OA models, including both mice and cynomolgus macaques, dabigatran attenuated cartilage degeneration, alleviated pain, and improved joint function. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms, we performed biochemical copurification coupled with mass spectrometry, identifying brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 2 (BIG2) as a previously unknown dabigatran-binding target. Mechanistically, dabigatran binds to BIG2, promoting BIG2-dependent TNFR1 release to dampen TNF-α signaling while enhancing BIG2-mediated IL-1R1 degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway to limit IL-1β effects. These findings establish BIG2-mediated receptor trafficking and membrane dynamics as a regulatory node that concurrently inhibits TNF-α and IL-1β signaling, suggesting this pathway as a potential therapeutic strategy for OA.

items.title: Helminth infections: from genomic discovery to public health interventions.
items.abstract: Helminths infect more than a billion people worldwide and cause substantial chronic morbidity, impaired physical and cognitive development in children, and reduced wellbeing and economic productivity, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Preventive chemotherapy, sanitation, vector control, and integrated programmes have substantially reduced infection intensity and morbidity in many settings, although sustaining these gains and advancing towards elimination require complementary tools. Advances in genomics, multiomics, and computational biology have added a complementary, data-rich dimension to established parasitology, supporting systematic target identification, improved molecular diagnostics, and new insights into transmission and drug response. In this Review, we examine how these approaches are reshaping the study of helminth infections and the implications of these approaches for diagnosis, treatment, and control. Translating these technological and scientific advances into effective interventions still requires representative data, experimental and field validation, accessible infrastructure, trained personnel, and sustainable implementation, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Ultimately, integrating genomic and molecular discoveries with clinical, epidemiological, and public health strategies within a One Health framework will be central to achieving measurable and sustained improvements in helminth control.

items.title: Consensus on the definition, components, and grading of composite postoperative pulmonary complication outcomes (PrECiSIOn): insights from an international Delphi expert panel.
items.abstract: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after surgery and contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality, and health-care burden, and are frequently used as endpoints in clinical studies. However, absence of standardised definitions and heterogeneity in component selection limit comparability across studies and might bias estimates of treatment effects. The Postoperative Pulmonary Complications-Evaluation for Consensus on Standardised Outcomes (PrECiSIOn) study was an international, mixed-method consensus study using a Delphi process to establish a standardised definition of PPCs, determine severity-based ranking of individual components, and define approaches for their assessment. A multidisciplinary panel of experts in PPCs was recruited and candidate PPC components were identified through a focused literature review, structured into domains, and evaluated across iterative Delphi rounds using a seven-point Likert scale, with consensus predefined as ≥75% agreement. Patient and patient care representative perspectives were incorporated through interviews and surveys, and panellists assigned severity weights to components reaching consensus. Input from 44 panellists and five patients and patient representatives informed the prioritisation of clinically meaningful outcomes. Consensus was achieved on a standardised PPC construct comprising components grouped into four domains: symptoms, diagnoses, therapies, and outcomes. Panellists supported the use of routinely collected clinical data and a standardised in-hospital monitoring approach but did not reach consensus on the optimal follow-up period or need for post-discharge surveillance. Severity-based rank ordering enabled hierarchical organisation of PPC components according to their clinical importance, supporting the development of ordinal composite outcomes that account for differences in severity between individual complications. This international consensus-based framework provides a standardised definition of PPCs incorporating severity-based rank ordering, addresses important limitations of existing composite outcomes, and might facilitate more consistent and clinically meaningful evaluation of perioperative interventions. Further work should focus on external validation, implementation in clinical trial analyses, and assessment of applicability across diverse patient populations and health-care settings.

items.title: A blended digital parenting intervention for the prevention of sexual violence, exploitative sex, and maltreatment of children at scale in Tanzania: a cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

sections.objective: Childhood sexual, physical, and verbal violence are global public health priorities, affecting 1 billion children each year. ParentApp integrates sexual violence prevention into WHO-UNICEF's open-access Parenting for Lifelong Health programme, using innovative blended digital delivery. We aimed to test the efficacy of ParentApp in preventing sexual violence and maltreatment against adolescent-aged children and improving preventive mechanisms such as family mental health and adolescent-caregiver relationships.
sections.methods: This cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in 80 Tanzanian sub-wards. Participants were primary caregivers aged 18 years and older and their adolescents (aged 10-17 years). Sub-wards were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either ParentApp (intervention group) or a control WASHApp programme. Clusters were randomly assigned in blocks of six, stratified by urban versus rural location. Statisticians carrying out randomisation and data analysts were masked; it was not possible to mask participants or researchers. Intervention groups received a low-cost Android phone installed with ParentApp, a 12-module offline-first app, with one in-person orientation session and remote support via WhatsApp group chats, at a delivery cost of US$6 per family at scale, or $10 with 20% smartphone provision. Control groups received a low-cost Android phone installed with WASHApp, a 12-module offline-first app for water, sanitation, and hygiene, with one in-person orientation session. The primary outcomes were adolescent sexual violence victimisation and maltreatment and high-risk situations for sexual violence, assessed in all participants irrespective of uptake and engagement at 5 months and 18 months post-baseline. The trial was registered on March 14, 2023, with OSF (https://osf.io/t9fxz) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 11 and Oct 9, 2023, 2692 caregiver-adolescent dyads were screened for study eligibility; 2396 adolescents (1217 [50·8%] female and 1179 [49·2%] male) and 2396 caregivers (1795 [74·9%] female and 601 [25·1%] male) were recruited. 2145 (89·5%) adolescents and 2252 (94·0%) caregivers were retained in the study and included in analyses at 18 months. Adolescent girls in ParentApp clusters had a substantial reduction in past-month sexual violence victimisation compared with those in control clusters (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0·43 [95% CI 0·21-0·86]; p=0·018), with no effect for boys (1·21 [0·59-2·43]; p=0·60). Past-month maltreatment (physical abuse, verbal abuse, and neglect) was lower in ParentApp clusters than in control clusters (adolescent report IRR 0·92 [0·88-0·96]; p<0·0001, caregiver report 0·87 [0·82-0·92]; p<0·0001). Past-month exposure to high-risk situations for sexual violence was lower in ParentApp clusters than in control clusters (adolescent girls IRR 0·87 [0·77-0·97]; p=0·012, adolescent boys 0·85 [0·79-0·91]; p<0·0001, caregiver report 0·81 [0·75-0·88]; p<0·0001). There were no reported adverse events.
sections.conclusion: A low-cost blended digital parenting programme in countries such as Tanzania could simultaneously reduce childhood sexual violence (for girls) and maltreatment and sexual violence risk situations (for girls and boys).

items.title: Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

items.title: COP1 is a temperature-responsive switch in Arabidopsis.
items.abstract: Temperature is molecular motion, but how living systems sense this is poorly understood. Many responses in plants integrate light and temperature signals, for example, via light receptors and the circadian clock. CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1 (COP1) regulates light signaling and is necessary for responding to temperature. We show that COP1 acts as a temperature-dependent switch, becoming activated by a warm temperature-induced conformational change. An intramolecular Val-Pro (VP) motif binds to the active site of COP1 at low temperatures, preventing substrate docking. At warmer temperatures, the VP motif becomes detached, enabling client proteins to bind and be degraded. This discovery explains how plants are able to obtain a precise readout of temperature within a given climate range. Altering the binding of the VP motif is sufficient to adjust the temperature range within which the plant responds. This helps us understand how plants are able to adapt to different climates.

items.title: Nicotianamine-driven nickel transport to sink organs underpins maize productivity.
items.abstract: Nickel (Ni), the last essential trace element identified in plants, has long been enigmatic regarding the genetic basis underlying its homeostasis and its agricultural significance. Using genome-wide association analysis, we identified ZmNAET1 as a key transporter controlling Ni allocation to seeds. Mechanistically, ZmNAET1 mediates nicotianamine secretion and enables nicotianamine-dependent phloem loading of Ni in nodes and subsequent Ni translocation into sink organs. Mutants lacking ZmNAET1 exhibit significant yield penalties, decreased seed germination velocity, and drastically shortened seed longevity. In an irreplaceable role, supplemented Ni fully rescued seed germination and proper vegetative development of the mutants. We show that NAET1-dependent delivery of Ni to urease is essential for amino acid turnover in developing sink organs, revealing an unappreciated role of Ni in yield formation of graminaceous plants. This study uncovers an underestimated requirement for nicotianamine and Ni and opens a new research avenue toward optimizing micronutrient provision for cereal crop productivity.

items.title: Right Heart Dysfunction in Valvular Heart Disease: Epidemiology, Prognosis, and Management Considerations.
items.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is an important determinant of clinical outcomes across a wide range of cardiovascular pathologies. As the prevalence of valvular heart disease (VHD) increases with the aging population, the intersection between RV function and VHD will become all the more relevant for proper risk assessment, treatment selection, and prognostication. Even though RV dysfunction may not always be attributed to VHD, we aim to give clinicians, researchers, and regulators a deep understanding of how patients with VHD should be evaluated for RV dysfunction and treated when RV dysfunction coexists with VHD. We begin with a discussion of the epidemiology and diagnostic evaluation of RV dysfunction in patients with a variety of VHD subgroups, including right-side (ie, associated with the tricuspid valve) and left-side (ie, associated with the mitral and aortic valves) VHD. Attention is also given in that section to contemporary methods and evolving techniques for identifying and phenotyping different forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD. No single imaging test practically or comprehensively captures all degrees and forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD; therefore, the discussion emphasizes integrating evidence from different imaging modalities and hemodynamic assessments. The second component of the review discusses how RV dysfunction affects therapeutic options, including medical, transcatheter, and surgical therapies for VHD. The focus of the discussion is on the interplay between RV dysfunction in patients with right-side VHD, namely tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Unlike left-side VHD, where RV dysfunction is a marker of overall disease severity but does not necessarily indicate futility or nonresponse to therapy, right-side VHD and TR-associated RV dysfunction identifies a subset of patients where intervention may precipitate even worse RV function. The nuances of these interactions between ventricular and valvular function are the emphasis of this section, and we aim to provide a framework for understanding RV function in the context of these different forms of VHD. Finally, the review concludes with an eye to the future, discussing the ways in which RV dysfunction can be identified and managed with the use of novel techniques. This discussion is increasingly relevant as RV dysfunction and VHD frequently coexist, and accurate identification is critical to matching the right treatment for the right patient.

items.title: Precursor lesions are associated with distinct growth kinetics after atrophy onset.

sections.objective: To evaluate whether atrophic lesions arising from different retinal precursors show distinct temporal growth kinetics in age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
sections.methods: Retrospective longitudinal cohort study. 109 eyes of 88 patients with intermediate AMD (iAMD) developing cRORA. Consecutive eyes with iAMD progressing to complete retinal pigment epithelium and outer retinal atrophy (cRORA) were identified by retrospective back-tracking of serial spectral-domain OCT. Precursors, defined as lesions that progressed to cRORA at the site of onset, were classified as drusenoid, subretinal drusenoid deposit (SDD), or acquired vitelliform lesion (AVL). Atrophy was segmented automatically on en face projections and manually corrected when needed. Temporal kinetics during the first 3 years after cRORA onset were assessed using piecewise linear time with knots at 1 and 2 years, adjusting for atrophic area, eccentricity, and number of foci at onset.
sections.results: Of 109 eyes progressing to cRORA, 66 arose from drusenoid, 31 from SDD, and 12 from AVL. After cRORA, the model-estimated growth rate was different according to the precursor lesions, with 0.197 mm/year in the drusenoid group, 0.383 mm/year in the SDD group, and 0.429 mm/year in the AVL group (P<0.001). Both SDD and AVL groups grew faster than the drusenoid group (both P<0.001), whereas SDD and AVL did not differ (P=0.44). Temporal kinetics also differed by precursor lesion (P<0.001). Compared with the drusenoid group, the SDD group did not differ in year 1 (difference, 0.041 mm/year; P=0.43) but grew faster in year 2 (0.306; P<0.001) and year 3 (0.237; P<0.001). AVL group showed faster growth in year 1 (0.396; P<0.001) and year 2 (0.248; P=0.002), but not year 3 (0.060; P=0.57). Differences persisted after adjustment for atrophy characteristics at onset. Parafoveal SDD burden provided no additional information once precursor lesion was accounted for (P=0.12).
sections.conclusion: The study finds distinct temporal trajectories: atrophy arising from drusenoid lesions grows more steadily, whereas from SDD accelerates later, and from AVL grows rapidly early then decelerates. SDD presence elsewhere may be less important than whether the atrophy arose from SDD. The findings may have prognostic implications, representing a stratification variable in clinical trials.
sections.other: Rate and temporal kinetics of square-root-transformed total atrophic area growth by precursor.

items.title: High-Dose Intravitreal Topotecan for Refractory or Recurrent Retinoblastoma: Efficacy, Safety and Intraocular Cytokine Profiles.

sections.objective: To evaluate the outcomes and safety of high-dose intravitreal topotecan (100 μg, IVitT100) in the treatment of refractory or recurrent intraocular retinoblastoma (RB).
sections.methods: Prospective, non-comparative case series. 15 consecutive patients (15 eyes) with refractory or recurrent RB at the Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University between October 2023 and September 2025. Participants received IVitT100 every four weeks. Clinical characteristics were recorded before and after treatment. Tumor control and injection-related complications were assessed at each visit. Aqueous humor cytokines and electroretinography (ERG) were analyzed to evaluate inflammatory changes and retinal function.
sections.results: At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6.0-14.0) after the final intravitreal injection, high-dose intravitreal topotecan achieved a globe salvage rate of 93%, with complete control of intraocular seeds in all eyes (100%) and complete regression of intraretinal tumors in 3 of 4 eyes (75%). Baseline ERG amplitude was 5.7 μV (IQR, 1.5-14.7), post-treatment amplitude was 5.7 μV (IQR, 1.9-15.8), showing no significant retinal function impairment (P = 0.429). None of the 27 cytokines showed significant changes between pre- and post-treatment measurements in RB eyes (all P > 0.05). No severe ocular or systemic adverse events were reported.
sections.conclusion: IVitT100 is highly effective for refractory or recurrent RB with vitreous seeds, subretinal seeds, and intraretinal tumors. It exhibits minimal retinal toxicity and does not induce intraocular inflammatory responses, supporting its role as a safe and effective first-line intravitreal therapy for advanced RB.
sections.other: Treatment outcomes, including intraretinal tumor and intraocular seeds control, globe salvage rate, and ocular and systemic adverse events, were assessed during follow-up.

items.title: Reoperations After Lateral Rectus Resection/Plication Versus Medial Rectus Recession for Age-Related Distance Esotropia.

sections.objective: Medial rectus (MR) recession and lateral rectus (LR) resection/plication are common surgical approaches for age-related distance esotropia (ARDE), but relative advantages of the two approaches are unclear. This study evaluates their comparative efficacy, rate of reoperation, and time to reoperations.
sections.methods: Retrospective, comparative interventional case series. Consecutive patients with ARDE undergoing strabismus surgery between 2014 and 2025 were reviewed.
sections.results: Surgical alignment effect and time to recurrence and reoperation. The study included 86 patients (58 females, 28 males) of mean age 70.5±8.7 years (standard deviation). Median postoperative follow-up was 1.5 (Interquartile range, IQR: 0.6-3.1, range: 0.5-10.8) years, and 61% were followed for more than 1 year. There was no difference between MR recession and LR resection/plication in the 34-37% rate of interventions by spectacle prism or reoperation required for unsatisfactory surgical outcomes. The reduction in distance ET in the LR resection/plication group was 12.6±9.8 (range: -2 to 38) Δ, similar to the 9.1±7.3 (range: -6 to 25) Δ in the MR recession group (p=0.067). Both procedures demonstrated identical surgical dose responses of 2Δ/mm. There was an insignificant trend towards higher reoperation of 30% in the MR group than 23% in the LR group. Median time to reoperation was longer at 2.8 (IQR:1.8-6.4) years after MR recession than LR resection/plication at 0.7 (IQR: 0.7-1.2) years (p=0.001).
sections.conclusion: Both MR recession and LR resection/plication have similar early surgical effect and eventual rate of reoperation for recurrence of ARDE. Patients undergoing LR resection/plication require earlier reoperation.

items.title: Occupational burnout among ophthalmologists: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Occupational burnout threatens clinician well-being, workforce stability, and the quality of patient care, yet its burden in ophthalmology has not been synthesized since 2021. We searched 5 databases from inception through March 13, 2026, and included 24 studies reporting burnout among ophthalmologists, ophthalmology trainees, and ophthalmology-specific health care professionals. Across the 12 studies with extractable prevalence data (n = 2,792), the pooled prevalence of burnout was 32.4% (95% confidence interval, 19.0%-49.5%; 95% prediction interval, 3.7%-85.6%), with extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 96.9%). All 9 sensitivity analyses produced estimates between 27.0% and 35.0%. Post hoc prevalence varied most with the operational definition of burnout, from 8.9% when all 3 Maslach dimensions were required to 52.7% when any 1 sufficed. Differences by instrument, career stage, and survey era were not statistically significant, and the numerically higher prevalence among residents largely disappeared after excluding the resident and attending studies with extreme definitions. Dissatisfaction with work-life balance (46.6%) was far more common than job dissatisfaction (20.1%). Women, academic or hospital-based practice, heavy workload, low work control, and inadequate support staff were the correlates reported most consistently. Approximately 1 in 3 ophthalmologists experiences burnout, although certainty is very low. Intervention research remains almost absent.

items.title: Scarring Alopecias Part 2: Treatments.
items.abstract: Primary cicatricial alopecias (PCAs) are a heterogeneous group of inflammatory disorders causing permanent, irreversible hair loss through hair follicle destruction and fibrotic replacement. Currently, there are no FDA-approved therapies. All treatments are used off label with the primary goals of halting inflammatory progression, providing symptom relief, and preserving viable follicles. Additionally, agents that prolong anagen are often utilized to increase the background hair density as a camouflaging method. Therapeutic selection is stratified by histologic inflammatory infiltrate pattern. Lymphocytic PCAs, including lichen planopilaris (LPP), frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA), central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (CCCA), and discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE), may respond to immunomodulatory agents. Meanwhile, neutrophilic variants, including folliculitis decalvans (FD) and dissecting cellulitis (DC), historically requires antimicrobial strategies. Emerging therapies address fibrotic mechanisms via topical and oral metformin, and Th17-mediated mechanisms via topical and oral JAK inhibitors and biologics targeting IL-17 and IL-23. Adjunctive modalities including topical and oral minoxidil, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), low-level light therapy (LLLT), and narrowband UVB (nbUVB) complement inflammation-directed care. This second part of the two-part CME series reviews evidence-based and emerging treatment options for PCAs.

items.title: Senescence induces clonal failure of hepatocyte plasticity and reshapes regenerative lineages.

sections.objective: Telomere dysregulation is a central driver of cellular senescence and chronic liver disease. Yet how physiological telomeric attrition, rather than uniform telomere loss, leads to hepatic functional decline remains unclear. We therefore investigate how resolvable telomere dysfunction reshapes liver regeneration.
sections.methods: An adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR-based strategy was developed to induce resolvable telomeric breaks in mouse hepatocytes while preserving endogenous telomere maintenance. Clonal dynamics, lineage tracing, and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling were used to characterize senescent hepatocyte behavior during chronic liver injury. Human cirrhotic liver samples were analyzed to assess the relationship between hepatocyte telomere length and intermediate cellular states. An in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte plasticity under telomere stress.
sections.results: Telomere-induced senescence did not substantially impair hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic function, but induced a clonal imbalance shaped by telomerase expression. Lineage tracing and single-nucleus transcriptomics demonstrated that senescent hepatocytes exhibited impaired hepatocyte-to-ductal metaplasia during chronic injury, with limited entry into the dedifferentiated state and failure to fully activate the ductal program. This incomplete transition disrupted epithelial composition and exacerbated the ductular reaction. Analyses of human cirrhotic livers revealed an association between preserved telomere integrity and bipotent hepatocyte states. Furthermore, the in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte dedifferentiation under telomere stress.
sections.conclusion: These findings identify senescence as a barrier to hepatobiliary clonal balance rather than a direct trigger of hepatocyte loss. Telomere dysfunction thereby promotes pathological epithelial remodeling during chronic liver injury.
sections.other: Telomere shortening is a common feature of chronic liver disease, but how it functionally contributes to regenerative failure remains incompletely understood. Our study shows that telomere dysfunction does not simply compromise hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic capacity. Instead, senescence acts as a clonal and lineage-selective constraint that limits hepatocyte plasticity and alters which cells contribute to regeneration. These findings provide a mechanistic link between telomere attrition, loss of regenerative diversity, and progressive liver dysfunction, and suggest that preservation of hepatocyte plasticity may be an important determinant of regenerative capacity in chronic liver disease.

items.title: Evolving management of upper extremity pseudoaneurysms: Role of observation and nonsurgical management.

sections.objective: While the natural history and treatment algorithm of femoral pseudoaneurysms has been well established, the management of Upper Extremity Pseudoaneurysm (UEPSA) is not clearly defined. We sought to evaluate our 30-year experience and management strategies of this pathology.
sections.methods: We reviewed 93 patients that were identified utilizing ICD9/10 codes from an initial 384 patients with the diagnosis of aneurysm of the upper extremity from 1992 to 2023. Patients with UEPSA secondary to iatrogenic arterial interrogation were analyzed by duplex based follow-up until successful thrombosis or subsequent intervention was performed. Dialysis access pseudoaneurysms or trauma related UEPSAs were excluded for analysis.
sections.results: A total of 93 patients were identified with a UEPSA (39 brachial, 43 radial, 6 axillary, 5 ulnar arteries); 12 additional patients were identified who had only a patent neck at the time of formal vascular laboratory imaging and were excluded from treatment strategy analysis (11 radial, 1 brachial). The mean time between iatrogenic event and vascular surgery evaluation was 22 days. Fifty-nine (63.4%) underwent surgical repair, 27 (29.0%) received conservative management, and 7 (7.5%) underwent thrombin injection. Of the 93 treatment group patients that were analyzed, separated into sizes, patients with pseudoaneurysms less than 2cm there were a total of 21/93 (22.5%) patients managed conservatively, and 16/93 (17.2%) patients managed surgically; in contrast for those with greater than 2cm UEPSAs, 6/93 (6.5%) patients were managed conservatively, 43/93 (46.2%) were managed surgically, and 7/93 (7.5%) with thrombin injection. Comparing the first 15 years of the study period there were 27 iatrogenic UEPSAs noted with only 3/27 (11.1%) managed conservatively, while after 2010 there were 66 iatrogenic pseudoaneurysms with 24/66 (36.4%) managed conservatively. Of the UEPSAs managed conservatively, only 3/24 (12.5%) failed conservative management and were recommended to pursue intervention.
sections.conclusion: Upper extremity pseudoaneurysms with significant symptomatic hematomas, suspected infection, and/or nerve related symptoms should undergo surgical exploration and repair. A consideration for conservative management of small pseudoaneurysms <2cm without the above presentation, observation and surveillance may be considered with more than 90% achieving successful spontaneous thrombosis.

items.title: Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes With the E-tegra™ Stent Graft System for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: Endoleaks, Limb Patency, Reinterventions, Aneurysm Sac Behaviour, and Mid-Term Follow-Up.

sections.objective: To systematically synthesize the published clinical evidence regarding endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the E-tegra™ stent graft system, evaluating technical success, endoleaks, limb patency, reinterventions, aneurysm sac behavior, and mid-term follow-up outcomes.
sections.methods: Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included. Because of cohort overlap and heterogeneous endpoint definitions, data were synthesized narratively and descriptively without formal quantitative pooling.
sections.results: Three eligible publications were identified, representing 209 unique patients across two underlying cohorts: the multicenter TIGRE registry (147 patients) and an independent single-center series (62 patients). Primary technical success was high, reaching 99.3% in the registry and 100% in the single-center cohort, with zero perioperative mortality across both. At mid-term follow-up (ranging from 18 months to 2 years), type II endoleak and iliac limb occlusion emerged as the primary complications. The TIGRE update reported 16 total complications (10.88%), including 8 type II endoleaks and 6 iliac limb occlusions, with a 2-year reintervention rate of 4.76%. In the single-center series, 1 type IIIa endoleak (1.6%) and 3 clinically significant type II endoleaks requiring embolization were observed. Favorable mid-term sac behavior was noted in the registry, with 72.11% of patients demonstrating >10-mm aneurysm sac shrinkage. Predefined anatomical hostility did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with adverse outcomes or reinterventions in the registry data.
sections.conclusion: Early and mid-term evidence for the E-tegra stent graft demonstrates high procedural success and acceptable clinical outcomes with competitive mid-term complication and reintervention rates. However, the current literature is strictly limited to single-arm observational data with short-to-medium horizons (18-24 months). Long-term durability and structural performance relative to well-established companion platforms remain unestablished, highlighting the critical need for continued prospective surveillance and comparative, long-term multicenter trials.

items.title: Advances in Retinal Cellular Imaging: Towards Single-Cell Resolution and Functional Biomarkers.
items.abstract: Retinal imaging has traditionally described tissue and layer level pathology, whereas direct assessment of individual cells in the living human retina has been limited by ocular aberrations, optical contrast and image analysis constraints. Adaptive optics (AO) has substantially changed this landscape by improving lateral resolution and enabling in vivo visualization of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), ganglion-cell-layer structures, immune cells and microvasculature. This review discusses human retinal cellular imaging across three major AO-enhanced platforms: flood-illumination adaptive optics (FIAO), adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) and adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO). These modalities provide complementary capabilities, including rapid en face imaging, depth-resolved volumetric assessment and flexible confocal, non-confocal and fluorescence-based contrast. Recent progress is also being shaped by faster wavefront correction, wider-field acquisition, compressed multichannel imaging, sensorless AO and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted reconstruction, segmentation and quantification. Beyond optical resolution, molecular labeling strategies are beginning to add biological specificity to retinal cellular imaging. Indocyanine green (ICG) supports AO-assisted assessment of RPE mosaic contrast, annexin V-based Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) provides a molecular readout of retinal cell stress and apoptosis, and curcumin-based imaging has been explored as an experimental retinal amyloid marker in Alzheimer's disease. Together, these advances indicate a shift from high-resolution visualization alone towards cellular and molecular biomarkers of disease activity, progression and treatment response. Further translation will require standardized acquisition, robust automated analysis, multimodal validation and larger prospective studies across devices, disease populations and clinical sites.

items.title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.

sections.objective: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR.
sections.methods: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed.
sections.results: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions.
sections.conclusion: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

items.title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

sections.objective: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis.
sections.results: A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I2 = 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I2 = 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I2 = 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I2 = 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I2 = 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I2 = 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I2 = 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I2 = 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes.
sections.conclusion: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.
sections.other: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE.

items.title: Topical sirolimus gel for hyperplastic rosacea: A randomized, double-blind, controlled study and exploration of two-dimensional to three-dimensional approximate protrusion volume (APV) assessment.

sections.objective: Hyperplastic rosacea is difficult to treat. Sirolimus may be a topical option. To evaluate topical sirolimus gel and explore two-dimensional-to-three-dimensional approximate protrusion volume (APV) assessment.
sections.methods: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 65 patients applied 0.2% sirolimus gel (n = 29) or placebo (n = 36) twice daily. The primary endpoint was an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score ≤1 after a 12-week cycle. Secondary and exploratory endpoints included Clinician's Erythema Assessment (CEA) success, artificial intelligence-estimated APV change, subgroup analyses, and correlations between APV and clinical scores.
sections.results: IGA success was 72.4% versus 33.3% (adjusted relative risk, 1.949; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.153-3.294; P = .013), and CEA success was 69.0% versus 30.6% (adjusted relative risk, 2.778; 95% CI, 1.627-4.743; P < .001). APV reduction was greater with sirolimus (-61.556 units; P < .001). Baseline APV correlated with IGA (ρ = 0.386; P = .001) and CEA (ρ = 0.314; P = .011). No serious adverse events occurred.
sections.conclusion: Topical sirolimus gel showed exploratory clinical and APV signals; confirmatory trials are needed.
sections.other: Single-center design, small sample, short follow-up, unvalidated algorithm, and no systemic absorption, quality-of-life, or satisfaction assessments.

items.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.

sections.objective: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain.
sections.methods: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated.
sections.results: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099).
sections.conclusion: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes.

items.title: Generation of Human Cardiomyocytes With Adult-Like Metabolism by a Chemically Defined Medium for Mitochondrial Disease Modeling.

sections.objective: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC cardiomyocytes) as a model for cardiac disease have become increasingly important, bolstered by the Food and Drug Administration's initiative to promote novel alternative methods for biomedical research. A key limitation of metabolically immature iPSC cardiomyocytes is their limited ability to accurately recapitulate mitochondria-dependent pathologies, such as Friedreich ataxia-associated cardiomyopathy. Adult cardiomyocytes are characterized by a high density of interfibrillar mitochondria, abundant respiratory complexes (I-V) that form supercomplexes, and efficient utilization of fatty acids to drive mitochondrial respiration. These unique metabolic structures and functions are largely missing in iPSC cardiomyocytes. Further, whether iPSC cardiomyocytes can efficiently utilize fatty acids for respiration in the presence of glucose, a unique adult feature, remains unclear.
sections.methods: We developed a chemically defined, 11-component maturation medium (MM11) designed using a bioinformatics-guided strategy that identified high-fidelity transcriptional markers of adult cardiac metabolic maturity. Human iPSC cardiomyocytes were treated with MM11 for 2 weeks and evaluated at the molecular, structural, and functional levels, with an emphasis on mitochondrial maturity. We benchmarked our results with isolated primary adult human cardiomyocytes. Last, we tested whether this method could enable us to more accurately model Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy.
sections.results: MM11 treatment increased expression of metabolic pathways, including mitochondrial respiration and fatty acid metabolism, at the transcript and protein levels. Ultrastructural analyses revealed the formation of interfibrillar mitochondria and mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes, a feature never shown in previous reports. Functionally, MM11-treated iPSC cardiomyocytes exhibited substantially increased oxidative phosphorylation and a metabolic preference for fatty acid utilization in the presence of physiologic substrates, as determined by oxygen consumption assays and 13C isotope tracing.
sections.conclusion: MM11 promotes robust metabolic maturation of human iPSC cardiomyocytes, enabling sophisticated mitochondrial architecture and substrate utilization. These metabolically matured cardiomyocytes more faithfully model mitochondria-dependent cardiac pathologies, including ischemia-reperfusion injury and Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy, improving the use of iPSC cardiomyocytes for mechanistic studies of human heart disease.

items.title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.

sections.objective: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain. The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD.
sections.methods: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.
sections.results: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.
sections.conclusion: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

items.title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Identifies Central Role for Inflammatory Pathways.

sections.objective: Epigenetic mechanisms underlying susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) remain poorly understood. Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways.
sections.methods: We first conducted an epigenome-wide association study of incident AAA (1324 cases and 42 065 noncases), performed stratified analyses by population group and smoking status, and conducted Mendelian randomization to facilitate causal inference of the cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG)-AAA association. Chromatin state, island context, and transcription factor binding were implicated through functional annotation of identified CpGs. To identify genes impacted by change in methylation state, we aligned associations with transcriptional data obtained in blood, aorta, and liver. We performed expression quantitative trait methylation to capture CpG-gene-expression links across the genome. Network Mendelian randomization was used to test cardiometabolic and inflammatory mediation. Finally, we developed a methylation risk score for AAA using penalized regression and evaluated its performance against a clinical model in the Million Veteran Program and 2 external studies.
sections.results: Epigenome-wide association study identified 1253 CpGs associated with incident AAA, and Mendelian randomization supported a putative causal role for 143 of these associations. Functional annotation pointed to predominantly distal, enhancer-centered regulation and enrichment of inflammatory transcription factor programs (eg, activator protein-1 and nuclear factor κB). This distal architecture was consistent with expression quantitative trait methylation results, which showed a larger number of trans associations. Among 143 CpGs associated with AAA in Mendelian randomization analyses, we identified 213 CpG-gene expression pairs with strong colocalization support, including AGER, C2, and DDR1. Multi-trait colocalization further prioritized 8 CpG-gene expression-AAA links with evidence of a shared genetic signal. Network Mendelian randomization identified 135 putative mediation pathways linking CpGs to AAA, including 58 via cardiometabolic traits and 77 via inflammation-related traits. Blood lipid traits mediated >40% of the associations between AAA risk and CpGs near LDLR (cg19305903) and TRIB1 (cg14128479). Among inflammation-related mediators, circulating DAG1, NEXN, MMP9, IL1RN, and MMP13 were prioritized as potential intermediates. Additionally, a CpG selection process was used to develop a methylation risk score for AAA, which strongly associated with disease in both the discovery cohort and 2 external validation cohorts, even after adjustment for a full suite of clinical covariates.
sections.conclusion: This study identified putative causal DNA methylation markers for AAA, and multi-omics analyses implicate activator protein-1-linked inflammatory transcriptional programs, blood lipids, and multiple inflammation-related proteins as key pathways underlying methylation-associated AAA risk.

items.title: The Association Between Hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center Designation Status and Stroke Rate Reporting in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Implications for Hospital Performance Assessment.

sections.objective: The Michigan Structural Heart Consortium showed that transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) stroke rates were associated with hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) designation, suggesting that hospital structural factors affect stroke reporting. We sought to determine whether CSC designation is nationally associated with reported stroke rates and the potential impact on hospital performance and Transcatheter Valve Therapy National Data Registry (TVTR) public reporting.
sections.methods: Consecutive TVTR cases from January 2016 through June 2023 were included, excluding sites reporting to the TVTR <1 year or performing <20 total TAVR procedures. The primary outcome was in-hospital stroke rate. Secondary outcomes were disabling stroke and 30-day stroke. Major bleeding, death, acute renal failure, and a composite end point were falsification end points to determine whether CSC status was uniquely associated with stroke. Multivariable hierarchical models were created starting with patient covariates and sequentially adding hospital variables to account for determinants of stroke. The impact of CSC status on hospital performance was estimated by correcting CSC hospital stroke rates in the validated TVTR 30-day composite model.
sections.results: A total of 525 919 TAVRs at 800 sites were included, and 10 963 strokes (2.1%) were reported within 30 days: 8284 (1.6%) in-hospital and 2679 (0.5%) after discharge. A total of 4733 (0.9%) were disabling strokes. Multivariate analysis showed that CSC status and participation in TAVR trials were independent predictors of in-hospital stroke rate (P=0.033 and 0.012) and disabling stroke (P=0.033 and 0.007), but not falsification end points (P=NS). Participation in TAVR trials and operator volume were independent predictors of 30-day stroke (P=0.039 and P=0.041). The impact of CSC status on the 30-day composite model showed performance improvement for 8 of 153 CSC hospitals.
sections.conclusion: CSC hospital status and participation in TAVR trials are significant predictors unique for stroke. Correcting for the association of CSC status on stroke rate resulted in an estimated 8 of 153 hospitals improving their TVTR 30-day composite model performance. Further work is needed to account for potential ascertainment bias for stroke in public reporting.

items.title: Short-Term Anticoagulant Therapy and Subclinical Leaflet Thickening in Transcatheter Aortic Valves: The NOTION-4 Trial.

sections.objective: Following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), subclinical leaflet thrombosis-visualized on cardiac computed tomography (CT) as hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT)-is common and might be associated with thromboembolic events. The NOTION-4 trial investigates different antithrombotic treatment strategies for the prevention of HALT.
sections.methods: NOTION-4 was a randomized controlled trial enrolling patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation shortly after successful TAVR. Patients were randomized to lifelong single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) or 3 months of direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) therapy followed by lifelong SAPT (DOAC-3m). The primary endpoint was HALT prevalence at 12 months. The trial was powered for superiority of the experimental strategy.
sections.results: Of 352 patients randomized 1:1, 5 were screen failures or withdrew consent, leaving 176 in the SAPT group and 171 in the DOAC-3m group. At 3 months, HALT was observed in 31.8% of patients receiving SAPT compared with 12.1% of those receiving DOAC-3m. At 1 year, HALT occurred in 32.2% of SAPT patients and 28.3% of DOAC-3m patients with available CT scans (risk difference: -3.9%; 95% CI: -14.4% to 6.6%; P = 0.54). The combined risk of all-cause mortality, stroke, or major/life-threatening bleeding at 12 months was 2.3% in the SAPT group vs 8.2% in the DOAC-3m group (risk difference: 5.9%; 95% CI: 1.2% to 10.6%).
sections.conclusion: Among TAVR patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation, 3 months of DOAC therapy significantly reduced the prevalence of HALT at 3 months compared with SAPT; however, this effect was attenuated by 9 months after discontinuation of DOAC therapy. (The Nordic Aortic Valve Intervention Trial 4 [NOTION-4]; NCT06449469).

items.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement or Medical Treatment for Paradoxical Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Valve Stenosis: REBOOT-PARADOX.

sections.objective: Paradoxical low-flow, low-gradient (pLFLG) aortic stenosis (AS) has an adverse prognosis in comparison to other AS subtypes. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has never been compared with optimal medical therapy (OMT) alone in a dedicated randomized trial in this population. The trial sought to determine whether TAVR added to OMT reduces all-cause mortality in symptomatic patients with pLFLG AS.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label trial, patients with symptomatic pLFLG AS (aortic valve area ≤1.0 cm2, mean gradient <40 mm Hg, stroke volume index <35 mL/m2, ejection fraction ≥50%) were randomly assigned 2:1 to TAVR plus OMT or OMT alone. The primary endpoint was all-cause death, assessed 2 years after enrollment of the last patient. Enrollment was stopped prematurely for slow recruitment.
sections.results: Of 783 planned patients, 120 (median age 82 years; 53.3% women) were randomized (80 TAVR, 40 OMT). A total of 19 OMT patients eventually crossed over to TAVR, most for symptom progression. The primary endpoint occurred in 29.0% vs 37.1% (HR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.41-1.66; P = 0.60), and 5-year mortality was 44.9% vs 56.6% (HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.43-1.35; P = 0.35). TAVR was associated with improved symptoms (NYHA functional class I/II at 1 year, 83.0% vs 59.0%) and lower cumulative incidence of first endpoint-related rehospitalizations, and there were no differences in functional capacity or quality of life.
sections.conclusion: Although the effect of TAVR on mortality remains unresolved, these findings support an individualized strategy with close surveillance and timely TAVR upon clinical deterioration in selected patients with pLFLG AS. Adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define the effect of early TAVR on prognosis. (accuRate Evaluation of Benefit with Optimal medical treatment with or withOut Transcatheter valve repair of PARADOXical low flow low gradient aortic stenosis [REBOOT-PARADOX Trial]; NCT03863132).

keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

items.title: Systemic Microvascular Endothelial Dysfunction in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes: A Pooled Analysis of GLADIATOR-HFpEF, IRON-HFpEF, EMPA-MVD, Hoorn Diabetes Care System, and Healthy Controls.

sections.objective: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder featuring microvascular dysfunction and metabolic comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the extent to which systemic microvascular abnormalities reflect HFpEF or coexisting T2D remains incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to characterize systemic microvascular dysfunction in patients with HFpEF and to evaluate the contribution of comorbid T2D.
sections.methods: Systemic microvascular function, defined as flow responses expressed as cutaneous vascular conductance, was assessed using laser speckle contrast analysis with iontophoresis of acetylcholine, insulin, and sodium nitroprusside. Analysis adjusted for age and sex were performed across healthy controls (n = 23), T2D (n = 138), HFpEF without T2D (n = 63), and HFpEF with T2D (n = 27).
sections.results: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls.
sections.conclusion: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bepranemab in people living with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Tau aggregation is a defining feature of the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease and an appealing therapeutic target, yet tau-directed antibodies tested to date-primarily targeting N-terminal epitopes-have failed to slow tau progression or cognitive decline. Bepranemab targets the tau mid-region, predicted in cell-based assays to more effectively block neuron-to-neuron tau spread than anti-tau antibodies targeting the N-terminus. We aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of bepranemab in slowing progression of tau pathology and clinical decline in people with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease.
sections.methods: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial recruited participants across 101 outpatient sites in Europe (eight countries), Canada, and the USA. Participants (aged 50-80 years) with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease were randomly assigned 1:1:1 (using an interactive response system) to intravenous bepranemab 45 mg/kg, bepranemab 90 mg/kg, or placebo (every 4 weeks for 76 weeks), stratified by diagnosis, apolipoprotein E ɛ4 carrier status, and symptomatic treatment use. The primary endpoint was change from baseline to week 80 in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) total score. Efficacy was assessed in the full analysis set (ie, all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of trial medication and had at least one valid post-baseline clinic visit and efficacy assessment). Safety was assessed in all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of the trial medication. No imputation was done for missing data. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04867616) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Aug 24, 2021, and Oct 25, 2022, 466 participants were randomly assigned to bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=154), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=155), or placebo (n=157) at 85 sites. Median age was 72·0 years (IQR 66·0-76·0), 259 (56%) were female, and 207 (44%) were male. In total, 460 participants were included in the full analysis set: bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=152), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=152), and placebo (n=156). Least-squares mean CDR-SB total score change from baseline to week 80 was 2·15 in the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 1·85 in the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group versus 1·81 in the placebo group, with differences versus placebo of 0·34 (95% CI -0·09 to 0·78, p=0·12; 80% CI 0·06 to 0·63) for the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 0·04 (-0·40 to 0·47, p=0·87; -0·25 to 0·32) for the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group. Frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events with bepranemab was similar to the placebo group (139 [91%] with bepranemab 45 mg/kg, 140 [91%] with bepranemab 90 mg/kg, and 142 [90%] with placebo); no treatment-related neuroinflammatory safety signals were identified clinically or on brain MRI scans. There were adverse events leading to death in four (1%) participants in the combined bepranemab groups and six (4%) in the placebo group; none were considered related to the trial treatment.
sections.conclusion: Treatment with bepranemab was associated with an acceptable safety profile. However, the primary endpoint was not met. Hypothesis-generating differences favouring bepranemab in tau PET and 14-item Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale should be tested prospectively in trials powered for tau PET outcomes and stratified by baseline tau burden and apolipoprotein E ɛ4 status.

items.title: Maternal and perinatal outcomes in pregnant women with Lassa fever: analysis from the LASCOPE prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Lassa fever, a viral haemorrhagic fever endemic in west Africa, is usually described as associated with severe maternal and perinatal outcomes. Previous studies reported maternal mortality of 33% (whereas overall mortality is about 14% in Nigeria for patients admitted to hospital) and fetal mortality is up to 60%. However, most evidence derives from small case series with substantial limitations. We aimed to assess maternal death and perinatal outcomes in a prospective cohort study with standardised medical care protocols.
sections.methods: We analysed data from the LASCOPE cohort from the Federal Medical Centre Owo, Nigeria, which included all patients with PCR-confirmed Lassa fever. In this analysis, non-pregnant women of childbearing age (15-45 years) were compared with pregnant women, defined as having an ongoing pregnancy during Lassa fever. The primary maternal outcome was all-cause mortality 28 days after admission and the primary pregnancy outcome was fetal death. Mortality at 28 days was compared using Kaplan-Meier estimates and a Cox proportional-hazards model, the cumulative incidence of fetal death was estimated with livebirth as a competing event, and the association between gestational age at symptom onset and fetal death was assessed by logistic regression.
sections.results: Between April 4, 2018, and Feb 18, 2023, of 1006 patients in the LASCOPE cohort admitted with PCR-confirmed Lassa fever, 703 were excluded for not being of childbearing age, and 303 were women of childbearing age, of whom 45 were pregnant. The median age of pregnant women was 28 years (IQR 24-32). The 28-day mortality was comparable between pregnant and non-pregnant women (four [9%; 95% CI 2-21] of 45 vs 19 [7%; 95% CI 4-11] of 258; hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·41-3·50]; log-rank p=0·75). Fetal case-fatality rate was 60% (27 of 45), with higher risk of fetal death if infection occurred early in the pregnancy (100% for the first trimester, 82% for the second trimester, and 25% for the third trimester). Each additional week of gestation at symptom onset was associated with a reduction in the odds of fetal death (odds ratio 0·77 [95% CI 0·61-0·90]). Among 15 liveborn infants, three (20%) died within 30 days.
sections.conclusion: Although the fetal prognosis was poor, as previously reported, maternal fatality was lower than previously indicated, potentially reflecting improved supportive care and patient monitoring. These findings suggest that maternal mortality might be lower than historically reported, while confirming the urgent need for specific therapeutic interventions to improve fetal outcomes.

items.title: Incidence and predictors of suboptimal functional outcomes despite successful reperfusion in paediatric stroke: a cohort study from the Save ChildS Pro registry.

sections.objective: Successful vessel reperfusion with persistent clinical deficit occurs in 40-60% of adults undergoing mechanical thrombectomy but has never been characterised in childhood stroke. We aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of so-called futile recanalisation, in which the occluded artery is reopened but the patient does not recover good function, in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke.
sections.methods: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023. Patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy and had successful recanalisation (expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [eTICI] grade ≥2b) were included.
