The primary outcome was suboptimal functional outcome despite successful recanalisation, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score greater than 2 at 90 days, on a scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death) on which 0-2 denotes functional independence; three additional thresholds (mRS score >1, Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure [PSOM] >1·0, and PSOM >0·5) were analysed as sensitivity analyses. Adjusted associations between candidate predictors (age, baseline Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [PedNIHSS] score, baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score [ASPECTS], and final eTICI grade) and each outcome were estimated using Firth-penalised multivariable logistic regression. Save ChildS Pro is registered with the German Clinical Trials Registry (DRKS00018960).
sections.results: 101 patients (54 [53%] males and 47 [47%] females; median age 11·0 years [IQR 6·0-15·0]) had successful recanalisation with 90-day follow-up and comprised the analytical cohort. A suboptimal outcome (mRS score >2) occurred in 18 (18%) of 101 patients. On Firth-adjusted multivariable analysis, lower final eTICI grade was significantly associated with suboptimal outcome (adjusted OR 0·44 [95% CI 0·23-0·84], p=0·012), and younger age was associated in the same direction (0·87 [0·78-0·97] per year, p=0·0098); baseline PedNIHSS score and baseline ASPECTS were not independently associated with a suboptimal outcome. Findings were directionally consistent across the three sensitivity thresholds.
sections.conclusion: In this analysis, 18% of children with successful recanalisation had a suboptimal functional outcome at 90 days, markedly lower than the proportion reported in adults (40-60%). Lower recanalisation quality and younger age were independently associated with suboptimal outcome, whereas baseline PedNIHSS score and ASPECTS had limited prognostic value. These findings highlight the need for longer-term studies and challenge the direct translation of adult prognostic frameworks to paediatric stroke, supporting age-specific approaches. Given the limited event count, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation.

items.title: Safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity of a combination of TMB-365 and TMB-380 in people living with HIV suppressed with antiretroviral therapy in the USA: a phase 1b/2a, open-label, dose-escalation study.

sections.objective: Long-acting antibody-based regimens might reduce treatment burden for people living with HIV. We aimed to assess safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity of TMB-365, a CD4-directed monoclonal antibody, combined with TMB-380, a long-acting broadly neutralising monoclonal antibody targeting gp120 CD4-binding site.
sections.methods: In this phase 1b/2a, open-label, dose-escalation study, virologically suppressed adults (aged 18-70 years) living with HIV on stable oral combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) were enrolled from six clinic sites in California, Florida, and Texas, in the USA. In phase 1b, participants received single intravenous doses of TMB-365 plus TMB-380 at either 2400 mg, 3200 mg, or 4800 mg and continued ART for 12-16 weeks. In phase 2a, participants discontinued ART at baseline and received 4800 mg of each antibody intravenously every 8 weeks, three times over 24 weeks, without pretreatment screening. Primary outcomes were safety and pharmacokinetics in phase 1b, and safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity in phase 2a. In phase 2a all treated participants were included in safety and efficacy analyses, except one participant inadvertently dosed after developing an acute medical condition before dosing. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05275998) and is complete.
sections.results: Between July 5, 2022, and Nov 20, 2024, 30 participants (28 male and two female) were enrolled in phase 1b, and 20 male participants were enrolled in phase 2a. In phase 2a, two participants discontinued prematurely, and one was lost to follow-up. No serious or grade 3 or worse adverse events were observed. All treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate. Pharmacokinetic targets were met at week 8 in the phase 1b 4800 mg group. In phase 2a, viral suppression at week 24 occurred in 16 (94%, 95% CI 71-100) of 17 participants in the per-protocol population and 16 (80%, 95% CI 56-94) of 20 participants in the intention-to-treat population. No confirmed virological failures were reported.
sections.conclusion: TMB-365 (4800 mg) plus TMB-380 (4800 mg) every 8 weeks appears safe, might be effective as maintenance therapy in virologically suppressed people living with HIV, and merits further study.

items.title: Risovalisib for PIK3CA-mutated recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
sections.methods: We conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients.
sections.results: Between Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four [4%]). There were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: These results support risovalisib as a potential novel treatment option for PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a rare yet lethal cancer in dire need of additional treatment options. Combination strategies including risovalisib could also be explored to further increase efficacy observed in this study.

items.title: Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.
items.abstract: Agriculture is both humanity's largest infrastructure and the leading driver of environmental degradation. Many early-stage biotechnologies could mitigate this impact, but their deployability has not been systematically evaluated. We analyze deployability of 77 biotechnologies across eight domains (crops, soils, livestock, watersheds, aquaculture, health and security, food loss/waste and frontiers) by applying a Balanced Readiness Level assessment spanning technological, market, regulatory, acceptance and organizational dimensions. We find that market viability and social acceptance, not technological readiness, represent the primary constraints. High-readiness technologies tend to be 'drop-in', contained, transient and perceived as natural. These characteristics indicate strategies to elevate overall deployability, such as addressing genetically modified organism containment. Assessing the scalability and environmental impacts of biotechnologies for prioritization requires additional quantitative analysis, as shown in a Fermi analysis of microbial fertilizers. We combine our findings into a near- to long-term roadmap for living infrastructure: predictively designed multicomponent biological communities that function as systems at the ecosystem level to enhance food security and environmental resilience.

items.title: Dialogical therapy plus treatment as usual versus treatment as usual in adults with distressing and persistent auditory hallucinations in the UK (Talking with Voices-II): a randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Existing treatments for auditory hallucinations (hereafter voice hearing) among people with serious mental health problems (SMHPs; diagnoses include schizophrenia spectrum disorders, bipolar disorders, and personality disorders) show only modest clinical benefits, produce inconsistent long-term outcomes, and seldom prioritise personal recovery as a primary treatment goal. We aimed to investigate the effectiveness of Talking with Voices (TwV), a lived-experience informed intervention in which therapists engage in direct dialogue with voices, in improving both personal recovery and clinical outcomes for individuals experiencing persistent and distressing voice hearing.
sections.methods: Talking with Voices-II was a rater-blinded, parallel-arm, multisite, randomised controlled trial to test the efficacy and underlying mechanisms of TwV therapy compared with treatment as usual (TAU) in community-based National Health Service mental health services across four UK sites. Participants with SMHPs who experienced distressing voices were randomly assigned (1:1), using random-sized blocks, stratified by site and presence of schizophrenia diagnosis, to receive either TwV plus TAU or TAU alone. Therapy was provided in up to 26 sessions over 8 months, and assessments were conducted at baseline, 8 months, and 14 months by assessors masked to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was the Questionnaire about the Process of Recovery score at 8 months, a self-reported measure of personal recovery in psychosis. Secondary outcomes were voice-related measures, self-beliefs, dissociation, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms. The primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle, and moderation and mediation were prespecified in the statistical analysis plan. The mediation analysis was carried out using the mediate command, utilising bootstrapping to obtain percentile CIs. The trial was prospectively registered with ISRCTN, ISRCTN15897915, and all research and clinical procedures were co-led by individuals with lived experience of psychosis.
sections.results: Between Sept 1, 2023, and June 30, 2025, we screened 1316 participants, of whom 309 consented, completed baseline assessments, and were randomly assigned to either TwV plus TAU (n=156) or TAU alone (n=153). The mean age of participants was 41·1 years (SD 13·1). 159 (52%) participants were men, 145 (47%) were women, and four (1%) were another gender, and one preferred not to say; 222 (72%) participants were White. At 8 months, personal recovery was significantly better in the TwV group than in the TAU group (adjusted difference 6·97 [95% CI 5·00-8·95]; p<0·0001; standardised effect size [SES] 0·63). Significant differences favouring TwV were found for 12 (80%) of 15 of secondary outcomes, unadjusted for multiple testing, including all voice-related measures, negative self-beliefs, and PTSD outcomes, with SES ranging from 0·18 to 0·86. There were no effects on dissociation-related measures or positive self-beliefs (SES ranging from <0·01 to 0·16). An effect was still evident on personal recovery at 14 months, although reduced (adjusted difference 3·55 [0·96-6·14]; p=0·0073; SES=0·32). 55 serious adverse events occurred in 36 participants in the TwV group, and 60 serious adverse events occurred in 45 participants in the TAU group, none of which were deemed definitely related to the therapy or research procedures.
sections.conclusion: TwV significantly improves personal recovery, showing efficacy for individuals with SMHPs who experience distressing voices. Further research comparing TwV with an active control and evaluating its implementation in routine care settings is warranted.

items.title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of antidepressants in the long-term treatment of major depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Major depressive disorder carries high risks of relapse and chronicity, necessitating treatments that achieve and maintain response (sustained response). This study aimed to compare antidepressants on their ability to achieve sustained response, and on acceptability, by synthesising data from randomised controlled trials.
sections.methods: For this systematic review and network meta-analysis, we searched the Cochrane Register, AMED, CINAHL, Embase, LILACS, MEDLINE, MEDLINE In-Progress, PsycINFO, the UK National Research Register, and regulatory agency websites from inception to March 27, 2026. We included double-blind randomised controlled trials that compared any of 21 antidepressants head-to-head or with placebo for long-term treatment (>12 weeks) of adult unipolar major depressive disorder. We included enrichment, non-enrichment, continuation, and continuation-extension designs, and extracted study-level data. We could not derive the sex or gender distribution of participants other than female and did not extract data on race or ethnicity. Primary outcomes were efficacy (sustained response rate) and acceptability (all-cause discontinuation). We synthesised data in random-effects pairwise and network meta-analyses to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs), using fluoxetine as a reference in the ranked forest plots. The primary analysis included head-to-head continuation and continuation-extension design studies. Enrichment design studies were incorporated in the analysis using a chain-of-evidence approach. Risk-of-bias assessment was done using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. No people with lived experience were involved in the design, conduct, or interpretation of this study.
sections.results: From 54 231 records, 115 studies (30 428 participants; mean age 45·3 years [SD 8·5], 20 066 [66%] female) were included. In head-to-head continuation and continuation-extension design studies (35 studies; n=9888), sustained response differed across antidepressants. Escitalopram (OR 1·62, 95% CI 1·21-2·18), duloxetine (OR 1·57, 1·08-2·26), and agomelatine (OR 1·40, 1·06-1·85) showed higher sustained response rates than fluoxetine. Bupropion and reboxetine showed lower sustained response rates against four other antidepressants in the league table of pairwise comparisons. Escitalopram (OR 0·60, 0·43-0·83) and duloxetine (OR 0·64, 0·44-0·95) demonstrated lower all-cause discontinuation compared with fluoxetine, while reboxetine and milnacipran showed higher all-cause discontinuation against six and four other antidepressants, respectively, in the league table of pairwise comparisons. Sensitivity analyses incorporating enrichment-design studies corroborated these results. However, the certainty of evidence of the network meta-analysis results and the risk of bias in the included studies (19 [54%] of 35 had high risk of bias) might limit the reliability of the current findings.
sections.conclusion: Antidepressants can differ in their efficacy for achieving sustained response and in their acceptability. These findings can inform the shared decision making for patients, prescribers, and carers in real-world practice. However, more head-to-head comparative studies are needed to provide reliable information about long-term effects of all licensed antidepressants.

items.title: Cellular agriculture for sustainable and programmable foods.
items.abstract: Cellular agriculture promises to reduce the environmental burden and inefficiencies of food systems. The question is no longer whether precision fermentation and cultivated meat production can produce alternative proteins and other food components, but whether they can attain the cost, scale and quality required for broad adoption. We examine cellular agriculture through the interrelated lenses of enabling technologies, food function and manufacturing economics. The field is approaching an inflection point where biological technology development is less important for commercial success than achieving scalable, affordable manufacturing. Key challenges include how products and their functional attributes are designed and how production processes are configured. For precision fermentation, the most compelling opportunities lie in functional approaches to improve taste, nutritional quality, health benefits and formulation rather than in direct imitation of existing foods or ingredients. For cultivated meat production, impact will come first from hybrid and ingredient-based products that capture specific values of cellular ingredients while avoiding the costs of full tissue mimicry.

items.title: Cardiovascular outcomes with survodutide in adults with obesity at increased cardiovascular risk (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Survodutide, a glucagon receptor and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, improved markers of cardiometabolic health in people with obesity, but cardiovascular safety for this new class remains to be established.
sections.methods: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT was a global, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicentre, event-driven, cardiovascular safety trial conducted at 524 clinical sites in 34 countries. We included participants aged 18 years or older with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater and established cardiovascular disease or at least two obesity complications or risk factors for cardiovascular disease; participants with chronic kidney disease were eligible if they also had a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater. Participants were randomly assigned by interactive response technology (1:1:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (up-titrated to 3·6 mg or 6·0 mg) or placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event (targeting 189 primary endpoint events). We assessed the non-inferiority of pooled survodutide compared with placebo with a margin of 1·65 for the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio (HR). Efficacy and safety analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of survodutide or placebo. The primary analysis was performed according to the treatment-regimen estimand, which assessed treatment effects regardless of any early discontinuation of survodutide or placebo, temporary stop, the use of protocol-prohibited obesity medications, or a prolonged dose-escalation period. This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06077864.
sections.results: From Nov 20, 2023, to Nov 8, 2024, we screened 7753 participants, of whom 5530 (71·3%) participants were recruited and randomly assigned to treatment. 23 (0·4%) participants were not treated; 1836 (33·3%) of 5507 participants received survodutide 3·6 mg, 1835 (33·3%) received 6·0 mg, and 1836 (33·3%) received placebo; 2194 (39·8%) were female, 3313 (60·2%) were male, and 4332 (78·7%) were White. Median time in study was 22·0 months (IQR 20·1-23·7). 1029 (56·0%) in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 1039 (56·6%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg group, and 1083 (59·0%) in the placebo group remained on treatment until study closeout. The primary endpoint occurred in 136 (3·7%) of 3671 participants in the survodutide group and in 76 (4·1%) 1836 participants in the placebo group (HR 0·89 [95% CI 0·67-1·18; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Adverse events occurred in 1708 (93·0%) of 1836 participants with survodutide 3·6 mg, 1708 (93·1%) of 1835 with survodutide 6·0 mg, and 1571 (85·6%) of 1836 with placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with survodutide than in the placebo group (nausea occurred in 882 [48·0%] of 1836 participants in the 3·6 mg group and 900 [49·0%] of 1835 in the 6·0 mg group vs 223 [12·1%] of 1836 in the placebo group, and vomiting occurred in 582 [31·7%] participants in the 3·6 mg group and 623 [34·0%] in the 6·0 mg group vs 89 [4·8%] in the placebo group). Gastrointestinal adverse events leading to treatment discontinuations occurred in 354 (19·3%) participants in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 (20·8%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 34 (1·9%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates across treatment groups (413 [22·5%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 [20·8%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 439 [23·9%] in the placebo group). Fatal adverse events were similar across treatment groups (16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 11 [0·6%] in the placebo group) and were primarily due to cardiac disorders (six [0·3%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, seven [0·4%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and six [0·3%] in the placebo group).
sections.conclusion: In participants with obesity with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease or at increased risk of cardiovascular disease, survodutide was not associated with increased risk for the primary composite endpoint of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event compared with placebo. This cardiovascular safety trial provides clinicians with reassuring data that treatment with survodutide, a novel glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.

sections.objective: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH.
sections.methods: We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete.
sections.results: Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]).
sections.conclusion: Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH.

items.title: Reconstructing developmental and disease progression with sample-level embeddings.
items.abstract: Single-cell genomics is transformative for characterizing cellular heterogeneity, but many biological questions require comparing samples rather than individual cells. Typical analyses compare "case" and "control" groups, ignoring sample-level variation within them. Here, we present scSLIDE (single-cell sample-level inference using density estimation), a framework that transforms each sample's single-cell data into a compact profile describing where its cells are distributed in high-dimensional space. By comparing these density profiles, scSLIDE calculates embeddings to characterize variation across samples. We implement scSLIDE in version 6 of our Seurat package and apply it to COVID-19 infection, Alzheimer's disease, and zebrafish embryogenesis. scSLIDE reveals patient subgroups, reconstructs disease trajectories, and identifies coordinated cellular programs across samples. We discover separable axes of infection and severity, a trajectory of Alzheimer's progression, and embryonic "pseudostages" that vary across and within time points. Our results demonstrate how case-control analyses collapse rich biological variation into binary labels and how sample-level embedding represents a powerful analytical alternative.

items.title: ANGPTL4 Inhibition in Adults with Elevated Triglyceride Levels.

sections.objective: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) inhibits lipoprotein lipase and regulates triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism. MAR001 is a monoclonal antibody against ANGPTL4 that is being evaluated for lowering triglyceride levels.
sections.methods: We conducted a two-part, phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. In part A, the focus of this report, we enrolled adults who had a nonfasting triglyceride level of at least 175 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 35 mg per deciliter at initial screening, followed by a fasting triglyceride level of at least 150 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 30 mg per deciliter on confirmatory screening. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive MAR001 at a dose of 300, 450, or 900 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 24 weeks. The primary end point was the percent change from baseline in the fasting triglyceride level at week 12, reported as the difference between each MAR001 dose group and the placebo group (placebo-adjusted change).
sections.results: A total of 236 participants were enrolled in the trial, with 177 assigned to receive MAR001 and 59 to receive placebo; a total of 235 participants received at least one dose of MAR001 or placebo and were included in the primary efficacy analyses. The mean age of the participants was 60.4 years, and 39% were women. The median triglyceride level at baseline was 249.5 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 210.0 to 313.0). At week 12, in an intention-to-treat analysis, the placebo-adjusted least-squares mean percent changes in the fasting triglyceride level were -39.1 percentage points, -40.5 percentage points, and -45.3 percentage points for the 300-mg, 450-mg, and 900-mg doses, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Adverse events occurred in 123 of 177 participants (69%) in the pooled MAR001 group and in 45 of 58 participants (78%) in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: Inhibition of ANGPTL4 with MAR001 significantly reduced fasting triglyceride levels at 12 weeks. (Funded by Marea Therapeutics; TYDAL-TIMI 78 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07028749.).

items.title: Human amniotic membrane transplantation for macular hole-associated retinal detachment: A systematic review of outcomes in refractory and complex cases.
items.abstract: We systematically review the anatomical and functional outcomes of human amniotic membrane (hAM) transplantation in the surgical management of macular hole-associated retinal detachment (MHRD). We conducted systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL for studies published from January, 2018, to March, 2026, reporting the use of hAM for MHRD. Primary outcomes included macular hole (MH) closure rate, retinal reattachment rate, and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) change. Risk of bias was assessed using JBI Critical Appraisal Checklists. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We included 18 studies encompassing approximately 196 eyes (12 case series, 3 case reports, 2 comparative studies, 1 prospective comparative). No randomized controlled trials were identified. The overall MH closure rate ranged from 70% to 100% across studies, with most series reporting closure rates above 90%. Retinal reattachment was achieved in 91.7% to 100% of cases. Mean BCVA improved significantly in the majority of studies, with the greatest improvement observed in the retinal detachment subgroup. Cryopreserved hAM with subretinal placement was the most commonly used technique, although epiretinal placement of lyophilized membranes showed comparable results. Graft dislocation or contraction occurred in 0% to 25% of cases. No major adverse events such as endophthalmitis, rejection, or significant inflammation were reported. We concluded that hAM transplantation appears to be a safe and effective rescue option for MHRD, particularly in cases where conventional approaches such as inverted ILM flap have failed or are not feasible, including recurrent MHRD in highly myopic eyes, cases with unavailable residual ILM, and complex retinal detachments with limited surgical alternatives. The evidence is limited to case series and case reports; randomized controlled trials are warranted to establish the comparative efficacy of hAM versus alternative techniques.

items.title: Late-onset filtering bleb complications: A review.
items.abstract: Late-onset filtering bleb dysfunction remains an important determinant of long-term outcomes following glaucoma filtration surgery. Although trabeculectomy provides sustained intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, progressive changes in bleb architecture and wound healing can result in filtration failure, hypotony, leakage, ocular discomfort, and sight-threatening infection. This review examines the clinical characteristics, underlying mechanisms, assessment, prevention, and management of late-onset bleb complications, with emphasis on individualized, mechanism-directed care. Standardized bleb grading systems facilitate documentation of morphology and longitudinal assessment. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography and ultrasound biomicroscopy complement clinical examination by delineating bleb architecture and identifying potential sites of outflow obstruction, while optical coherence tomography angiography offers an evolving approach to evaluating bleb vascularity. Elevated IOP may arise from internal ostial obstruction, scleral flap adhesion, subconjunctival fibrosis, or encapsulation. Management depends on the site and extent of dysfunction and includes medical therapy, laser intervention, antifibrotic-augmented needling, and surgical revision. Conversely, excessive filtration and compromised conjunctival integrity may cause persistent hypotony, bleb leakage, and hypotony-related structural changes. Treatment ranges from selected conservative measures to compression sutures, conjunctival advancement, and tissue grafting, according to the underlying defect and associated complications. Bleb-related infection requires urgent recognition and treatment, with management determined by the extent of intraocular involvement. Related complications following glaucoma drainage device implantation, nonpenetrating surgery, and subconjunctival microstent procedures are also considered. Successful long-term care requires balancing adequate aqueous drainage against the risks of overfiltration, tissue fragility, and infection. Lifelong surveillance, patient education, and timely intervention remain central to preserving visual function. Future advances in quantitative imaging, targeted wound modulation, and safer filtration strategies may improve the durability and safety of bleb-dependent glaucoma surgery.

items.title: Intravenous pulse methylprednisolone versus placebo for ethambutol-induced optic neuropathy (EtON): A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial.

sections.objective: Ethambutol-induced optic neuropathy (EtON) is a dose-dependent adverse drug effect that may cause irreversible visual impairment, with no established therapeutic interventions beyond drug cessation. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of high-dose, short-term intravenous methylprednisolone (IVMP) among patients with EtON.
sections.methods: This was a prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial (RCT) conducted at a tertiary care center in India (March 2021 to August 2024). A total of 100 patients with EtON were randomized (1:1) using block randomization. Participants received either high-dose IVMP (1gram per day for 5 days) or placebo, alongside standard-of-care therapy.
sections.results: At 6 months, 36 (72.0%) patients in the IVMP arm versus 23 (46.0%) in the placebo arm achieved an improvement of two or more lines in BCVA (p=0.008). However, the between-group difference in mean final BCVA was not statistically significant (0.54 (0.6) vs 0.61 (0.6), p=0.534). Significant improvement in visual field parameters was noted in IVMP arm: mean MD (-9.40 vs -13.99 (mean difference: 4.59, 95% CI: 1.35-7.83)) and mean VFI (71.27 vs 62.35 (mean difference: 8.92; 95% CI: 0.20-17.65)). Adjusted analysis confirmed improvement in visual outcomes with IVMP (adjusted risk ratio: 1.62; 95% CI: 1.14, 2.29), consistent across subgroups. No serious treatment-related adverse events were observed.
sections.conclusion: Short-term high-dose IVMP administration was associated with a greater proportion of BCVA responders and better visual field parameters in patients with EtON. This is the first RCT to evaluate the role of corticosteroids in EtON. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger trials.
sections.other: Patients reporting visual loss while receiving ethambutol and diagnosed with EtON using a pre-defined diagnostic criteria were enrolled. The primary endpoint was two or more lines improvement in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) on Snellen's chart (equivalent to at least ten letters on the logMAR) at 6 months. Secondary endpoints included improvement in mean deviation (MD) and visual field index (VFI) on automated perimetry, along with safety, and adjusted treatment effects.

items.title: Mycetoma in the United States: A Clinical Review.
items.abstract: Mycetoma is a neglected chronic granulomatous infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue caused by filamentous bacteria (actinomycetoma) or fungi (eumycetoma). Although classically associated with tropical and subtropical regions, cases have been reported in the United States and the disease is underrecognized, leading to misdiagnosis and delayed treatment. This clinical review synthesizes United States-focused evidence on mycetoma epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, and management. In the United States, mycetoma may be acquired abroad or locally, particularly in warmer regions, and reported demographic patterns differ from endemic areas, with cases often affecting older and urban populations. Clinically, it usually presents as a slowly progressive, painless subcutaneous nodule with draining sinuses and grain-containing discharge. Accurate distinction between actinomycetoma and eumycetoma is essential for appropriate treatment. Diagnosis relies on early collection of grains and deep tissue for histopathology and culture, with bedside microscopy as an adjunct, and imaging to define disease extent and bone involvement. Actinomycetoma is managed with prolonged antibiotics and is often cured without surgery, whereas eumycetoma typically requires long-term antifungal therapy plus surgical excision, with higher recurrence risk and rates of amputation.

items.title: Prognosis of Patients with Delayed Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Rupture after Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Multicentre Retrospective Study in France.

sections.objective: The majority of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) undergo endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture.
sections.methods: A multicentre retrospective study of patients who presented with ruptured AAA after successful EVAR between 2007 and 2022 at 22 academic hospitals was conducted. The index EVAR procedures were performed between 2002 and 2020. Data were extracted from electronic hospital records and computed tomography scans. Death during follow up was ascertained using the French register of deceased persons. Survival probabilities at 30, 90, and 365 days were estimated with Kaplan-Meier estimators. Cox proportional hazards survival regression was used to identify determinants associated with increased risk of death.
sections.results: One hundred and nine patients (96 men) were included, with a mean age of 79.1 ± 9 years at the time of rupture. The median time from index EVAR to rupture was 50 months (range 0 - 179 months). Sixty-seven patients had open surgery (of which 37% underwent suprarenal cross clamping), 39 received endovascular treatment, and three underwent hybrid repair. Overall mortality was 26.6% at thirty days, increasing to 33.9% at ninety days, and 41.3% at 1 year. Neither the type of endoleak nor the type of repair was significantly associated with risk of death during follow up. Post-operative complications were frequent, including renal complications (44.0%), major haemorrhage (22.9%), respiratory distress (19.3%), and mesenteric ischaemia (6%).
sections.conclusion: This study presented a large multicentre series of patients treated for ruptured AAA after EVAR. Despite considerable progress in stent graft technology, EVAR offers little protection in the event of late rupture, even among patients with type II endoleak only. The mortality rate in this study is within the range of those published based on de novo AAA rupture.

items.title: Leadership, Teamwork, and Healthcare Economics Training in Vascular Surgery Residency Programs: A National Cross-Specialty FREIDA Analysis.

sections.objective: To compare reported training in leadership, interprofessional teamwork, and healthcare economics among vascular surgery residency programs and 10 other surgical and procedural specialties.
sections.methods: We reviewed FREIDA educational-benefits data for 11 specialties on June 20, 2025, excluding programs without these data. Vascular surgery residency programs were compared with the highest-reporting specialty in each category and with the remaining 10 specialties combined using two-sided Fisher exact tests.
sections.results: Of 1,717 programs, 810 (47.2%) reported educational-benefits data, including 36 of 78 (46.2%) vascular surgery residency programs. Among these 36 programs, 13 (36.1%) reported leadership training, 20 (55.6%) formal interprofessional teamwork programs, 19 (52.8%) healthcare economics instruction, and 6 (16.7%) reported all three. Compared with the highest-reporting specialty, vascular surgery residency programs had lower reporting rates for leadership (36.1% vs 56.3% in obstetrics and gynecology; P = .030), teamwork (55.6% vs 80.2% in obstetrics and gynecology; P = .003), economics (52.8% vs 80.8% in interventional radiology; P = .009), and all three (16.7% vs 35.5% in obstetrics and gynecology; P = .033). Comparisons with the remaining 10 specialties combined were not statistically significant for leadership (36.1% vs 51.0%; P = .089), teamwork (55.6% vs 67.7%; P = .147), or economics (52.8% vs 59.7%; P = .488).
sections.conclusion: Vascular surgery residency programs ranked among the lowest specialties in reported SBP-aligned training, with only 16.7% reporting all three domains. Although pooled comparisons were not statistically significant, these findings highlight an opportunity for specialty-wide standardization of SBP education.

items.title: Post-approval study preliminary 1-month outcomes of the first 100 patients treated with an off-the-shelf multibranch aortic device.

sections.objective: To report the preliminary 1-month outcomes from the post-approval study of the first 100 patients treated with the GORE® EXCLUDER® Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE).
sections.methods: This multicenter, nonrandomized, prospective study of the TAMBE aortic component included endovascular repair of an aortic disease involving the visceral vessels. Demographics, core-lab adjudicated imaging characteristics, perioperative metrics, and postoperative 1-month outcomes are reported.
sections.results: The first 100 patients treated were 30% female, 81% white, and the median was age 74 years. Anatomic classifications included 48 patients (49.0%) with Extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA), 21 (21.4%) with pararenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), 12 (12.2%) with juxtarenal AAA, and 17 patients with post dissection pathology (n=11) or 'other' (n=6). Enrollment and treatment of 45.0% of the patients were at sites without prior TAMBE device experience. Prior aortic surgery was noted in 48.0% of patients treated. For patients with Extent I-III TAAA (n=22), staging of the TAMBE procedure was planned with initial proximal thoracic endovascular aortic repair in 7 patients (31.8%). Median aneurysm diameter was 6.2 cm. The GORE® VIABAHN® VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis was used in all patients, with additional use of a VIABAHN® self-expanding stent in six patients. Intentional non-use of one or more portals (with planned plug occlusion) was a strategy used in 15 (15.0%) patients. Median procedure time was 280 minutes, and median length of stay was four days with 83 patients (83.8%) discharged to home. Branch target vessel technical success rate was 98.9% (average of 1.39 stents into the celiac, 1.44 superior mesenteric artery, 1.62 right renal, and 1.59 left renal per portal). Three patients (3.0%) died, all were procedure related. Major adverse events in 8 patients (8.1%, 3 had ≥1 event) included 1 (1.0%) respiratory failure, 4 (4.0%) permanent paraplegia, 4 (4.0%) renal function decline, and 1 (1.0%) bowel ischemia. No patient experienced a major stroke, aneurysm rupture, or myocardial infarction. A total of eight Type 1c or Type IIIa/IIIc endoleaks were detected in 6 (6.1%) patients. No conversion to open-surgical repair, rupture, or device migration/integrity issues were reported.
sections.conclusion: The preliminary analysis of the FDA-mandated post-approval study 1-month outcomes in this prospective multicenter cohort treated with the TAMBE device demonstrates applicability to more extensive thoracoabdominal pathology with similar outcomes to the pivotal trial. Distinct findings for the TAMBE device in the real-world include successful treatment of post-dissection aneurysms, increased staging strategies for spinal cord protection with low paraplegia rates, and rapid adoption by many sites that did not participate in the pivotal trial.

items.title: Revascularization Outcomes in Patients with Femoropopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease Presenting with Claudication.

sections.objective: Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and optimal medical therapy (OMT), including smoking cessation, are first-line treatments for claudication. Revascularization is reserved for quality-of-life-limiting symptoms refractory to conservative management; however, the optimal revascularization strategy for femoropopliteal disease remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy (ET) and bypass strategies in patients undergoing revascularization for claudication.
sections.methods: We analyzed Vascular Quality Initiative data (2016-2024) for patients undergoing first-time elective revascularization for femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease (PAD) presenting with claudication. Three 1:1 propensity score-matched cohorts were constructed: ET vs single-segment great saphenous vein (SSGSV) bypass, ET vs prosthetic graft (PG) bypass, and PG vs SSGSV bypass. The primary outcome was one-year freedom from persistent claudication. Secondary outcomes included one-year loss of patency, reintervention, and all-cause mortality. Outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression.
sections.results: We identified 27,335 patients (30,483 limbs): ET 27,111 (88.9%), SSGSV 1,399 (4.6%), and PG 1,973 (6.5%). Matching yielded 1,294 ET-SSGSV pairs, 1,801 ET-PG pairs, and 1,242 PG-SSGSV pairs with well-balanced baseline characteristics. At one year, symptom-free rates were 92.0% for SSGSV, 90.0% for PG, and 89.6% for ET. Compared with SSGSV, ET was associated with a higher risk of persistent claudication at one-year (HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.10-2.00; P=0.010). No significant differences in one-year symptom relief were observed between ET and PG or between PG and SSGSV. Across all matched comparisons, loss of patency, reintervention, and mortality did not differ significantly.
sections.conclusion: SET and OMT should remain first-line therapy for claudication. Among patients proceeding to revascularization after unsuccessful conservative care, SSGSV bypass was associated with greater symptom relief than ET at one year, while all strategies achieved high symptom-free rates (≥89%). ET and PG demonstrated comparable outcomes across symptom relief, patency, reintervention, and survival. There were no significant differences between PG and SSGSV. Given vein-preservation considerations and procedural invasiveness in claudication, strategy selection should be individualized to anatomy, comorbidities and patient goals. Prospective studies are needed to clarify long-term durability, and quality-of-life effects.

items.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
items.abstract: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confocal microscopy. Despite the wide diffusion of digital cameras, smartphones, and high-end slit-lamp systems, ocular surface photography (OSP) remains hampered by the absence of standardised acquisition and processing protocols. The convex, aspheric geometry of the ocular surface, off-axis illumination, peripheral defocus, automatic colour correction, and pupil-driven exposure variation in retroillumination limit reproducibility, inter-device comparability, and clinical utility. In this review we critically appraise current OSP applications across major ocular surface conditions (dry eye disease, conjunctival hyperaemia, infectious keratitis, ocular surface burns, and ocular surface neoplasia), mapping the hardware, software, and reproducibility limitations that constrain clinical practice. We then examine how these limitations propagate into artificial intelligence (AI) development, where the absence of large, well-annotated, demographically diverse OSP datasets, together with the lack of reproducible quantitative phenotypes and reliable labels, is now the principal bottleneck to clinically deployable models; we discuss patient-level data partitioning and external validation, and outline how deep learning, federated learning and foundation models can both utilise and improve OSP. Finally, we propose a minimum acquisition and dataset specification, tiered by clinical setting from research to community screening, and a staged roadmap that combines hardware standardisation (focus-stacked, illumination-controlled, colour-calibrated acquisition), interoperable metadata-rich storage (DICOM where infrastructure permits), quantitative phenotype definition, and diverse international dataset collaborations, so that the ocular surface can benefit from quantitative imaging and AI as other areas of ophthalmology have begun to.

items.title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.

sections.objective: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.
sections.results: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).
sections.conclusion: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

items.title: The IgG4ward! Foundation guidelines on the treatment of IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease is a chronic, immune-mediated, systemic condition that presents as tumour-like masses. Since publication of the last international consensus statement on the treatment of IgG4-related disease in 2015, the related literature has expanded considerably, with two phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trials published within the past 2 years. This foundation of evidence for treatment decisions justified new, dedicated treatment guidelines. 62 investigators-comprising 52 physicians, one medical reference librarian, eight patients, and one caregiver from 15 countries across six continents-were assembled to form a treatment guidelines group. The physicians had a broad range of specialties and patient representation spanned the full spectrum of organ involvement. The treatment guidelines group generated 183 candidate questions, which were consolidated into 40 final questions approved by the IgG4ward! Advisory Board. These questions formed the basis of a systematic literature search, led by a medical reference librarian, which informed the development of 28 treatment statements. Supporting evidence for each statement was independently graded using the 2011 Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence framework. The 52 physicians voted electronically on their level of agreement with each statement; consensus required more than 80% to agree or strongly agree with the statement, and was reached for 22 of the 28 statements. The evidence base reflects marked recent progress due to the publication of phase 3 clinical trials, although most statements still rely on low-level evidence. This effort provides cohesive, consensus-based guidelines from a geographically and professionally diverse group of experts in IgG4-related disease, reflecting the evolution in the field since 2015. Despite this progress, important knowledge gaps remain, and are highlighted to guide future research.

items.title: Naegleria fowleri in a warming world: epidemiology, genotypic distribution, management challenges, and priorities for public health action.
items.abstract: Naegleria fowleri causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, a fatal infection with profound implications for global health burden and water safety. Rising global temperatures and ageing water infrastructure are expanding the ecological range of this pathogen, increasing exposure risk in both high-income and resource-constrained settings. The infection mainly occurs through contact with warm freshwater and brackish waters and inhalation of cyst-laden dust; however, surveillance systems remain fragmented and under-resourced, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Diagnosis is often delayed or made post-mortem, and survival is exceedingly rare. In this Review, we synthesised the current knowledge on global epidemiology, genotypic distribution, and environmental drivers of N fowleri emergence and identified key gaps in monitoring, water treatment, and governance. We propose that climate-resilient water safety strategies, integrated surveillance, and cross-sectoral collaboration are urgently needed to mitigate the risk of Nfowleri exposure and to minimise future cases of primary amoebic meningoencephalitis. Strengthening global health systems to address this emerging threat will require coordinated investment, policy innovation, and research to close knowledge gaps and protect clinically vulnerable populations.

items.title: Prioritising malaria interventions to maximise health: the role of economic evaluation.
items.abstract: Malaria decision makers face difficult choices about how to allocate scarce resources to complex intervention packages across heterogeneous areas and populations. Such decisions must balance competing objectives, including health maximisation, equity, and political acceptability. The current WHO-supported subnational tailoring process improves on uniform national planning by targeting interventions to local contexts based on determinants of malaria risk. However, the WHO guidance does not provide a transparent, systematic framework for weighing the health benefits of malaria interventions against the resources required, within budget constraints. Health economic evaluation, the science of maximising health with finite resources, should be central to malaria decision making, thereby informing decision makers about health-maximising choices even when other considerations take precedence. We propose improvements, including a revised prioritisation approach explicitly informed by economic evaluation principles. We also discuss how research activities can better support health maximisation and how all stakeholders can contribute to improving malaria priority setting.

items.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.

sections.objective: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear.
sections.methods: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy.
sections.results: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

items.title: Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest.

sections.objective: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking.
sections.methods: We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome).
sections.results: From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80).
sections.conclusion: Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).

items.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.

sections.objective: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity.
sections.methods: In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand.
sections.results: A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

items.title: HIV, obesity, and stigma: lessons for programmes, policy, and practice.
items.abstract: HIV has generated four decades of activism, research, and policy reform that produced measurement tools, theoretical frameworks, and consensus that stigma undermines prevention, delays treatment, and entrenches inequity. Weight stigma follows a strikingly similar pattern, operating through visibility, assumptions of personal control, and moralised concern, and is now recognised as a public health priority in its own right. These two forms of stigma increasingly intersect in the same bodies: antiretroviral therapy, particularly newer regimens, is associated with substantial weight gain, so that people once stigmatised for wasting now risk a second, contradictory stigma for excess weight. This intersection is complex; internalised stigma from either condition can resurface long after apparent resolution, even when viral suppression has been reached or after major weight loss. HIV and obesity differ in diagnostic certainty, visibility, permanence, and the origins of activism and legal protection, which helps explain why HIV stigma reduction remains decades ahead. Applying the Health Stigma and Discrimination Framework to this intersection clarifies shared drivers, facilitators, manifestations, and outcomes. Community leadership, rejection of false prevention-versus-treatment trade-offs, equitable access to pharmacotherapy, and integration of obesity care into existing HIV services offer a practical path towards reducing both stigmas.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: B cells play a central role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and are a therapeutic target. We therefore assessed the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β, a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, in patients with active SLE.
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial, we enrolled patients who were aged 18-80 years, fulfilled the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology-American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for SLE, and had active disease (defined as a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 [SLEDAI-2K] score of 8 or more and positivity for antinuclear antibodies or anti-double stranded DNA antibodies) at 30 tertiary hospitals in China. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to receive obinutuzumab β or placebo, stratified by SLEDAI-2K score and 24-h urine protein level. Patients, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment allocation. Patients received intravenous infusions of obinutuzumab β (1000 mg) or placebo on days 1, 15, 169, 183, 365, and 379. All patients maintained their background standard therapy. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients with an SLE Responder Index (SRI)-4 response at week 12 assessed in all patients who were randomly assigned and received at least one dose of study treatment (ie, the full analysis set). Safety was assessed in all patients who received any study treatment and had at least one post-dose safety assessment (ie, the safety analysis set) over 52 weeks. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05796206) and is complete. People with lived experience were not involved as research partners in this study.
sections.results: Between May 26, 2023, and July 29, 2024, 171 patients were screened for eligibility. Of these, 123 patients were randomly assigned to receive obinutuzumab β (n=61) or placebo (n=62) and were included in both the full analysis set and safety analysis sets. The mean age was 36·1 years (SD 10·3). 115 (93%) of 123 patients were female, eight (7%) were male, and 117 (95%) were Han Chinese ethnicity. At week 12, 32 (52%) of 61 patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 21 (34%) of 62 in the placebo group had an SRI-4 response (adjusted risk difference 19 percentage points, 95% CI 3-36; p=0·022). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 (20%) patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 14 (23%) in the placebo group. One fatal treatment-emergent adverse event (sepsis) occurred in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: Obinutuzumab β plus standard therapy improved SRI-4 response at week 12 in Chinese patients with active SLE, with a generally manageable safety profile over 52 weeks. These phase 2 findings support further evaluation and longer-term safety follow-up.

items.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease.

sections.objective: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown.
sections.methods: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo. The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.
sections.results: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
sections.results: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

items.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease.

sections.objective: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized.
sections.methods: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks.
sections.results: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group.
sections.conclusion: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.

sections.objective: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
sections.results: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups.
sections.conclusion: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

items.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

sections.objective: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion.
