Thirty-day outcomes were examined.ResultsFemoropopliteal bypass was the most common procedure followed by femoral-distal bypass for both vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Vascular surgeons were more likely to perform femoral-distal procedures and use single-segment saphenous vein grafts (SSSV) for both claudication and CLTI. Vascular surgeons were less likely to use other non-SSSV conduits for claudication patients (40.6% vs 54.6%, p < 0.01), but no difference in CLTI (38.9%% vs 40.1%, p = 0.74). There was no significant difference in 30-day mortality/morbidities between surgeons for either claudication or CLTI. However, 30-day major amputation for CLTI was significantly better with vascular surgeons (3.0% vs 7.5%, p < 0.01). In CLTI patients, after correcting for operation type and conduit usage, vascular surgeons continued to be associated with lower major amputation (aOR = 0.46, 95 CI = 0.29-0.72, p < 0.01).ConclusionVascular surgeons have better limb salvage than non-vascular surgeons. This could not be explained by the higher use of SSSV; thus, other factors such as surgical skill may account for better outcomes.

items.title: The Impact of Undernutrition on Post-Tuberculosis Lung-Function: A Prospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Undernutrition is the leading driver of tuberculosis worldwide, yet its effect on the lungs of people who complete treatment is not well defined.
sections.methods: Adults (≥18 years) with drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis were enrolled at treatment initiation in India. We measured associations of baseline body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and premorbid BMI with spirometry, chest radiograph score, six-minute walk distance and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire score. Plasma IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-6 were measured at baseline and month 2; counterfactual mediation analysis partitioned the effect of undernutrition on lung function into direct and inflammation-mediated components.
sections.results: Of 156 participants analyzed, 76 (48.7%) had a ventilatory defect; 52 (33.3%) had airflow obstruction and 31 (19.9%) had restrictive spirometry. Each 1 kg/m2 higher baseline BMI was associated with lower odds of any ventilatory defect (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.90), and BMI below 16 kg/m2 carried five-fold higher odds than BMI ≥18.5 kg/m2 (aOR, 5.08; 95% CI, 1.76-16.02). MUAC and premorbid BMI showed similar associations. Lower BMI was associated with restrictive spirometry (aOR, 0.74 per kg/m2; 95% CI, 0.59-0.89) but not airflow obstruction (aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.80-1.03). Undernourished participants had higher baseline IL-6, which mediated 32% (FEV1) and 49% (FVC) of the association with impaired lung function.
sections.conclusion: Undernutrition before and at treatment initiation is a potentially modifiable determinant of post-treatment lung impairment, with systemic inflammation mediating part of the effect. Nutritional assessment belongs in routine tuberculosis care, and nutritional support should be tested to prevent lung-function impairment in tuberculosis survivors.
sections.other: Among adults treated for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis, is undernutrition associated with worse post-treatment lung function, radiographic severity, exercise capacity and respiratory quality of life, and does systemic inflammation mediate that association?

items.title: The impact of removing prior authorization for guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medications for COPD: a population-based cohort study.

sections.objective: Most patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) do not receive maintenance inhaled therapies in concordance with evidence-based clinical guidelines. Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), the recommended first-line therapy, is underused, while inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) are often used in discordance with clinical guidelines. In July 2020, British Columbia's (BC) universal drug plan removed prior authorization requirements for coverage for LAMA medications and restricted coverage for ICS/LABA.
sections.methods: In a population-based cohort study using provincial administrative health data, we identified patients with COPD using a validated case definition and followed them from January 2019 (18 months pre-policy) to December 2022 (30 months post-policy). Using interrupted time series analysis, we evaluated the monthly proportion of patients filling a prescription for ICS/LABA and LAMA, mean canisters dispensed, proportion of days covered (PDC), rates of ICS/LABA discontinuation, LAMA (re)initiation, and initiating LAMA as first maintenance therapy. We report absolute differences between observed and counterfactual outcomes at study end.
sections.results: The cohort included 47,583 patients with COPD (mean 71.5 years, 46.5% female, 31.7 months mean follow-up). Thirty months post-policy change, ICS/LABA use decreased by -1.3% (95% CI -2.4, -0.3) and LAMA use increased by 0.8% (95% CI 0.1, 1.6). There was no significant change in the number of ICS/LABA canisters dispensed, PDC or proportion discontinuing ICS/LABA. Mean LAMA canisters dispensed increased by 9.8 per 1,000 patients (95% CI 1.0, 18.7) and PDC increased by 1.5% (95% CI 0.5, 2.4). (Re)initiation of LAMA or initiating LAMA as maintenance therapy increased by 0.2% (95% CI 0.02, 0.3) and 34.8% (95% CI 22.3, 48.6), respectively. Total combined drug costs did not change.
sections.conclusion: Changes to drug coverage in BC were associated with improved guideline-concordant medication use.
sections.other: What is the impact of this policy change on guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medication use?

items.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis.

sections.objective: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF.
sections.methods: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence.
sections.results: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD.
sections.conclusion: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.
sections.other: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations?

items.title: Three-Year Outcomes of Trabeculotomy vs Combined Trabeculotomy-Trabeculectomy for Primary Congenital Glaucoma.

sections.objective: To determine whether trabeculotomy is noninferior to combined trabeculotomy-trabeculectomy (CTT) for primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) with a horizontal corneal diameter (HCD) of 12-14 mm.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomized, controlled noninferiority trial. Children from birth through 3 years of age with PCG, a HCD of 12 to 14 mm, and no previous intraocular or laser surgery were eligible. Two hundred and forty-eight children were enrolled from January 2015 through April 2021, and the final follow-up was completed in April 2024. One eligible eye per child was randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to trabeculotomy or CTT.
sections.results: Overall, 124 children were assigned to trabeculotomy (mean age, 9.8 months; 76.6% male) and 124 to CTT (mean age, 9.9 months; 68.5% male). In the intention-to-treat population, qualified success at 36 months was achieved in 102 of 124 eyes (82.3%) in the trabeculotomy group and 105 of 124 eyes (84.7%) in the CTT group (risk difference: -2.4%; 95%CI, -11.7 to 6.9; Pnoninferiority= 0.004). Corresponding rates in the per-protocol population were 90.3% and 92.9%, respectively (risk difference -2.6%; 95%CI -10.3 to 4.9; Pnoninferiority< 0.001). Mean IOP reduction was -12.1 mm Hg (95%CI, -12.9 to -11.4) and -13.2 mm Hg (95%CI, -14.0 to -12.4) in the trabeculotomy and CTT groups, respectively (P=0.067). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Adverse events occurred in 56 children (45.2%) in the trabeculotomy group and 67 (54.0%) in the CTT group (P = 0.162). Hyphema was the most common adverse event in both groups, and most cases resolved spontaneously.
sections.conclusion: Trabeculotomy was noninferior to CTT for qualified surgical success at 36 months in PCG patients with a HCD of 12-14 mm. These findings suggest that trabeculotomy may be an alternative to CTT in this population.
sections.other: The primary outcome was qualified surgical success at 36 months, defined as an intraocular pressure (IOP) of 5 to 21 mmHg with or without glaucoma medications, without vision-threatening complications or additional glaucoma surgery. The noninferiority margin was -15 percentage points. Exploratory secondary outcomes included changes in IOP, ocular morphometric and functional outcomes, and adverse events.

items.title: Systematic overestimation using in silico-driven curation in a population database caused reevaluation of the genetic prevalence of Alport Syndrome.

sections.objective: A landmark study by Gibson and coworkers in 2021 estimated that one in 106 individuals carry a predicted pathogenic COL4A3 or COL4A4 variant, suggesting autosomal dominant Alport syndrome is massively underdiagnosed. However, pathogenicity of all triple-helical Glycine substitutions was inferred using in silico tools, which may overestimate prevalence.
sections.methods: COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 variants were extracted from population database gnomADv4.1.1 (about 800,000 individuals, including UK Biobank) and from a clinical exome cohort of 29,055 patients (Eurofins Biomnis), stratified into a kidney disease group (KIDNEY) of 8663 individuals and 20,392 individuals of a non-kidney control group (NON-KIDNEY). Three curation strategies were compared: a ClinVar-dependent model, an in silico-driven model adapted from Gibson, and an Expert Strategy combining stringent allele frequency thresholds, high-confidence loss-of-function filtering, and with ClinVar validation for missense variants. Estimates were validated against the control group and replicated in the non-UKB Biobank subset.
sections.results: Applied to gnomADv4.1.1, the Gibson methodology yielded one in 221, a 52% reduction from the original one in 106 (gnomADv2). The Expert Strategy estimated one in 283, validated in the NON-KIDNEY group (one in 295; concordance ratio 0.96), whereas Gibson inflated the control rate by 91% (one in 154 vs. one in 295). Glycine substitutions (COL4A3 p.Gly1277Ser odds ratio 0.95; COL4A4 p.Gly999Glu odds ratio 1.01) were misclassified by all in silico tools. Expert Strategy variants were found in one in 44 KIDNEY patients (odds ratio 6.76). Enrichment was unchanged by high-confidence loss-of-function restriction.
sections.conclusion: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome affects one in 283 individuals, one to two orders of magnitude above classical clinical estimates (one in 5,000 to one in 53,000), confirming underdiagnosis, but substantially lower than the Gibson estimate. These findings argue for downgrading the PM2 rarity criterion in collagenopathies. Systematic COL4A3/COL4A4 screening in chronic kidney disease is justified by a diagnostic yield of one in 44.

items.title: Modified immune cell therapy targets kidney-resident tertiary lymphoid structures and ameliorates murine lupus nephritis.

sections.objective: Modified immune cells (MIC), i.e. mononuclear cells challenged with mitomycin C can induce immunotolerance. MIC treatment has been successful in several animal models of autoimmunity and in clinical trials after solid organ transplantation, but the mechanism for reduced inflammation is not fully understood.
sections.methods: To investigate the efficacy of MIC therapy in lupus nephritis, splenocytes from syngeneic NZB/W F1 (BWF1) donor mice were incubated with mitomycin C, and then into BWF1 recipients at 25 weeks of age. Animals were followed for another five weeks to assess disease progression by histological, flow cytometric, and serological parameters. An in vitro phagocytosis assay was conducted to determine the clearance of MIC from 25 patients with lupus and from matched healthy individuals by autologous macrophages.
sections.results: In BWF1 mice, MIC therapy reduced the clinical burden of lupus nephritis disease progression with lower protein excretion and lower serum creatinine levels in the standard-dose compared to the control group. High-dose MIC therapy during active diseases showed no additional benefit. More than 86% of animals had dense lymphocytic aggregates close to the kidney pelvis. These tertiary lymphoid structures differed between MIC-treated animals and controls, with a loss of organization, loss of separation of B-cell and T-cell areas and disintegration of germinal centers after MIC treatment. In the peripheral blood, MIC-treated animals had higher numbers of CD19+CD5+CD1dhigh regulatory-like B lymphocytes. Although MIC treatment was beneficial, higher dosing offered no additional clinical benefit in mice. Macrophages from the patients with lupus efficiently cleared MIC in vitro, ruling out defective clearance as a limiting factor.
sections.conclusion: Our clinically applicable cell therapy approach has the potential to control lupus nephritis by specifically dampening deleterious autoimmune responses.

items.title: Ontogenically distinct macrophages occupy discrete kidney niches and contribute to monocyte recruitment in experimental crescentic glomerulonephritis.

sections.objective: Crescentic glomerulonephritis (cGN) is characterized by aggressive immune-mediated glomerular injury with prominent macrophage accumulation that correlates with disease severity. However, the distinct contributions of kidney-resident macrophages (KRMs) of different ontogenies remain poorly defined.
sections.methods: To explore this, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), reporter-based bone marrow chimeras, timed clodronate liposome treatment, and chemokine blockade to define the spatiotemporal dynamics and functional roles of macrophage populations in nephrotoxic serum nephritis (NTSN), a model of cGN.
sections.results: scRNA-seq of total kidney and CD45+ immune cells revealed that proliferating macrophages and infiltrating monocytes expanded sharply by day five and declined by day ten, indicating that local proliferation, in addition to monocyte recruitment, contributes substantially to early macrophage accumulation in NTSN. Two major KRM subpopulations were distinguished by high Ccr2 or Mrc1 expression, consistent with bone marrow and embryonically seeded, self-renewing KRM population, respectively. In Cx3cr1-GFP recipient mice reconstituted with Ccr2-RFP+ donor bone marrow, embryonic-derived GFP+ KRMs were enriched in the outer medulla and corticomedullary region, whereas donor-derived RFP+ monocytes/macrophages preferentially accumulated in the cortex, including within and around the inflamed glomeruli. A timed clodronate liposome regimen that preferentially reduced recipient-retained GFP+ KRMs decreased the cortical accumulation of RFP+ cells, albuminuria, and histologic kidney injury in NTSN mice. Cell-cell communication analysis identified macrophage-associated CCL12 expression, a murine ortholog of human CCL2, as a candidate mediator of cortical CCR2+ monocyte recruitment. CCL12 neutralization reduced cortical monocyte accumulation and ameliorated kidney damage in NTSN mice.
sections.conclusion: These findings indicate that ontogenically distinct and spatially segregated macrophage populations cooperate during early cGN and support further investigation of the CCR2 axis as a therapeutic target for macrophage-mediated kidney injury in cGN.

items.title: Associations between Antidiabetic Drug Classes and Aortic Aneurysm Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a potentially life threatening condition that often remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods. Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear. This study evaluated associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA.
sections.methods: This was a nationwide, population based, retrospective cohort study of adults with T2DM in Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database between 2009 and 2022. Associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with time varying medication exposure, adjusted for demographic characteristics, diabetes severity, comorbidities, tobacco related diagnoses, and concomitant medications. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were considered exploratory.
sections.results: Among 3 295 564 adults with T2DM (mean age 60.0 years; 52.8% men) followed for 8.5 ± 4.7 years, 45.5% received at least three antidiabetic drug classes. In multivariable time varying Cox models, metformin (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.82), thiazolidinediones (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 - 0.77), sulfonylureas/meglitinides (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 - 0.85), and α-glucosidase inhibitors (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77 - 0.89) were associated with lower AA risk. DPP-4 inhibitors (aHR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90 - 1.00), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), and glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 - 0.95) also showed inverse associations, whereas insulin use was associated with higher AA risk (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08 - 1.20). The inverse associations of conventional oral antidiabetic agents remained robust across sensitivity analyses. In contrast, the inverse associations for DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and GLP-1RAs were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in patients with an index date from 2011 onward.
sections.conclusion: In this nationwide T2DM cohort, conventional oral antidiabetic agents were consistently associated with a lower observed AA risk. Although newer glucose lowering therapies showed similar inverse associations, these findings were less robust and warrant cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

items.title: Baseline Macular OCT Thickness of Ocular Hypertensive Patients Improves Prediction of Glaucoma.

sections.objective: To determine whether baseline macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness add prognostic value for glaucomatous visual field (VF) damage in patients with ocular hypertension.
sections.methods: Retrospective clinical cohort study. 330 eyes of 235 patients with ocular hypertension, defined by intraocular pressure of 22 mmHg or higher or an International Classification of Diseases coded diagnosis, without repeatable glaucomatous VF damage at baseline. Eyes came from both the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study and a clinical cohort at the Shiley Eye Institute. Baseline GCIPL and cpRNFL thickness were measured from the first good-quality Cirrus optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular and optic-disc cubes. Clinical predictors were assessed with the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS)-European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) Risk Calculator. Repeatable glaucomatous VF damage required a Glaucoma Hemifield Test outside normal limits or a pattern standard deviation at the 5% level or worse on three consecutive reliable Humphrey 24-2 examinations.
sections.results: Glaucomatous VF damage developed in 47 of 330 eyes (14%) over a median 4.4 years. Adjusted for the Risk Calculator, thinner macular GCIPL was associated with conversion (hazard ratio [HR] 1.89 per 1-SD thinner; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.50 to 2.37; P < .001), and every macular sector was significant (HR 1.71 to 2.02). The Risk Calculator alone showed modest discrimination (Harrell C-index, 0.57). Adding macular GCIPL improved discrimination (ΔC +0.101; 95% CI, +0.022 to +0.220). Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22).
sections.conclusion: In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.
sections.other: Hazard ratios per 1 standard deviation (SD) of thinner global and sectoral GCIPL or cpRNFL, and the change in the Harrell concordance (C) index (ΔC) after adding each measure to the Risk Calculator.

items.title: Effect of Electronic Behavioral Nudges on Low-Value Preoperative Testing: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Robust randomized trials have demonstrated that routine testing before cataract surgery does not improve outcomes; however, despite this evidence and long-standing professional society recommendations discouraging routine testing, preoperative testing remains frequent in real-world practice, with most patients undergoing cataract surgery receiving at least 1 preoperative test. To measure whether electronic health record (EHR)-embedded, behavioral science-informed nudges reduce preoperative testing.
sections.methods: This pragmatic randomized clinical trial was conducted at a large academic health system (UCLA Health) in Los Angeles, California. Physicians performing preoperative evaluations were randomized to 1 of 3 EHR nudge alerts or usual care. All encounters with patients undergoing a preoperative visit with a randomized physician within 30 days of cataract surgery were silently enrolled. Patients were enrolled from June 24, 2021, to April 11, 2023. Data were analyzed from June 2020 (1 year prior to first enrollment) to April 2024 (1 year after last enrollment). The EHR interruptive alerts cited professional society recommendations against routine testing; each emphasized a different potential patient harm, including lack of safety benefit, financial burden, or psychological stress.
sections.results: During the enrollment period, 229 of 776 randomized physicians had 1 or more eligible encounter during which a patient was enrolled. Together, these clinicians had 1045 preoperative encounters during the intervention period with 967 unique patients. Mean (SD) patient age was 72.1 (9.1) years, and 595 encounters (56.9%) were with female patients. Mean (SD) signed preoperative testing rates decreased from 83% (29%) to 79% (31%) in the combined intervention arms vs 84% (30%) to 82% (31%) in the control arm. In mixed-effects models, exposure to any nudge was not associated with a reduction in overall testing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.34-1.34). In prespecified secondary analyses, 16% of orders were cancelled following exposure to a nudge, and the psychological stress nudge was associated with decreases in rates of complete blood cell count (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.75; P = .01) and electrocardiogram orders (aOR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.21-0.83; P = .01) vs control.
sections.conclusion: This randomized clinical trial of EHR nudges did not reach statistical significance on the primary outcome of overall preoperative testing. Secondary outcomes suggest future studies might consider the role of a psychological stress nudge in combination with other behavioral, workflow, and/or payment changes.
sections.other: The primary outcome was the change in the proportion of preoperative cataract surgery encounters with any signed testing order(s) between the 12-month period before the physicians' first encounter (enrollment) and the 12-month postencounter period. Secondary outcomes included order cancellation rates among clinicians exposed to the intervention, separate comparisons of each nudge, and analyses comparing orders for specific categories of tests.

items.title: Potential Disparities in Access to Adult Strabismus Care.

sections.objective: Adult strabismus impacts quality of life through diplopia, eye strain, and psychological burden. Access to care may be limited by various factors, yet disparities in adult strabismus care have not been examined nationally. To evaluate potential disparities in access to adult strabismus care across the US by practice type, insurance status, and county-level socioeconomic characteristics.
sections.methods: This national secret shopper study used standardized telephone calls to US pediatric ophthalmology practices identified through the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus and the American Academy of Ophthalmology that simulated appointment scheduling for an adult patients with strabismus. Of 1064 practices contacted, 1060 were included after excluding 4 clinics with disconnected phone numbers. These data were analyzed from August 2025 to September 2026.
sections.results: Overall, 23.8% (252 of 1060) of practices offered an appointment under at least 1 insurance scenario. Patients using Medicaid had a lower appointment success rate than those with commercial insurance (161 of 648 [24.8%] vs 91 of 194 [46.9%]; difference, -22.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -29.8 to -14.3; P < .001). In multivariable regression, other practice types (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.28-2.58; P = .001) and commercial insurance (aOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.67-3.33; P = .001) had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority counties (aOR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.45-0.97; P = .04) and lower median household income counties (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.44-0.93; P = .02) had lower odds. Among practices offering appointments, academic centers had longer wait times than other practices (mean [SD], 95.1 [59.3] days vs 57.0 [54.1] days; 38.1 days difference; 95% CI, 21.2-55.1; P < .001), as did lower-income counties (mean [SD], 78.6 [68.1] days vs 61.3 [52.6] days; -17.4 days difference; 95% CI, -33.3 to -1.4; P = .03).
sections.conclusion: This national secret shopper study identified potential disparities in adult strabismus care access. Commercial insurance and other practice types had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority and lower-income counties had reduced access and longer wait times. These findings highlight a potential unmet likely benefit of adult strabismus practitioners and support targeted policy interventions to improve equitable access to care.
sections.other: Practice type (academic vs other), insurance type (Medicaid vs commercial insurance), and county-level characteristics, including race and ethnicity majority, median household income, Area Deprivation Index (ADI), and Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Appointment success (ability to schedule appointment during call) and appointment wait time (days between call date and earliest available appointment).

items.title: Genome-Wide Association Study Meta-Analysis of Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

sections.objective: The pathophysiology of central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) remains incompletely understood, and there is ongoing debate regarding the origin of primary dysfunction. To elucidate the genetic architecture of CSC and map susceptibility loci to specific ocular cell types and molecular pathways.
sections.methods: This genetic association study was a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis aggregating data from 5 large biobank cohorts and included 2584 patients with CSC and 1 044 455 control participants of European ancestry. Cohort data were from July 1, 2010, to October 31, 2023; data analysis was performed from Febuary 2024 to January 2026. Post-GWAS functional mapping was performed using mendelian randomization, bayesian colocalization, and single-cell disease relevance scoring across human ocular tissue atlases. The relevance of the genetic findings was demonstrated by building a CSC genetic risk score and applying it to the UK Biobank (UKB).
sections.results: The meta-analysis identified 10 risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold (P < 5 × 10-8), including 3 novel loci (TGFB1, LINC00551, and LOC105375630) and 7 replicated loci (CFH, GATA5, PREX1, CD46, NOTCH4, PTPRB, and TNFRSF10A). Integrative post-GWAS analysis prioritized 10 genes, including TGFB1, TNFRSF10A, and CFH, as likely causal effectors. Single-cell enrichment mapping revealed that CSC genetic risk is concentrated in scleral tissue (P < .001) and vascular endothelial cells (P < .001). Mendelian randomization pointed to circulating TGFB1 and TNFRSF10A levels as associated with CSC risk. A CSC genetic risk score applied in UKB revealed a higher frequency of CSC-relevant abnormalities on macular optical coherence tomography in participants in the top 1% of polygenic risk (18/109 [16.5%] vs 8/134 [6.0%]; difference, 10.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.6-19.1; adjusted odds ratio, 4.05; 95% CI, 1.65-10.87; P = .002).
sections.conclusion: Convergent genetic evidence supports CSC as a primary disorder of the sclera and choroidal vasculature with retinal pigment epithelium changes likely representing a downstream consequence. Integrative post-GWAS analysis pointed to complement regulation (CFH, CD46), vascular integrity and endothelial cell signaling (PTPRB, TNFRSF10A, NOTCH4, PREX1), and scleral extracellular matrix biology (TGFB1) as important in CSC.
sections.other: Identification of risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold, prioritized putative causal genes, enrichment of genetic risk within specific ocular tissues and cell types, and performance of a GRS in the independent UKB dataset.

items.title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD).
sections.methods: Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD. Single-vessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in the left anterior descending coronary artery only. Multivessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in all 3 major coronary arteries. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events, comprising a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure.
sections.results: Multivessel assessment identified more patients with CMD than single-vessel assessment (46.7% vs 24.1%; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up period of 4.3 years, an increased number of vessels with CMD was associated with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events after adjustment for diabetes mellitus, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of myocardial infarction (adjusted HR: 1.963 per vessel; 95% CI: 1.513-2.548; P < 0.001). Multivessel assessment showed superior prognostic performance compared with single-vessel assessment when added to a clinical risk factor model (area under the curve: 0.751 vs 0.707; P = 0.034).
sections.conclusion: Multivessel assessment by angio-IMR improved the diagnostic yield of CMD and added incremental prognostic information compared with single-vessel assessment in patients with NOCAD.

items.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in older adults: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Multimorbidity, non-specific symptoms, and atypical disease manifestations are common in adults aged 65 years or older, complicating diagnostic and prognostic assessment. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides real-time bedside imaging that can support clinical decision making in this population; however, evidence on its use in older adults has not been systematically mapped. This scoping Review, endorsed by the European Geriatric Medicine Society, mapped POCUS utilisation across health-care settings, application domains, clinical indications, and outcomes. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles investigating the use of POCUS in older adults (defined as studies that exclusively enrolled older adults ≥65 years or reported a mixed-age study population with a mean age of 65 years or older) and published in English or another language represented within the review team (Italian, French, German, Spanish, Danish, or Turkish) with no restrictions on publication date. Of the 3897 records, 240 (6%) studies were included; 87 (36%) focused on older adult or geriatric-targeted populations and 153 (64%) on mixed-age populations with a mean age of 65 years or older. Evidence came predominantly from acute care, with few studies in geriatric settings. Thoracic POCUS was the most frequently investigated single-organ domain; multiorgan POCUS was also prominent. Diagnostic support and prognostic stratification predominated, whereas longitudinal monitoring and patient-centred outcomes were infrequent. Evidence on POCUS applications in older adults remains uneven, highlighting the need for further research in under-represented geriatric care settings and on patient-centred outcomes.

items.title: Development and validation of early warning scores predicting 24 h mortality addressing intercurrent medical interventions in Denmark: a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 2·08 million hospital encounters.

sections.objective: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is widely used to predict patient deterioration, but retrospective validations face intervention bias and emphasise discrimination performance over clinical utility. We aimed to compare the clinical net benefit of NEWS against simplified scoring rules and machine learning models, to determine whether simpler approaches suffice or if complex models offer meaningful advantages, and to evaluate performance heterogeneity across patient subgroups.
sections.methods: In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, we included data from 15 Danish hospitals (ten hospital networks) across the Capital and Zealand regions of Denmark, between Oct 16, 2018, and Oct 16, 2023. We included all adults (aged ≥18 years) with a hospital encounter with at least one NEWS assessment. Demographic and clinical data, NEWS data, and time of death were extracted from hospital and regional electronic health records. Patients were followed up until death or completion of the 24 h observation period after the initial NEWS score was recorded, whichever occurred first. The outcome was all-cause mortality within 24 h of the initial NEWS recording. We compared NEWS against both simpler and more complex approaches for predicting 24 h mortality: simplified NEWS (NEWS without blood pressure and temperature), Demographic Early Warning Score (DEWS; simplified NEWS with age and sex), and a model based on Extreme Gradient Boosting Early Warning Score (XGB-EWS) incorporating vital signs, demographics, laboratory markers, plus medical history embeddings extracted using sentence transformers. We used propensity score weighting to mitigate intervention bias and evaluated performance using net benefit, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and calibration.
sections.results: This study included data for 2 080 765 hospital encounters representing 825 200 unique patients over 5 years. The majority (50·9%) of the weighted population was aged 18-65 years, 50·4% were female, 49·6% were male, and 66·2% were admitted to internal and acute medicine clinical specialties. Decision curve analysis in the overall population showed maximum net benefit differences of 1·9 additional correct mortality identifications per 10 000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS, and 1·5 per 10 000 patients between NEWS and simplified NEWS. However, stratified analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: in the high-risk group (initial NEWS ≥7), XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 78·1 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, whereas simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum performance loss of 60·2 per 10 000 patients. Conversely, in the low-risk group (NEWS 0-4), differences were minimal: XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 0·9 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, while simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum loss of 0·1 per 10 000 patients.
sections.conclusion: Model complexity produced small average clinical utility gains, concentrated among patients initially classified as high risk by NEWS. These findings support prospective trials of risk-stratified monitoring based on the first NEWS assessment, testing simplified approaches for lower-risk patients while retaining full NEWS or electronic health record models for higher-risk patients.

items.title: Investigating the path to degrowth on the island of Ikaria, Greece: a cross-sectional household survey.

sections.objective: Achieving high wellbeing while remaining within planetary boundaries is central to post-growth and degrowth research. Although no country meets minimum social thresholds without exceeding biophysical limits, localised territories might provide exceptions. We aimed to assess whether the Greek island of Ikaria offers an empirical example of real-existing degrowth, where high levels of wellbeing are maintained alongside low household carbon footprints, and to identify the household and structural factors associated with carbon footprints and potential pathways for further reductions.
sections.methods: We conducted a cross-sectional primary household survey across Ikaria between Oct 8 and Dec 12, 2023, collecting data on household composition, dwelling characteristics, energy use, mobility, income, employment, and wellbeing. Households with members permanently residing in Ikaria, defined as residing on the island for more than 8 months per year, and those with at least one adult household member able to provide informed consent and respond to the questionnaire were eligible to participate in the survey. Surveys were in Greek and conducted in person across five villages and the main towns of Raches, Evdilos, and Agios Kirykos. We calculated household carbon footprints using household spending data. Carbon intensity factors (expressed in kg CO2 equivalent [CO2e] per euro) were applied to reported household expenditures across electricity, heating oil, transport, food, clothing, and goods, using emission factors from environmentally extended input-output models and household carbon footprint databases. To explore the determinants of carbon footprint, we examined sociodemographic and structural variables and compared low-emitting and high-emitting households using Welch's t tests and ordinary least squares regressions. Wellbeing was assessed based on decent living standards, benchmarks, objective wellbeing indicators, and self-reported life satisfaction. Finally, we developed demand-side and supply-side scenarios to examine potential carbon footprint reductions while maintaining or enhancing wellbeing.
sections.results: From the 159 initial responses, ten were excluded as incomplete and 149 household surveys were included for the analysis. The sample represented approximately 4% of Ikaria's estimated households and mirrored the island's population distribution. Ikaria's per-capita household carbon footprint was 2·35-2·94 tCO2e per year, depending on the correction factor applied from the existing literature; this carbon footprint is substantially less than the EU average and close to Paris Agreement lifestyle benchmarks. Assuming a mean annual household carbon footprint of 2·94 tCO2e per capita per year, analysis of emissions distribution showed the largest contributions were housing (1·382 tCO2e [47%]), consumption (0·929 tCO2e [32%]), and transport (0·629 tCO2e [21%]). The island performed particularly well with respect to social connections, attachment to place, physical activity, and life satisfaction. Ikaria met or exceeded nearly all decent living thresholds, with high life satisfaction (mean score of 7·1 of 10), strong social support, and widespread participation in community life. Carbon footprints varied little by income; instead, household size and dwelling characteristics were stronger predictors. Regression analysis confirmed that higher life satisfaction was not substantially associated with a higher carbon footprint. Moderate demand-side reductions combined with renewable electricity could further reduce the footprint from 2·94 to 1·60-1·70 tCO2e per capita per year. Real-life equivalents showed that households already attaining footprints below the target had wellbeing outcomes similar to those of households above the target.
sections.conclusion: Our analysis using the data from Ikaria shows that high wellbeing can coexist with low carbon footprints that vary little between households, supported by provisioning systems grounded in social cohesion, sufficiency, and localised economies. Targeted sufficiency measures and distributed renewable energy could place the island within its fair share of 1·5°C compatible emissions. Thus, our study provides quantitative evidence indicating real-existing degrowth within Europe and illustrates a viable pathway for other islands and peripheral regions.

items.title: Immunogenicity and safety of Sabin inactivated poliovirus vaccine in a sequential schedule with bivalent oral poliovirus vaccine in Nepal: a single-centre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial.

sections.objective: Sabin inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV) might be a cost-effective alternative to conventional Salk IPV; however, immunogenicity data for sequential bivalent oral poliovirus vaccine (bOPV)-Sabin IPV schedules used in routine immunisation are scarce. We aim to compare the immunogenicity and safety of Sabin IPV with Salk IPV in routine bOPV-IPV sequential schedules for infants.
sections.methods: This single-centre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial was conducted at the Siddhi Memorial Hospital (Bhaktapur, Nepal). Healthy infants aged 6-8 weeks, with bodyweight of at least 3·0 kg, and who resided in Bhaktapur without planned migration were eligible. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1), using permuted blocks (sizes two, four, and six), to receive a full dose of Sabin IPV (LG Chem, Seoul, South Korea) or Salk IPV (Bilthoven Biologicals, Bilthoven, Netherlands). Each 0·5 mL dose was given intramuscularly at ages 14 weeks and 9 months. Infants also received bOPV (Bio Farma, Bandung, Indonesia) at ages 6, 10, and 14 weeks as part of routine immunisation. Participants, parents, investigators, clinical and research staff, data analysts, and laboratory assessors were masked to IPV allocation; vaccinators were unmasked. The primary outcome was type 2 seroconversion (change from <8 of reciprocal neutralising antibodies to ≥8 after vaccination) at age 10 months (ie, 4 weeks after the second IPV dose, with a study visit window of 1 week), assessed in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population as the risk difference with a non-inferiority margin of -10 percentage points. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, ACTRN12622000929707 (completed).
sections.results: Between March 26, 2023, and Nov 7, 2024, 1235 infants were screened for eligibility and 775 were excluded. 460 infants were randomly assigned to receive Sabin IPV or Salk IPV (230 in each group), with one randomisation error. The median age of infants was 46 days (IQR 45-48). More male infants (251 [55%] of 459) than female infants (208 [45%]) were enrolled. Type 2 seroconversion after two IPV doses at age 10 months in the mITT population occurred in 210 (99% [95% CI 97 to 100]) of 212 infants in the Sabin IPV group compared with 214 (100% [97 to 100]) of 215 in Salk IPV group (unadjusted risk difference: -0·5% [-2·1 to 1·1]), with the lower bound of 95% CI above the non-inferiority margin. The most common adverse event was fever at age 14 weeks (95 [43%] infants in the Sabin IPV group vs 100 [45%] in the Salk IPV group). Of 42 serious adverse events (in 37 [8%] of 459 infants), none were causally related to IPV.
sections.conclusion: Two full doses of Sabin IPV coadministered with routine childhood vaccines was non-inferior and had a similar safety profile to conventional Salk IPV.

items.title: Activity and safety of first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial.

sections.objective: Pumitamig, an investigational bispecific antibody targeting programmed death ligand-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, has shown preliminary efficacy across several tumour types. We aimed to evaluate the safety and activity of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
sections.methods: In this single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial conducted at ten sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in China, patients aged 18-75 years with histologically documented, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and one or more measurable lesion (as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1) received first-line pumitamig (20 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. In phase 1b, six patients received pumitamig (20 mg/kg once every 2 weeks intravenously plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) and were monitored for treatment-emergent adverse events, before subsequent enrolment in phase 2. The primary endpoints were confirmed objective response rate and safety, assessed in the efficacy-evaluable population, defined as all patients who received one or more doses of study drug and had measurable disease at baseline and at least one efficacy assessment. This trial is registered with chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2200060400) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05918133), and is closed to recruitment.
sections.results: Between June 27, 2022, and March 15, 2023, 42 patients were enrolled, received one or more doses of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel (median duration of exposure 9·0 months, 95% CI 6·9-11·7) and had one or more tumour assessments. All patients were Chinese and female; median age was 53 years (IQR 41-60). At a median follow-up of 35·2 months (95% CI 33·0-36·1), the confirmed objective response rate was 73·8% (95% CI 58·0-86·1; 31 of 42 patients), including one complete response and 30 partial responses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were decreased neutrophil count (13 [31%] of 42 patients), decreased white blood cell count (11 [26%]), proteinuria (six [14%]), and febrile neutropenia (five [12%]). Nine (21%) patients reported 14 treatment-related serious adverse events (alanine aminotransferase increased n=2; febrile neutropenia n=2; pancreatitis n=2; and ascites, aspartate aminotransferase increased, abdominal distension, γ-glutamyltransferase increased, blood alkaline phosphatase increased, cataract, macular oedema, and retinal vein occlusion all n=1). Treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation of both nab-paclitaxel and pumitamig in four (10%) patients, discontinuation of nab-paclitaxel only in three (7%) patients, and discontinuation of pumitamig only in two (5%) patients. There were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: Treatment with first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel showed encouraging antitumour activity in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and a safety profile consistent with the mode of actions of both agents. These findings warrant further clinical evaluation in global phase 2 and 3 trials.
sections.other: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial. 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia. Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.
sections.results: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.
sections.conclusion: Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.other: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.

items.title: Interventions for adhesive capsulitis: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: To compare the benefits and harms of therapeutic interventions for adhesive capsulitis.
sections.methods: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
sections.results: A total of 189 randomised controlled trials involving 12 988 participants and 59 interventions were included. Most trials contributing to principal outcomes were at high risk of bias (71% for pain, 72% for function, and 71% for range of motion). At short term follow-up, moderate certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduced pain compared with usual care (mean difference -1.97 on a 0-10 scale, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.97 to -0.97). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve function (mean difference -11.42 on a 0-100 scale, 95% CI -16.68 to -6.15), although direct and indirect estimates were limited by important incoherence. For short term range of motion, moderate certainty evidence suggested that manipulation under anaesthesia combined with intra-articular steroid injections probably improved flexion (mean difference 33.29°, 95% CI 11.19° to 55.39°), as did manipulation under anaesthesia alone (26.16°, 8.19° to 44.13°). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve flexion (22.42°, 12.99° to 31.84°) and abduction (18.62°, 8.09° to 29.14°), but both comparisons were limited by important incoherence. At mid-term follow-up, evidence for possible improvements in function with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and flexion with passive mobilisation was of low certainty, while evidence for pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy was of very low certainty. Most other comparative estimates were supported by low or very low certainty evidence. Comparative safety remained highly uncertain because adverse events were incompletely and inconsistently reported; the absence of reported adverse events should not be interpreted as evidence of absence of harm.
sections.conclusion: Moderate certainty evidence suggests short term pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and improved short term flexion with manipulation under anaesthesia, with or without intra-articular steroid injections. Most other treatment effects remain uncertain because of low certainty and incoherence, and comparative safety and mid-term effects are poorly established. The available evidence is mainly short term and outcome specific. Longer term comparative effectiveness, overall benefits and harms, and applicability beyond predominantly primary adhesive capsulitis remain uncertain.
sections.other: Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 May 2025, with an update in November 2025. Randomised controlled trials enrolling adults with adhesive capsulitis, comparing active treatment with another intervention, placebo, or usual care. Pain, function, range of motion, and adverse events. PROSPERO CRD420251070468.

items.title: Retinoblastoma.
items.abstract: Retinoblastoma, the most common primary intraocular malignancy of childhood, represents a substantial global health equity concern, exemplifying profound disparities in global burden and outcome despite being a largely curable cancer. Retinoblastoma is thought to arise from cone photoreceptor precursor cells of the developing retina, mainly driven by biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumour suppressor gene. Fewer than 2% of cases have no detectable RB1 pathogenic variant; approximately half of these cases instead show high-level amplification of the MYCN oncogene. Diagnosis and monitoring currently rely on clinical examination and multimodal imaging. Emerging molecular diagnostic approaches such as aqueous humour liquid biopsy hold promise for minimally invasive tumour characterisation and real-time disease monitoring. Management has shifted towards eye-preserving strategies, with intra-arterial, intravitreal, and intracameral chemotherapy showing efficacy and safety. The global burden and mortality of retinoblastoma remains highest in regions with a low sociodemographic index, highlighting the need for continued interdisciplinary, equity-focused efforts to ensure timely diagnosis and accessible, high-quality care worldwide. This Seminar reviews the advances in retinoblastoma biology, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and global efforts to reduce inequities.

items.title: Preparing for responsive management versus renal dialysis in older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity in the UK (Prepare for Kidney Care): a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: The comparative effectiveness of conservative kidney management and dialysis in older people (aged ≥80 years regardless of frailty and comorbidity or aged 65-79 years if frailty or multimorbidity are present) living with kidney failure is unknown. We aimed to assess the relative effectiveness of preparing for responsive management-a protocolised version of conservative kidney management-and preparing for renal dialysis.
sections.methods: Prepare for Kidney Care was a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial conducted in 31 kidney centres in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min per 1·73 m2, confirmed by at least one additional reading in the 12 months preceding consent that was not due to acute kidney injury, and were either aged 80 years or older, or aged 65-79 years with a WHO performance status of at least 3 or a Davies comorbidity score of at least 2. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to prepare for responsive management-a patient-centred approach focused on slowing disease progression, active symptom management, and preserving quality of life without the use of dialysis or kidney transplantation-or to prepare for renal dialysis. Randomisation was stratified by centre and minimised by age; a centralised system ensured allocation concealment until randomisation had taken place. The primary outcome was the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), combining length and health-related quality of life from the patient-reported EQ-5D-5L scale, including all follow-up from randomisation to Aug 31, 2025. The primary outcome was analysed by intention to treat in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants, with missing EQ-5D-5L values for living participants imputed. Harms (hospital admissions and dialysis access complications) and adverse events (deaths and hospital admissions, by cause) were assessed in the full analysis set. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, 17133653 (completed).
sections.results: From July 1, 2017, to Aug 31, 2024, 6120 patients were screened across 31 kidney centres in the UK, 445 (7%) of whom were eligible and agreed to be randomly assigned. 228 (51%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for responsive management and 217 (49%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for renal dialysis. Median age was 82 years (IQR 80 to 86) and 137 (31%) of 445 participants were female. After a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years (SD 2·1), mean QALYs were 1·354 (95% CI 1·201 to 1·508) in the prepare for responsive management group and 1·472 (1·288 to 1·655) in the prepare for renal dialysis group (adjusted mean difference -0·147 [95% CI -0·350 to 0·056] p=0·16). Specific harms outcomes were not prespecified, but hospital admission rates were similar in the two groups and dialysis access complications were significantly lower in the prepare for responsive management group (adjusted incident rate ratio 0·41 [95% CI 0·19 to 0·88]), based on 74 events in 36 participants across both groups. There were 667 serious adverse events in the prepare for responsive management group (157 [69%] of 228 participants died, with 510 hospital admissions) and 578 in the prepare for renal dialysis group (136 [63%] of 217 participants died, with 442 hospital admissions). None of these serious adverse events met the criteria for expedited reporting.
sections.conclusion: Among older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity, we found no evidence that either preparing for responsive management or preparing for renal dialysis was superior in terms of QALYs over a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years. This trial provides novel comparative information for clinical decision making.

items.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element.
items.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.

items.title: Alternate eye patching improves long-term alignment stability after surgery for intermittent exotropia: a randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Postoperative exodrift remains a major challenge following surgical correction of intermittent exotropia (IXT), and evidence supporting adjunctive strategies to improve long-term alignment is limited. This study evaluated the effect of alternate eye patching on 12-month postoperative alignment stability after successful surgical correction in divergence excess IXT.
sections.results: At 12 months, alignment stability was significantly higher in Group A compared with Group B (83.3% vs 60.0%, p = 0.045). Significant exodrift occurred less frequently in Group A (16.7% vs 40.0%, p = 0.045). Mean postoperative deviation was lower in Group A at all follow-up visits (p < 0.05). No patients in Group A required reoperation compared with 10% in Group B, although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.112).
sections.conclusion: Alternate eye patching may improve postoperative alignment stability and reduce postoperative exodrift for divergence excess intermittent exotropia. Early postoperative modulation of binocular visual balance may contribute to improved long-term alignment outcomes.
sections.other: This randomised clinical trial was conducted at an institutional tertiary care centre and included 60 children (3-12 years) undergoing bilateral lateral rectus recession who were randomised only after confirmation of early postoperative alignment ( ≤ 10 prism dioptres [PD]), creating a post-success randomised design to evaluate the effect of alternate eye patching on alignment maintenance. Participants were assigned to alternate eye patching (Group A) or standard postoperative care (Group B). Patching was prescribed for 1 h daily per eye for 3 months. Patients were followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was alignment stability ( ≤ 10 PD). Secondary outcomes included exodrift ( > 10 PD), mean deviation, and reoperation rate. Pan African Clinical Trial Registry (PACTR202505751499770), registered on May 14, 2025. https://pactr.samrc.ac.za/.

items.title: Short-term Risk of Inflammatory Eye Reactions Following Bisphosphonate Use: A nationwide case-case-time-control study.

sections.objective: To evaluate short-term associations between bisphosphonate exposure and uveitis, scleritis, and cystoid macular edema (CME).
sections.methods: Nationwide case-case-time-control (CCTC) study. Patients with incident uveitis, scleritis, or CME identified from Taiwan's national health claims data (2011-2021), with matched future cases serving as controls to adjust for temporal exposure trends. Bisphosphonate exposure during the 30-day hazard window immediately preceding each event was compared with exposure during an earlier 30-day reference window, separated by a 90-day washout period. Each case was matched to a future case to account for temporal trends in bisphosphonate use. Analyses were stratified by administration route and individual agent. Sensitivity analyses varied window lengths, washout periods, and lag structures. Denosumab and teriparatide served as negative-control exposures.
sections.results: We identified 269,545 incident uveitis cases, 132,585 scleritis cases, and 115,914 CME cases; over 96% were matched to a future case and included in CCTC analyses. After accounting for exposure trends, any bisphosphonate use was associated with an increased short-term risk of uveitis (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.00-1.56), driven primarily by anterior uveitis (OR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.10-1.86). In analyses stratified by administration route and individual agent, intravenous bisphosphonates (OR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.22-2.61), particularly zoledronic acid (OR, 2.82; 95% CI, 1.70-4.67), were associated with increased uveitis risk. Oral bisphosphonates were not associated with uveitis (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.74-1.33). No clear associations were observed for scleritis or CME. Findings were consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses, and associations for negative-control exposures were null.
sections.conclusion: Short-term associations between bisphosphonate use and ocular inflammatory events varied by administration route and outcome. Increased uveitis risk was concentrated among intravenous formulations, particularly zoledronic acid, whereas no clear associations were found for scleritis or CME. These findings may inform monitoring for ocular symptoms among patients receiving intravenous bisphosphonates.
sections.other: Incident uveitis, scleritis, and CME, with associations quantified using CCTC odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

items.title: Best practices in communication of environmental health risks due to localised pollution events: a mixed-methods systematic review.
items.abstract: Localised environmental pollution can generate acute concern, particularly when the health effects are uncertain. Media coverage can amplify fear and stress, necessitating transparent risk communication. This mixed-methods systematic Review (PROSPERO registration number CRD42024568007) focuses on strategies for communicating health risks associated with local pollution. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Scopus, and PsycArticles on April 19, 2024, (from inception) and May 22, 2026 (Jan 1, 2000 onwards), supplemented by Google Scholar and OAIster (July 9, 2026), Global Index Medicus (July 10, 2026), and backward and forward citation tracking (July 16 and 17, 2026) all from Jan 1, 2000 onwards. Of 29 216 studies identified, 105 were eligible (61 quantitative, 30 qualitative, and 14 mixed-methods); all papers were written in English and included exposed populations. Review articles, animal studies, and in-vitro or in-silico studies were excluded. Quantitative outcomes comprised changes in knowledge, behaviour, stress, or fear, whereas qualitative studies analysed communication preferences or experiences. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Qualitative data were analysed through thematic synthesis with CERQual assessment. Quantitative findings were narratively synthesised because of heterogeneity. Results were integrated using a convergent mixed-methods approach. Communities valued clear, plain-language explanations of pollutants, health effects, and exposure-reduction actions, supported by simple visuals and multiple communication channels. Interpersonal and community-embedded communication, especially from trusted local figures, enhanced understanding, reduced distress, and strengthened trust. Timely, consistent updates and transparent discussion of uncertainty were well received when delivered by trusted sources and combined with practical guidance but were less effective or potentially counterproductive when institutional trust was weak. Community collaboration improved the clarity, relevance, and acceptance of messages. Effective communication regarding local pollution depended on trust-building through open, empathic, and community-centred engagement. Clear, accessible messages from multiple media channels, supported by interpersonal dialogue, helped communities to understand risks without generating disproportionate worry.

items.title: National, regional, and global trends in adolescent physical activity from 2010 to 2025: a pooled analysis of 389 surveys with 3·2 million participants from 140 countries.

sections.objective: Physical activity during adolescence improves current and future physical and mental health and contributes to preventing non-communicable diseases. We aimed to update national, regional, and global estimates of adolescent physical activity, examine the distribution of activity across days of the week, assess trends from 2010 to 2025, and progress towards the 2030 global target.
sections.methods: We pooled data from population-based surveys of self-reported number of active days (≥60 min of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity) in the past week among adolescents aged 11-17 years collected in or after 2008. Using Bayesian ordinal models, we estimated the distribution of active days per week and mean active days per week, by sex, age, country, and year. Separate models were fitted for boys and girls. We computed the posterior probability that boys' statistics were higher than girls', and that mean active days per week were higher in 2025 than in 2010. We generated projections to 2030 to assess progress towards the global target of a 15% relative reduction in the percentage of adolescents reporting fewer than 7 active days per week.
sections.results: In 2025, 24·9% (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 21·8-28·5) of adolescents globally reported 0 active days per week, and 13·9% (12·6-15·6) reported being active on 7 days per week. The global mean was 2·7 (95% UI 2·6-2·9) active days per week. Globally, there was no change detected between 2010 and 2025. No country is on track to meet the 2030 global target. Girls' mean active days per week were lower than boys' globally (2·4 [2·2-2·7] vs 3·0 [2·8-3·2], posterior probability >0·99) and in all regions (posterior probability was 0·63 in Oceania and ≥0·89 in all other regions). In central and eastern Europe and central Asia, east Asia and the Pacific, and high-income western (comprising western Europe, northern America, Australia, and New Zealand) regions, mean active days per week (3·8-4·1 vs 2·2-2·7 in other regions) and the change in mean active days per week from 2010 to 2025 (small increases of 0·1-0·3 active days vs no change detected) were more favourable than in other regions. However, in these three regions, mean active days per week declined with age (1·2-1·4 and 0·5-0·8 fewer days at age 17 years than at age 11 years for girls and boys, respectively).
sections.conclusion: Globally, adolescent physical activity remains low, especially among girls. Increasing physical activity will require effectively implemented, context-specific actions that prioritise the least active adolescents together with whole-population approaches that address socioeconomic, environmental, and cultural barriers.

items.title: Global, regional, and national burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

sections.objective: Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages.
sections.methods: We used estimates from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to assess the burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Mortality was modelled with the Cause of Death Ensemble model and prevalence with the Disease Modelling Meta-Regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Years of life lost (YLLs) were calculated as the number of deaths for each age-sex-location-year multiplied by the standard life expectancy at each age. Severity-specific prevalence values were multiplied by their respective disability weights (with asymptomatic cases assigned zero disability) to estimate years lived with disability (YLDs). Disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were computed by summing YLDs and YLLs. We report prevalence, mortality, YLDs, YLLs, and DALYs as counts and age-standardised and age-specific rates per 100 000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), stratified by sex, GBD region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI).
sections.results: In 1990 and 2023, the global counts for prevalence attributable to gallbladder and biliary diseases were 157·4 million (95% UI 134·0 to 183·3) and 264·4 million (226·0 to 309·9), for deaths were 65 800 (95% UI 53 000 to 78 800) and 146 700 (121 800 to 171 300), and for DALYs were 4·8 million (95% UI 3·5 to 6·2) and 8·2 million (6·3 to 10·6), representing substantial increases. However, age-standardised rates declined over the same period, from 3573·2 (95% UI 3045·5 to 4159·1) per 100 000 population to 2990·1 (2561·5 to 3492·5) per 100 000 population for prevalence, from 1·95 (1·58 to 2·31) per 100 000 population to 1·67 (1·39 to 1·95) per 100 000 population for mortality, and from 111·5 (84·1 to 143·3) per 100 000 population to 92·3 (70·9 to 119·6) per 100 000 population for DALYs. Over the past three decades, females had higher age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates than males, while sex differences in mortality rates were smaller. In 2023, age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates were lowest in south Asia and highest in central and western Europe, central Asia, and many regions in Latin America. By contrast, several regions in sub-Saharan Africa had relatively low prevalence and DALY rates but comparatively high mortality rates. National patterns broadly mirrored these regional profiles. In 2023, prevalence and DALY counts peaked in middle to early-older adulthood (ages 55-69 years), but age-specific rates continued to rise into the oldest age groups, with DALYs dominated by YLDs in midlife and early-older adulthood and by YLLs at older ages (≥80 years). The number of deaths peaked in the ninth decade of life, but age-specific rates also peaked in the oldest age groups. Across GBD regions, the association between SDI and age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates generally followed a reversed U-shaped pattern, with the lowest rates at low SDI, peak rates at intermediate SDI, and declining rates at the highest SDI levels. The association between SDI and mortality rate was less clear.
sections.conclusion: The global burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases is rising in absolute terms despite declining age-standardised rates, underscoring the importance of population growth and ageing. Health systems, particularly in settings with rapidly ageing populations and intermediate SDI levels, will need to expand diagnostic, elective, and emergency surgical capacity while investing in prevention of obesity and metabolic risk factors. Marked regional and national heterogeneity, as well as differences in risk factors, might reflect variance in health-system capacity and access to care, including timely diagnosis, availability of surgical services, and perioperative care. The predominance of non-fatal disability in midlife and rising mortality in older age groups indicates that integrated strategies spanning risk-factor control, early diagnosis, elective management, and robust acute care for older adults are essential to reduce both YLDs and YLLs.

items.authors: GBD 2023 Gallbladder and Biliary Disease Collaborators

items.title: Cancer in the Commonwealth: a Lancet Oncology Commission.
items.abstract: Cancer is now one of the defining health and development challenges of our time. The 56 nations of the Commonwealth, home to 2·7 billion people, mirror this global burden. Recorded cancer cases across member states rose by 35% in 2008-18 and the number of deaths reached almost 1·7 million in 2018. The Lancet Oncology Commission on cancer in the Commonwealth was convened to ask a deceptively simple question: how can 56 diverse nations act collectively to close the widening gap between the burden of cancer and the capacity of each country to respond? 80 researchers, clinicians, policy makers, and civil society members, organised into five working groups and ten research streams, spent 2 years assembling the evidence base for this report. Using a validated microsimulation model, we estimate that 5-year net survival across eleven common cancers in the Commonwealth stood at just 30·7% in 2020, ranging from 4·1% in low-income countries (LICs) to 59·0% in high-income countries (HICs), driven overwhelmingly by late-stage presentation, which affects 62% of patients in LICs compared with 43% in HICs. This difference in survival is compounded by chronic underinvestment. Infrastructure gaps are equally stark: only 12% of countries meet international benchmarks for CT imaging, 22% for hospital density, and 40% for radiotherapy. Governance is underdeveloped too: barely one-third of Commonwealth countries have a national cancer control plan meeting basic quality criteria. Research investment also mirrors these inequities: between 2016 and 2023, Commonwealth countries collectively invested only US$165 per cancer-related disability adjusted life year. Yet the case for investment is unambiguous. Our modelling shows that a comprehensive scaleup of treatment, imaging, and quality of care could raise 5-year net survival across the Commonwealth from 30·7% to 52·9%, averting an estimated 5·8 million deaths and adding 113 million life-years between 2025 and 2035, at an incremental cost of $36·7 billion, delivering a return of between four and twenty dollars on every dollar invested. Crucially, this investment need not depend chiefly on external aid, which is contracting sharply at present.
