Our modelling for 38 low-income and middle-income Commonwealth countries suggests that up to $701 billion in additional domestic fiscal space could be mobilised between 2025 and 2030, through budget reprioritisation, macroeconomic growth, targeted taxation, and prudent borrowing. On this evidence, the Commission proposes six priority actions. These commitments are ambitious, set against an unusually turbulent geopolitical backdrop of declining official development assistance, fiscal retrenchment, and contested multilateralism. Yet it is precisely this backdrop that gives the Commonwealth its distinctive advantage: a voluntary association spanning every income level and continent, bound by common legal and regulatory traditions, capable of collective action that neither purely bilateral aid nor multilateral institutions under strain can easily replicate.

items.title: Survival in patients with renal cell carcinoma and brain metastases: an update of the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment.

sections.objective: Brain metastases are a common and serious consequence for patients with renal cell carcinoma. This study aimed to determine if survival has changed since the introduction of current therapies, identify prognostic factors, update the prognostic index (the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment [GPA]) in the context of contemporary multi-modal therapies, compare outcomes with legacy cohorts, and determine whether overall survival correlates with intracranial progression-free survival.
sections.methods: An international consortium of 21 academic institutions contributed uniformly-curated retrospective data from 1049 patients with newly-diagnosed renal cell carcinoma with brain metastases (RCC-BM) treated between Jan 1, 2016, and Dec 31, 2022. Patients treated between 1985-2007 (n=286) and 2006-15 (n=711) were considered legacy cohorts and compared to the current cohort. Significant prognostic factors for survival were identified through combined multivariable analyses and used to update the Renal GPA. Intracranial progression-free survival was defined as the interval from date of initial RCC-BM diagnosis to date of first salvage treatment.
sections.results: Of the 1049 patients, 773 (73·7%) patients were male and 276 (26·3%) were female; the majority (851 [81·1%]) were White, and the median age was 63·9 years (IQR 56·2-70·3). The median overall survival was 20·0 months (95% CI 18·0-23·4), with a median follow-up of 53·4 months (95% CI 50·2-56·8). Overall survival for the legacy cohorts were 9·6 months (95% CI 8-11) and 12·0 months (5-11), respectively. In combined multivariable analyses, significant prognostic factors for inferior survival were lower Karnofsky Performance Status, lower baseline serum albumin, higher number of brain metastases, and presence of extracranial metastases. These factors were incorporated into the updated Renal GPA. Median survival was 4·8 months (95% CI 3·0-8·1) for patients with GPA 0-1·0, 12·4 months (10·6-17·2) for GPA 1·5-2·0, 33·6 months (27·5-40·0) for GPA 2·5-3·0, and 51·2 months (34·1-undefined) for GPA 3·5-4·0. Median intracranial progression-free survival was 9·6 months (95% CI 8·4-10·6). The Spearman's rank correlation between intracranial progression-free survival and overall survival was moderately strong (0·74 [95% CI 0·70-0·78]; p<0·0001).
sections.conclusion: Survival has improved compared to the legacy cohorts but varies widely by GPA. The updated Renal GPA can be used to estimate survival, intracranial progression-free survival, individualise treatment, design and stratify clinical trials, and refine clinical trial eligibility.

items.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.

sections.objective: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
sections.methods: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).
sections.results: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.
sections.conclusion: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.

items.title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.

sections.objective: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.
sections.methods: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.
sections.results: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).
sections.conclusion: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

items.title: Bare-Metal vs Covered Balloon-Expandable Stents for Transplant Renal Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study.

sections.objective: To compare short- and long-term outcomes of bare-metal (BMS) vs covered (CS) balloon-expandable stents in transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS).
sections.methods: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure. Long-term outcomes included Doppler ultrasound parameters - peak systolic velocity (PSV), acceleration time (AT) and resistive index (RI) - and restenosis/occlusion rates requiring or not intervention. Graft survival at the latest follow-up was recorded.
sections.results: A total of 40 patients (mean age 58 ± 13 years, 68% male) were treated with BMS (n = 31) or CS (n = 9). Clinical improvement was observed in 71% of BMS and 83% of CS patients (P = 1.00). Median sCr decreased by 26% and 33% in BMS and CS patients, respectively (P = .30). At a median follow-up of 29 months, there were no statistically significant differences between groups in median PSV reduction (47% BMS vs 47% CS; P = .44), AT improvement (36% BMS vs 25% CS; P = .38) or RI increase (15% BMS vs 33% CS; P = .12). In the BMS group, 2 cases of in-stent restenosis occurred (6.5%). In the CS group, 1 stent occlusion occurred (11%), resulting in graft loss. At final follow-up, overall graft survival was 85%.
sections.conclusion: In this pilot study, BMS and CS showed no significant differences in TRAS outcomes. Further studies are warranted to better guide stent selection.Clinical ImpactIn transplant renal artery stenosis, balloon-expandable covered stents achieved clinical, biochemical and Doppler outcomes comparable to bare-metal stents, despite being used in more complex, atherosclerotic and longer lesions. This first direct comparison suggests that covered stents may be a reasonable option when heavy calcification, a friable wall or mural thrombus raise concern for embolisation or rupture, while bare-metal stents remain appropriate for most lesions. The single late covered-stent occlusion with graft loss highlights the need for careful platform selection and antiplatelet management. These pilot data should inform adequately powered multicentre registries rather than directly change practice.

items.title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.

sections.objective: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity.
sections.results: A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%. Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; P = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; P = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients.
sections.conclusion: In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

items.title: Treatment Strategies and Outcomes of Aneurysms Affecting Small and Medium Arteries in Neurofibromatosis Type 1. A systematic review.

sections.objective: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms.
sections.methods: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169825). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting management and outcomes of NF1-associated arterial aneurysms. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Primary outcomes included treatment strategies, technical success, complications, and mortality. Isolated aortic aneurysms or aortic dissections were not considered the primary target of the review. However, studies reporting concomitant aortic disease and aneurysmal involvement of non-aortic arteries were retained when relevant data on NF1-associated vasculopathy and its management were available.
sections.results: Eighty-six studies including 99 patients (mean age 42 years; 44.4% male) were analyzed. Aneurysms were most frequently located in cervico-vertebral (45.2%) and visceral arteries (24.0%). Multifocal disease was present in 12.1% of patients. Overall, 65.7% of patients presented with aneurysm rupture or acute hemorrhage. This high proportion should be interpreted cautiously because of the substantial publication bias inherent to a literature predominantly based on case reports and small case series. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently used approach (68.7%), followed by open surgery (19.2%), hybrid repair (5.0%), and conservative management (9.1%). Endovascular treatment showed a reported technical success rate exceeding 90%. Recanalization (6.3%), delayed thrombosis (4.2%), and new aneurysm formation (5.3%) were observed. Open repair was mainly used for anatomically complex or endovascularly inaccessible lesions. Overall mortality was 8.1%, primarily in patients presenting with rupture.
sections.conclusion: NF1-associated aneurysms require an individualized, anatomy-driven management strategy. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently reported treatment and appears to be a viable option in anatomically suitable patients, while open and hybrid techniques remain important for selected complex lesions. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from case reports and small case series and does not permit comparative assessment of treatment strategies. Lifelong imaging surveillance is mandatory due to the risk of recurrence and new aneurysm formation.

items.title: Sepsis-related hospitalisation risk in preterm-born and term-born children and adolescents: a nationwide registry study.

sections.objective: The burden of severe infections in children remains inadequately characterised. Preterm birth is a risk factor for neonatal sepsis, but whether this risk persists beyond the neonatal period is unclear. We examined the risk of sepsis-related hospitalisation during childhood and adolescence in term-born and preterm-born children.
sections.methods: Norwegian nationwide birth registry data (Jan 1, 1992-Dec 31, 2021) were linked with hospital discharge data (Jan 1, 2008-Dec 31, 2021). Using a standardised definition, sepsis-related hospitalisations were classified as explicit (sepsis diagnosis code) or implicit (infection plus organ dysfunction diagnosis codes). We estimated rate ratios (RRs) using adjusted negative binomial regression and sibling-controlled odds ratios (ORs) using conditional logistic regression by completed weeks of gestation (23-27, 28-31, 32-33, 34-36, 37-38, and 39-41 weeks), stratified by age (3-11 months, 1-5 years, and 6-15 years).
sections.results: Following 1,672,009 births, 13,158 sepsis episodes were available in the data. Hospitalisation rates for sepsis-related admissions were highest at ages 3-11 months (84.4 per 1000 person-years [95% CI 62.2-106.7] for 23-27 weeks gestation and 3.2 per 1000 person-years [95% CI 3.0-3.4] for 39-41 weeks gestation). Compared with term-born children, rates of sepsis-related hospitalisations increased by lower gestational age groups in both population and sibling analyses. Comparing extremely preterm versus term-born children, RRs were 26.5 (95% CI 20.2-34.7) at ages 3-11 months, 14.8 (11.2-19.6) at ages 1-5 years, and 6.7 (3.9-11.4) at ages 6-15 years. Sibling ORs were 24.9 (10.8-57.4), 29.7 (11.3-77.8), and 3.1 (1.2-8.0), respectively.
sections.conclusion: Lower gestational age was robustly associated with an increased risk of sepsis-related hospitalisation throughout childhood and adolescence, supporting that low gestational age at birth should be recognised as a persistent risk factor for severe infections beyond the neonatal period.

items.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson's disease therapy.
items.abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation has shown promising neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in progressive neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease. However, its invasive nature introduces procedural and device-related risks. Here we introduce a magnetoelectric particulate system for oral delivery and non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation through the gut. The system comprises a magneto-responsive nickel ferrite core and a piezoelectric barium titanate shell, conjugated with capsaicin to specifically target TRPV1 receptors, ensuring effective adherence to the stomach lining after oral administration. Upon magnetic field stimulation, the particles generate electrical pulses that activate vagal afferent fibres, engaging the nucleus tractus solitarius in the brainstem via the gut-brain axis. This activation enhances norepinephrine production in the locus coeruleus and dopamine synthesis in the substantia nigra. Vagal efferent activation triggers the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, mitigating both neuroinflammation and systemic inflammation. This non-invasive approach demonstrates potential for alleviating motor symptoms and non-motor anxiety in Parkinson's disease, offering valuable insights into its mechanisms and clinical applications.

items.title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.

sections.objective: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality.
sections.methods: In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods.
sections.results: Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality.
sections.conclusion: Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency.

items.title: Acquired cytomegalovirus in children: pathogen, bystander, or immune trainer?
items.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is one of the most common infections worldwide, with acquisition occurring predominantly in early childhood (younger than 5 years). Although congenital CMV is a recognised cause of neurodevelopmental impairment, the consequences of postnatally acquired CMV in children remain poorly defined and are often assumed to be benign. However, accumulating evidence suggests that acquired CMV infection is biologically active even when clinically silent, with the capacity to shape immune ontogeny, influence immune responses to other pathogens and vaccines, and alter health trajectories across the life course. In this Review, we examine the epidemiology, transmission pathways, immune responses, and clinical consequences of acquired CMV infection in childhood. We synthesise evidence to evaluate whether acquired CMV acts as a driver of pathology, a neutral bystander, or a beneficial immune trainer. The effects of CMV are highly context-dependent, determined by the timing of acquisition, host immune maturity, maternal health, co-infections, and broader social and environmental factors. Evidence of harm is strongest in infants with heightened biological or contextual risk, such as infants born preterm and those living with or exposed to HIV, whereas effects in children who are immunocompetent are heterogeneous and often clinically silent. Acquired CMV should be understood as a context-dependent immune modifier rather than a uniformly benign or pathogenic infection. This reframing of acquired CMV has important implications for policy and research. Universal intervention is unlikely to be appropriate; instead, targeted CMV prevention and treatment strategies for populations at high risk of CMV infection and severe disease integrated into maternal and child health programmes could offer the greatest benefit. Defining high-risk populations and critical windows for intervention should be prioritised to translate emerging evidence into improvements in childhood morbidity and equity.

items.title: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes.
items.abstract: The Altiplano Cundiboyacense in the eastern Colombian Andes preserves one of the Americas' most continuous archaeological sequences, recording cultural and demographic change. We generated genome-wide data from 212 individuals spanning over 7,000 years, including early-middle and middle Holocene hunter-gatherers, initial late Holocene groups with mixed economies and the earliest isotopic evidence of maize consumption, and increasingly sedentary Herrera and Muisca populations. Individuals predating the Herrera Period form a lineage that persisted for five millennia, structured by drift in small groups without external gene flow. Two individuals dating ∼2,800 years before present (BP) retain autochthonous ancestry while showing isotopic signatures consistent with maize consumption, decoupling subsistence change from population replacement. The emergence of Herrera culture ∼2,200 BP coincided with a sharp genetic break by ∼2,000 BP, which reflects migration by people descended from admixture ∼4,000 BP between groups with Chibchan- and Amazonian-Andean-related ancestries. Herrera and Muisca Period individuals show north-south genetic substructure paralleling archaeological differentiation.

items.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.

sections.objective: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.
sections.methods: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.
sections.results: A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

items.title: Ocular Magnification Correction Influences Glaucoma-Related Microvascular Measurements in OCT Angiography.

sections.objective: To evaluate the impact of axial length (AL) handling strategies on optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-derived vessel density and its interpretation in glaucoma.
sections.methods: This cross-sectional study included 1091 participants (1823 eyes). Vessel density was quantified using fixed region of interest (ROI) and AL-rescaled ROI approaches. Comparisons of glaucoma versus normal eyes were evaluated using generalized estimating equation (GEE) models adjusted for age, sex, systemic hypertension, OCTA signal strength index, and AL. Associations between vessel density and visual field mean deviation (VF MD) were evaluated using multivariable GEE models.
sections.results: Glaucoma eyes had longer AL than normal eyes (P < 0.001). Under the fixed-ROI approach, deep vessel density was positively associated with AL, whereas superficial vessel density showed no significant association. After rescaling, both were inversely associated with AL (P < 0.001). Although rescaling increased apparent glaucoma-normal differences, estimates were similar after AL adjustment (superficial: β = -0.35 vs. -0.36 mm⁻1; deep: β = -1.03 vs. -1.09 mm⁻1). In the age- and sex-matched cohort (544 participants; 890 eyes), differences remained similar between approaches (superficial: β = -0.293 vs. -0.310 mm⁻1; deep: β = -0.963 vs. -0.992 mm⁻1). Both vessel density measures were associated with VF MD after AL adjustment. AL rescaling improved deep vessel density model fit and yielded slightly higher discrimination in sensitivity analyses allowing nonlinear AL effects (superficial: area under the curve [AUC] = 0.884 vs. 0.868; deep: AUC = 0.895 vs. 0.869).
sections.conclusion: Ocular magnification correction influenced OCTA measurements, but its incremental impact on glaucoma-related associations after AL adjustment was small. The clinical relevance remains uncertain.

items.title: Tetrahydrobiopterin Supplementation Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells Against NMDA-Induced Excitotoxicity Through nNOS-Coupled Nitric Oxide Signaling.

sections.objective: Excitotoxic injury triggered by excessive N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor activation represents an important mechanism underlying retinal neurodegeneration in glaucoma. Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), an essential cofactor for nitric oxide synthase (NOS), exhibits neuroprotective potential in multiple neurodegenerative diseases, but its role in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) under excitotoxic injury remains unclear. This study assessed the neuroprotective effects of BH4 against excitotoxic retinal injury and explored its underlying mechanisms.
sections.methods: Glutamate-treated R28 cells and intravitreal NMDA-injected rat retinas were used as in vitro and in vivo excitotoxic injury models, respectively. BH4 levels were measured after injury. Cell viability, oxidative stress, apoptosis, RGC survival, retinal morphology, visual function, and NOS activity were assessed following BH4 supplementation.
sections.results: BH4 levels were significantly reduced in glutamate-injured R28 cells and NMDA-damaged retinas. BH4 supplementation improved cell survival, reduced oxidative stress, and attenuated apoptosis in injured R28 cells. In vivo, BH4 preserved RGC survival, alleviated retinal damage, and improved visual function after NMDA injury. Mechanistically, BH4 restored neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) coupling and activity, increased nitric oxide levels, re-established nitroso-redox homeostasis, and suppressed apoptotic signaling.
sections.conclusion: BH4 deficiency contributes to glutamate-induced retinal neurodegeneration by promoting nNOS uncoupling and nitroso-redox imbalance. Restoring BH4 levels protects against excitotoxic RGC damage, suggesting the BH4-nNOS axis as a potential therapeutic target for retinal neurodegeneration.

items.title: Natural History of an Unusual Chorioretinal Phenotype Associated With the RHO p.(Met216Lys) Variant.

sections.objective: While variants in RHO are a leading cause of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (RP), the c.647T>A p.(Met216Lys) variant gives rise to a phenotype that can mimic choroideremia. We describe its long-term natural history.
sections.methods: Patients were included from four centers (in France, the United Kingdom, and the United States). Clinical features analyzed included pedigrees, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), visual fields, color vision, electroretinography, and multimodal imaging (color fundus photography, short-wavelength and near-infrared fundus autofluorescence [SW- and NIR-AF], and spectral domain optical coherence tomography [SD-OCT]).
sections.results: Seventeen patients (11 women; median age at first examination, 45 years [range, 13-68 years]) from eight unrelated families were included. Follow-up was available for 13 individuals (median, 159 months [range, 24-286 months]). Impaired night vision was the predominant presenting symptom (71%), with BCVA relatively preserved at baseline. Visual fields showed pericentral round scotomas, enlarging and coalescing over time, with relative sparing of the far periphery. On SW-AF, younger patients showed a diffuse granular pattern, whereas older patients showed well-demarcated patches of autofluorescence loss. Serial imaging in seven patients confirmed that these patches enlarged and coalesced within individuals over time. Color fundus photography showed preserved optic disc color and normal retinal vessel caliber. SD-OCT demonstrated outer retinal tubulations, a thinned choroid, and progressive ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss (median rate of EZ width loss, 176 µm per year).
sections.conclusion: The RHO c.647T>A p.(Met216Lys) variant is associated with a slowly progressive, unusual chorioretinal dystrophy phenotype that can closely mimic choroideremia. Our findings suggest pathogenetic mechanisms that differ from typical RHO-associated RP.

items.title: Detection of Abnormalities in the RPE in Long-Chain 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency Chorioretinopathy Using Optical Coherence Tomography-Derived Optical Attenuation Coefficients.

sections.objective: To detect abnormalities in the RPE in long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (LCHADD) chorioretinopathy, a novel method using optical attenuation coefficients (OACs) was used to enhance the contrast between regions with high and low attenuation.
sections.methods: LCHADD patients were scanned over the central macula using two commercial optical coherence tomography (OCT) devices. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging was performed during the same visit to detect RPE abnormalities based on lipofuscin distribution. OAC was derived from OCT data. En face OAC of the retina (internal limiting membrane to Bruch's membrane [BM]), en face OCT of the RPE (16 µm above the BM to the BM), and corresponding FAF images were compared to evaluate the ability of the OAC to detect RPE abnormalities. Pairwise comparisons were performed across all LCHADD stages, along with correlations with traditional clinical metrics including LCHADD severity, best-corrected visual acuity, and plasma acylcarnitines.
sections.results: Forty-three eyes from 22 LCHADD patients were evaluated and categorized into 6 stages. OAC images of the retina revealed RPE defects consistent with FAF, with clearer and more detailed visualization of RPE disruption. Compared with OCT images, OAC images facilitated visualization of pathological changes and provided a better visual comparison between the preserved and degenerated RPE at advanced stages. The mean retinal OAC decreased significantly (P < 0.001) with disease progression and differed significantly across disease stages (all P ≤ 0.002), showing strong correlations with traditional clinical metrics.
sections.conclusion: OCT-based OAC is a promising tool for both the quantitative and qualitative assessment of RPE abnormalities in LCHADD chorioretinopathy.

items.title: Discovering a Novel AAV2-Based Capsid for RPE Transduction Via Intravitreal Injection for Leber Congenital Amaurosis Type 2 Gene Therapy.

sections.objective: Several retinal degenerations initiate because of gene defects in the outermost retinal layer, the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Subretinal injection achieves optimal RPE transduction but has limitations, including iatrogenic damage. Here, we develop and evaluate the efficacy of a novel adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid with intravitreal delivery, in an effort to overcome limitations of subretinal delivery for treatment of retinal degenerations that require precise targeting of the outer retina.
sections.methods: We conducted a high-throughput screening of 1.28 × 109 AAV2 capsids, each with a different 7-mer peptide insertion to alter its binding properties, to be delivered with intravitreal (IVT) injection, a less invasive surgical procedure. A novel AAV variant, variant 3 (AAV2.Var3) was found to transduce RPE cells with CAG-GFP and Best1-GFP in mouse eyes. For comparison, a leading, clinical-stage vector that is also AAV2-based, 7m8, effectively transduces the outer retina but has limited success targeting RPE through IVT delivery. To test the therapeutic efficacy of variant 3, we packaged therapeutic gene, hRPE65, and injected it intravitreally in rd12 mice, a disease model for Leber congenital amaurosis type 2.
sections.results: AAV2.Var3-hRPE65 treated mice cohorts showed an increase in RPE65 protein expression and function as well as visual function in response to light flashes. Translatability of AAV2.Var3 for intravitreal gene delivery was validated by AAV2.Var3-Best1-GFP vector induced expression of GFP in peripheral RPE cells in non-human primate macaque.
sections.conclusion: Variant 3 is capable of RPE transduction with IVT injection, serving as a vehicle for less invasive IVT gene delivery to the RPE. Therapeutic gene delivery leads to functional results with efficiency limitations.

items.title: Volumetric Quantification of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs) in Coronary Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) have been reported as correlates of several systemic conditions. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, number, area, and volume of RIPLs and to evaluate their association with coronary artery disease (CAD) using a contemporary imaged coronary angiography (CA) cohort.
sections.methods: CA patients were imaged using an SS-OCTA device during the same visit. Structural volumes comprising 500 B-scans were pixel-wise annotated by three graders. RIPLs were quantified by presence, count, area and volume for the first time. CAD severity was assessed using the Gensini score (GS). Associations between RIPL metrics and CAD were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Multivariable and age and sex adjusted models were calculated. Multiple testing corrections were applied to primary analyses.
sections.results: RIPLs were detected in 38.0% of eyes. In models with the Gensini score (GS) as outcome, RIPL metrics showed weak and inconsistent trends and were not statistically significant, especially after adjustment. The GS showed no significant associations with RIPL presence (β = 0.132, P = 0.102), area (β = 0.173, P = 0.093), count (β = 0.023, P = 0.165), or volume (β = 0.240, P = 0.085) either. Cardiovascular risk factors were not independently associated with RIPL metrics. Those negative findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses using the SYNTAX II and SCORE2.
sections.conclusion: In this contemporary coronary angiography cohort with high-density OCT imaging, RIPL burden was not significantly associated with CAD and no robust or proportional association with CAD severity was found. In this work, no other disease specific associations could be established.

items.title: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists' National Ophthalmology Database: report 15, severe vision loss following cataract surgery.

sections.objective: To investigate rates of severe vision loss post-cataract surgery.
sections.results: Severe vision loss was recorded in 3723 (0.21%) eyes, including 3 eyes (2 patients) from 2 718 immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery (ISBCS) eyes. The highest observed SVL rate was 10.68% for eyes recorded as left aphakic after surgery and the second highest observed SVL rate (3.32%) was when posterior capsular rupture occurred. The SVL rate was higher than the overall rate for eyes with previous intravitreal injections (0.76%), eyes with optic nerve or central nervous system problems (0.74%), age-related macular degeneration (0.52%), previous vitrectomy surgery (0.49%), diabetic retinopathy (0.45%), glaucoma (0.42%) or corneal pathology (0.33%). Of 1,642,386 (93.8%) eyes that were not preoperatively legally blind, 2731 (0.2%) were postoperatively legally blind. Of these, 2294 (84.0%) eyes experienced severe vision loss.
sections.conclusion: Severe vision loss from any cause following cataract surgery occurs infrequently. However, it has a higher prevalence in eyes left aphakic, when PCR occurs and for certain ocular comorbidities.
sections.other: Post-cataract severe vision loss (SVL) was defined as a loss of ≥0.60 LogMAR between preoperative presenting visual acuity and postoperative visual acuity. The term 'legally blind' was used for eyes with a corrected visual acuity worse than 1.30 LogMAR. Between 2010 and 2024, there were 1,750,553 eligible operations performed on 1,217,267 patients by 3766 surgeons from 132 centres supplying data to the Royal College of Ophthalmologists National Ophthalmology Database Cataract Audit.

items.title: Making better use of patients' time: feasibility of performing self-administered vision assessments in waiting rooms.

sections.objective: Patients often spend significant time in clinic waiting rooms. This study assessed the feasibility of using this "wasted" time to perform self-administered vision assessments directly within the waiting area.
sections.methods: Glaucoma patients attending routine appointments were asked to complete either a pen-and-paper (SpotChecks) or digital (PopCSF) contrast sensitivity (CS) test. Ambient illuminance, background noise, and crowd levels were recorded to assess potential environmental confounds. Test durations and patient feedback were recorded. Visual-Functioning Index-7 (VF-7) and Pelli-Robson CS (reference) test results were collected for comparison.
sections.results: Of 173 patients approached, 155 (89.6%) agreed to participate, and 151(97.4%) participants completed testing before their appointment (77/78 pen-and-paper; 74/74 digital). Environmental factors had no significant impact (all P > 0.05). Median completion times were 3.0 {2.6-4.5} minutes (pen-and-paper) and 2.5 {2.0-3.5} minutes (digital). Age did not impact the pen-and-paper test duration (P = 0.944) but weakly correlated with the digital test duration (rdigital = 0.27, P = 0.020). Functional CS scores correlated with Pelli-Robson reference measurements (rpen-and-paper = 0.81; rdigital = 0.62), age (rpen-and-paper = -0.58; rdigital = -0.37), logMAR visual acuity (rpen-and-paper = -0.42; rdigital = -0.44), and visual field mean deviation scores (rpen-and-paper = -0.54; rdigital = -0.63). Both tests were highly acceptable to patients ( > 80% on all questions). Visit durations were longer for participants (109 vs 88 min, P = 0.007), but this was attributed to consenting and related research activities rather than the tests themselves.
sections.conclusion: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that it is feasible for patients to self-administer portable vision tests in clinic waiting rooms. Using CS as a representative example, this approach may enable additional data collection, potentially improving patient management, clinic flow, and/or patient satisfaction.

items.title: Development and External Evaluation of a Clinical Score for High Pretreatment Interferon-γ Release Assay Responses in Psoriasis: A Multicenter Study in China.

sections.objective: The NPF/IPC statement exempts routine tuberculosis (TB) testing for IL-17/IL-23 inhibitors in low-burden settings, but elimination may be unsafe in high-burden regions. To develop and evaluate a clinical score estimating the probability of a high pretreatment interferon-γ release assay (IGRA) response in psoriasis patients before biologic therapy in China.
sections.methods: Adult patients with psoriasis scheduled to initiate biologic therapy who underwent pretreatment screening were retrospectively included from four Chinese hospitals. Logistic regression was used to develop and evaluate the score.
sections.results: The psoriasis TB risk score (PTRS) comprised six items: age>43.0 years (1), BMI>24.8 kg/m2 (2), married status (1), smoking (2), alcohol consumption (3), and acitretin use (-2). The AUC was 0.799 (95% CI, 0.758-0.840) in the development cohort, 0.697 (0.625-0.768) in validation cohort 1, and 0.621 (0.462-0.780) in the exploratory Shenzhen cohort. Positivity rates in the development, validation, and external validation cohorts were 2.4%/8.8%/33.2%, 3.7%/11.8%/20.8%, and 2.9%/8.8%/13.7% for the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively.
sections.conclusion: The PTRS stratified the probability of a high pretreatment IGRA response in Chinese cohorts; local validation is required before the score is used to modify testing practice.
sections.other: Retrospective design without longitudinal TB outcomes; performance declined in the geographically distinct cohort.

items.title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.

sections.objective: To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort.
sections.methods: External validation in a prospective population-based cohort. Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts. We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV).
sections.results: Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility.
sections.conclusion: The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.
sections.other: Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC).

items.title: Trends in the burden of diseases and their associations with multidimensional development among children and adolescents in China from 2000 to 2019: a retrospective analysis of a nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional survey.

sections.objective: Rapid social progress has transformed the health profile of Chinese children and adolescents, with declining diseases associated with poverty and rising diseases associated with wealth. This study aims to describe national trends in disease transitions and examine their associations with multidimensional provincial development.
sections.methods: In this retrospective study, we analysed data from the 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019 waves of the nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional Chinese National Surveys on Students' Constitution and Health in Han Chinese children and adolescents aged 7-18 years from 30 provinces in mainland China. The survey used a multistage, stratified, cluster-sampling design with balanced distributions by age, sex, and residence (urban vs rural). Collected data were prevalences of diseases associated with wealth and development (overweight and obesity, dental caries, and visual impairment) and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with wealth) in addition to diseases associated with poverty (undernutrition, anaemia, and Ascaris infestation), and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with poverty). We integrated 13 provincial indicators reflecting economic, social, environmental, infrastructure, and innovation development to construct a Multidimensional Equality Development Index (MEDI) using an entropy method. To examine national trends in disease transitions and their associations with multidimensional development we used mixed-effects logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. Population-attributable fractions were estimated to describe how development domains related to disease patterns.
sections.results: The study included 1 085 072 participants across five survey waves. Between 2000 and 2019, nationally, the prevalence of diseases associated with wealth increased and that of diseases associated with poverty declined substantially. In 2019, prevalence of visual impairment was highest (67·8%), followed by overweight and obesity (24·3%), dental caries (21·9%), multimorbidity associated with wealth (20·1%), anaemia (10·1%), undernutrition (4·7%), Ascaris infestation (0·8%), and multimorbidity associated with poverty (0·5%). The overall median MEDI score increased from 0·11 (IQR 0·09-0·16) in 2000 to 0·20 (0·15-0·28) in 2019. When data were pooled over 20 years, restricted cubic-spline analyses showed a non-linear association between MEDI score and odds of the disease outcome; higher MEDI scores were generally associated with lower odds of diseases associated with poverty, and higher odds of diseases associated with wealth (excluding visual impairment).
sections.conclusion: Multidimensional development was associated with simultaneous reductions in prevalence of diseases associated with poverty and increases in prevalence of diseases associated with wealth. Disparities in most diseases associated with wealth between higher and lower MEDI areas have largely narrowed, suggesting a potential dual burden in lower MEDI areas and the need for targeted strategies. These findings highlight the need to enhance cross-sector investments to promote balanced, sustainable improvements in child and adolescent health.

items.title: Estimated global treatment costs for 31 cancer types by stage, year, and follow-up period: a systematic review and modelling study.

sections.objective: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446).
sections.results: Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers.
sections.conclusion: These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings.

items.title: Effect of ethnicity on response to treatment escalation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR): a longitudinal cohort study.

sections.objective: Ethnic disparities in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) outcomes are well documented, but data on treatment response across ethnic groups remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate the effect of ethnicity on clinical outcomes following treatment escalation in a diverse UK cohort.
sections.methods: In this longitudinal cohort study, we analysed data from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR), including patients recruited from 64 UK secondary and tertiary rheumatology and nephrology centres. Eligible patients were aged 16 years and older, with active moderate-to-severe SLE, defined as having at least one BILAG A score, at least two BILAG B scores, or a SLEDAI-2K score of at least 6, who had initiated rituximab or belimumab within the past 12 months, or standard immunosuppressive therapy within the past 1 month. Ethnicity was categorised as White, South Asian, Black, East Asian, or mixed or other ethnicities. The primary outcome was major clinical response (MCR) at 6 months and 12 months, measured using mixed-effects logistic regression. Individuals with lived experience of SLE were involved in the study design.
sections.results: Between July 1, 2010, and Nov 10, 2021, 1688 patients were recruited to the BILAG-BR. Of these, 1266 were excluded because they did not meet the study eligibility criteria, and 422 patients were included in the study. 383 (91%) patients were female, 39 (9%) were male, and the median age was 40·5 years (IQR 31·3-50·8). 245 (58%) of 422 patients were White, 77 (18%) were South Asian, 70 (17%) were Black, 19 (5%) were East Asian, and 11 (3%) were of mixed or other ethnicities. At baseline, Black patients had higher baseline disease activity, greater organ damage, and more comorbidities. At 12 months, 99 (23%) of 422 patients had met MCR criteria, including eight (42%) of 19 East Asian patients, 23 (30%) of 77 South Asian patients, 60 (24%) of 245 White patients, seven (10%) of 70 Black patients, and one (9%) of 11 patients with mixed or other ethnicities. In the adjusted five-group model, patients of Black ethnicity had lower odds (OR 0·13 [95% CI 0·02-0·88]) of meeting MCR criteria compared with White patients.
sections.conclusion: MCR criteria were met by fewer than a quarter of patients after treatment escalation. Patients of Black ethnicity had higher baseline disease burden and lower observed response than White patients. These results support the need for more personalised, equitable approaches to SLE management and reinforce the importance of ensuring diversity in clinical research.

items.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.

sections.objective: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.
sections.methods: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.
sections.results: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.
sections.conclusion: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

items.title: Reframing the manosphere: a public health response to a commercial ecosystem.
items.abstract: The manosphere, a diffuse commercial ecosystem and loose collection of online communities united by shared beliefs about masculinity, misogyny, and male victimisation, is an under-recognised determinant of health harms. This network has been implicated in considerable health harms: widespread mental health impacts, especially in young people; violence against women, girls, and gender minorities; and delegitimising help-seeking in boys and men. In this Viewpoint, we argue that the manosphere is best understood and addressed as a public health problem.

items.title: Charting a course to men's health and wellbeing: applying a lens of power and politics to improve men's health outcomes.
items.abstract: Despite long-standing evidence of poor health and life expectancy outcomes among men, particularly among men who are socially or structurally marginalised, men's health has generally received little and uneven attention in health policy and practice. Its gendered and intersectional aspects have been especially overlooked. This third paper in the Lancet Men's Health Series examines why men's health has received so little policy attention and proposes strategies to raise men's health on national and global agendas. We applied a gender lens to the 3-i theory-based framework and analysed how ideas, interests, and institutions shape the prioritisation of men's health within national and global policy agendas. We review the modest development of men's health policies and assess how power and politics, including the roles of a range of stakeholders from global and national health spaces, commercial actors, and civil society organisations, have shaped the construction of the problem as well as policy attention and framing, resource allocation, and interventions. The scarcity of attention paid to men's health on global and national agendas reflects how power operates through ideas and institutions which contribute to the conflation of gender with women, institutional inertia, and contested constructions of individual versus structural drivers of ill health. We highlight how this has created a space in which commercial actors, including the manosphere, can shape narratives and influence men's health in ways that align with commercial or ideological interests. We conclude by proposing politically informed strategies that recognise how power, institutional arrangements, and competing interests shape men's health policy within prevailing gender and structural orders. We identify entry points for advancing men's health equity and wellbeing that draw on empirical evidence and technical guidance, are grounded in political realities, and are consistent with a commitment to gender justice for all people.

items.title: A global men's health epidemiology within an intersectional framework.
items.abstract: Males have lower life expectancies and greater disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) than females, and particularly poor outcomes are seen among males in marginalised contexts. In this paper, we provide an epidemiological overview and highlight the intersectional nature of men's health. We analyse mortality and DALYs data from the 1990-2023 Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Studies to illustrate our intersectional framework and draw attention to how health varies in men and to show key themes. Conditions that contribute most to the poor health of males include non-communicable diseases (eg, cardiovascular diseases and cancers), substance use, suicide, injuries (eg, road traffic incidents and interpersonal violence), and respiratory infections (eg, tuberculosis and COVID-19). Although cardiovascular disease and cancer make the largest contributions to men's higher mortality rates, determinants of health such as violence and war, migration, economic stagnation, and labour market changes due to automation and new technologies will disproportionally affect their health in the future. Injuries, violence, and other external morbidity causes often occur at a young age and in unequal distributions across the sexes, making a large contribution to DALYs. Although biology plays a role, the pattern of many diseases contributing to health differences reflects the intersection of health behaviours, shaped by patriarchy, ideas of masculinity, and structural drivers (including commercial determinants of health); many of these are preventable. Although improvements in some health behaviours are seen, exceptions occur in marginalising social conditions (eg, incarcerated men, men experiencing homelessness, men with mental illnesses, men with substance use disorders, men with low income, men who have sex with men, and those who are gender non-conforming). Multiple data sources detail men's shorter life expectancies and the drivers compared with women, but going beyond sex disaggregation remains challenging and is an urgent priority for research and health monitoring.

items.title: Men's health: an intersectional and multilevel framework for understanding syndemic patterns of health.
items.abstract: Men occupy a privileged position within gender power relations: the male body has been the default reference point for biomedical research and therapeutic development (with the historical exclusion of women from medical trials), and men dominate health services leadership and exercise well documented medical misogyny. Yet despite their privileged position, many aspects of men's health outcomes are neglected and undertheorised because they are not examined through an intersectional gender lens. Although consideration of gender and masculinity is important for understanding men's health, research thus far has focused predominantly on men's harmful health behaviours, overemphasising individual determinants of health, and a deficit-based approach. Little attention has been paid to the influence of structural determinants of men's health risks and vulnerabilities, or the gender-specific health outcomes of worsening social and economic inequalities. In this first paper of a Lancet Series on men's health, we present a conceptual framework for understanding men's health from an intersectional perspective, highlighting how structural, social, and commercial determinants of health, intersectionality, and syndemic theory can be combined to analyse men's health at different socioecological levels. We illustrate the framework using four selected case studies that show how the health outcomes of marginalised men are influenced by complex interactions. We provide a working definition of men's health that reflects existing literature and builds on the conceptual framework and case studies. Promotion of gender justice and health equity requires moving beyond one-dimensional approaches that construct men as problematic individuals, and towards better understanding and action on the broader set of power systems and structural determinants underpinning men's health.

items.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.

sections.objective: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis.
sections.methods: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement.
sections.results: Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH.
sections.conclusion: Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design.

items.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS.
sections.methods: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group.
sections.conclusion: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended.

items.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

items.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
items.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF.
