Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.
items.authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)

items.title: Intralesional cemiplimab for patients with early-stage cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: Results from a dose-escalation study with expansion cohorts.

sections.objective: Non-surgical treatment of patients with early-stage (1-2 cm diameter) cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) remains an unmet need. This study investigates low-dose intralesional cemiplimab for these patients. The primary objective was safety of low-dose intralesional cemiplimab. Efficacy was a secondary objective.
sections.methods: This was an open-label, phase 1 pilot study with dose escalation and expansion cohorts (NCT03889912). One lesion was injected per patient. Cemiplimab was initially administered at 5, 15, and 44 mg weekly, for 12 weeks. Subsequently, Expansion Cohorts A and B received 5 mg intralesional cemiplimab weekly or every 2 weeks, respectively, for 6 weeks. Visual response assessments were performed at Weeks 7 and 13, and surgery at Week 13.
sections.results: Across 41 patients, cemiplimab showed an acceptable safety profile. In Expansion Cohorts A and B, treatment-emergent adverse events were all grade ≤2. Week 13 visual and pathologic complete response rates were both 58.3% in Cohort A and 41.7% and 66.7%, respectively, in Cohort B.
sections.conclusion: Low-dose intralesional cemiplimab demonstrated efficacy against early-stage CSCC, with an acceptable safety profile. These data support further study of 5 mg intralesional cemiplimab weekly.
sections.other: The small number of participants limits generalizability. Intralesional cemiplimab administration may have been variable.

items.title: Contralateral Major Amputation Following Diabetes- and Peripheral Artery Disease-Related Limb Loss: A Systematic Review and Pooled Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.
sections.methods: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or prior ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.
sections.results: Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was 6 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 3-9), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P=.622), geographic region (P=.662), study era (P=.893), or DM prevalence (P=.127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI versus non-CLTI PAD or DM versus post-ipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P<.001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11-64%).
sections.conclusion: NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

items.title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.

sections.objective: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.
sections.methods: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.
sections.results: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).
sections.conclusion: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus and mortality risk in preterm infants: a Bayesian meta-analysis across gestational age groups.

sections.objective: Recent randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses have questioned the safety of early pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants, suggesting possible increases in the risk of mortality and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Whether these risks vary by gestational age remains uncertain. We aimed to compare the effects of pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks versus those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater.
sections.methods: For this Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for randomised controlled trials enrolling infants with a gestational age less than 32 weeks and echocardiographically confirmed patent ductus arteriosus who were randomly assigned either to pharmacological treatment or to placebo or expectant management. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality before 36 weeks' postmenstrual age and secondary outcomes were moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. RRs greater than 1 indicated harm. We calculated the posterior probability of harm (Prharm=P[logRR>0]) and Bayes factors comparing harm versus benefit (BFharm/benefit). This study is registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024622527).
sections.results: Ten randomised controlled trials including 2365 infants (1133 female and 1232 male) were analysed; 1045 had a gestational age less than 26 weeks. Pharmacological treatment was associated with increased mortality in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks (RR 1·12 [95% CrI 0·90-1·41], Prharm=0·85, BFharm/benefit=5·48), in those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater (1·22 [0·90-1·77], Prharm=0·89, BFharm/benefit=7·82), and in the overall population (1·23 [95% CrI 1·00-1·54], Prharm=0·97, BFharm/benefit=36·04). For bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite outcome of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, analyses explicitly incorporating the possibility of no effect indicated that the data were more consistent with the no-effect model than with either the benefit or the harm model.
sections.conclusion: The currently available randomised evidence is consistent with an increased mortality risk associated with pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment, without evidence of a compensatory reduction in bronchopulmonary dysplasia. This association was evident both below and above the 26-week gestational age threshold. These findings question the safety of routine pharmacological treatment and underscore the need for more selective, evidence-based approaches for patent ductus arteriosus management.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.
sections.methods: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).
sections.results: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group).
sections.conclusion: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
sections.other: For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process.
sections.methods: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]).
sections.results: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups.
sections.conclusion: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes.
sections.other: For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.
